short_description.id: Jaō Gongen adalah dewa ular yang dipuja di seluruh Jepang dengan nama termasuk Jaōhime.
short_description.en: Jaō Gongen is a snake deity worshiped across Japan under names including Jaōhime.

long_description.id: Jaō Gongen adalah dewa ular yang dipuja di seluruh Jepang dengan nama termasuk Jaōhime. Pemujaan kolam serta air terjun menghubungkan dewa ini dengan kekayaan dan keberhasilan peternakan ulat sutra.
long_description.en: Jaō Gongen is a snake deity worshiped across Japan under names including Jaōhime. Pond and waterfall worship connects the deity with wealth and successful sericulture.

long_description.id: Legenda Miyazaki membuat pelarian menjanjikan pemujaan kepada ular raksasa yang melindunginya. Versi Aira membuat Sumiyoshi membunuh ular kolam penerima kurban.
long_description.en: A Miyazaki legend makes a fugitive promise worship to the giant snake that shelters him. An Aira version instead has Sumiyoshi kill the sacrificial pond snake.

long_description.id: Pada zaman Edo, gelar Jaō Gongen juga diberikan kepada ular yang diangkat menjadi dewa; di Nagai, Hanaizumi, kuilnya konon bermula dari pemujaan roh ular setelah keluarga pembunuh ular besar terus ditimpa kemalangan. Laporan tahun 1921 dari Tokushima mencatat dewa ular bernama 蛇王大明神 di semak belukar yang populer karena dipercaya mengabulkan permohonan, bermula dari seorang penebang bambu yang melihat ekor ular besar. Polisi kemudian melarang ziarah ke sana dan pemujaannya dihapuskan.
long_description.en: In the Edo period, the title Jaō Gongen was also given to snakes raised to divine rank; at Nagai, Hanaizumi, the shrine is said to have begun with the worship of a snake's spirit after the family that killed a great serpent suffered continued misfortune. A 1921 report from Tokushima records a serpent deity named 蛇王大明神 in a thicket, popular for granting wishes, which began when a bamboo cutter saw a great serpent's tail. The police later banned visits and the cult was abolished.

statement.en: Jaō Gongen is a snake deity worshiped across Japan under names including Jaōhime.

claims.quote: 東北地方から九州地方にかけて、日本各地の寺社や祠・石碑などに数多くその名が確認されている。池や滝の主などとして祀られることが多い。 ヘビを信仰するという点で、弁財天などと同様に富をもたらす財神として、蛇王が祀られることも多い。山形県尾花沢市鶴巻田の旧家には、家の板の間を蛇王様が通ったときに残った鱗のあとを切り抜いて、蛇王大権現のご神体として、招財や養蚕の成功を願っていたという。

statement.id: Pemujaan kolam serta air terjun menghubungkan dewa ini dengan kekayaan dan keberhasilan peternakan ulat sutra.
statement.en: Pond and waterfall worship connects the deity with wealth and successful sericulture.

claims.quote: 宮崎県には、平家滅亡後に那珂郡に落ち延びてきた野辺相模守という武士が、追手から隠れるために入った大蛇に蛇王権現としてまつることを誓い、かくまってもらったという伝説がある。大蛇の穴に隠れて無事に追手から逃れることのできた相模守は、農民となったあとも約束どおり、大蛇を蛇王権現として祠にまつっていたという。

statement.id: Legenda Miyazaki membuat pelarian menjanjikan pemujaan kepada ular raksasa yang melindunginya.
statement.en: A Miyazaki legend makes a fugitive promise worship to the giant snake that shelters him.

claims.quote: 鹿児島県の姶良では、「御池の主」として蛇王権現が祀られており、池の大蛇に生贄がささげられていたが、その大蛇を住吉大神が退治したという伝説を伴っている。

statement.id: Versi Aira membuat Sumiyoshi membunuh ular kolam penerima kurban.
statement.en: An Aira version instead has Sumiyoshi kill the sacrificial pond snake.

claims.quote: 江戸時代には、各地でヘビに対して神位が与えられる際にも称号として蛇王権現が用いられている。岩手県花泉町永井の蛇王権現社は、大蛇を殺した後に家の者に不幸がつづいたため、蛇の霊を祀ったのがはじまりだとされる。

statement.id: Pada zaman Edo, gelar Jaō Gongen dipakai di berbagai tempat ketika ular diberi kedudukan ilahi; kuil Jaō Gongen di Nagai, Hanaizumi (岩手県花泉町永井), konon bermula dari pemujaan roh ular setelah keluarga yang membunuh seekor ular besar terus ditimpa kemalangan.
statement.en: In the Edo period, the title Jaō Gongen was used in various places when snakes were granted divine rank; the Jaō Gongen shrine at Nagai, Hanaizumi (岩手県花泉町永井), is said to have begun with the worship of a snake's spirit after a family that killed a great serpent suffered continued misfortune.

claims.quote: 藪林の中に蛇王大明神があって願い事がかなうといい非常にはやった。祠はなく、幟を立てて賽銭箱を置いただけのもの。

statement.id: Sebuah laporan tahun 1921 dari Kokufu, Tokushima, mencatat dewa 蛇王大明神 di semak belukar yang sangat populer karena dipercaya mengabulkan permohonan; tidak ada kuil kecil, hanya panji dan kotak persembahan.
statement.en: A 1921 report from Kokufu, Tokushima, records a deity 蛇王大明神 in a thicket that became very popular for granting wishes; there was no shrine building, only banners and an offering box.

claims.quote: 竹伐の男が大蛇の尾を見て逃げ帰り村民に伝えたのが始まりという。警察署が参詣を禁じ、蛇王様も廃されてしまった。

statement.id: Pemujaan itu bermula dari seorang penebang bambu yang melihat ekor ular besar lalu lari dan memberi tahu penduduk desa; kantor polisi kemudian melarang ziarah, dan Hebiō-sama (蛇王様) pun dihapuskan.
statement.en: The cult began when a bamboo cutter saw the tail of a great serpent, fled and told the villagers; the police later banned visits, and Hebiō-sama (蛇王様) was abolished.

short_description.id: Krivapeta adalah perempuan liar berkaki terbalik dalam tradisi rakyat Valli del Natisone yang tinggal di gua dekat sungai.
short_description.en: The Krivapeta is a wild woman with reversed feet in the folk tradition of the Valli del Natisone, living in caves near streams.

long_description.id: Krivapeta adalah tokoh dalam tradisi rakyat Valli del Natisone. Ia bukan penyihir, melainkan perempuan yang hidup terasing di gua dekat sungai, dengan kaki terbalik, tumit di depan dan jari di belakang; namanya berasal dari kata Slovenia kriv, "bengkok", dan peta, "tumit". Para Krivapeta berambut hijau panjang dan berpakaian putih.
long_description.en: The Krivapeta is a figure of the folk tradition of the Valli del Natisone. She is not a witch but a woman living apart in caves near streams, with reversed feet, heels in front and toes behind; her name comes from Slovene kriv, "crooked", and peta, "heel". The Krivapete have long green hair and dress in white.

long_description.id: Mereka bisa kejam atau baik, misalnya memberi tahu petani waktu terbaik untuk menabur, tetapi sebagai imbalan dapat meminta anak kecil. Cerita menakutkan ini dipakai untuk menjauhkan anak-anak dari tempat berbahaya.
long_description.en: They can be cruel or kind, telling farmers the best time to sow, but may demand small children in return. These frightening tales served to keep children away from dangerous places.

long_description.id: Kajian folklor Slovenia menyebut krivopete sebagai perempuan liar berkaki terbalik yang dikenal di ujung barat laut wilayah etnis Slovenia, yaitu di Trenta, Breginj, Livško, dan Lembah Natisone di Slavia Veneta, Italia. Ceritanya biasanya terikat pada tempat nyata yang dapat dilacak lewat nama-nama tempat, dan tempat tinggal mereka umumnya medan yang seram atau sulit dijangkau: gua, ceruk batu, jurang terjal, dan sungai kecil.
long_description.en: A Slovene folklore study describes the krivopete as wild women with reversed feet known in the far north-western corner of the Slovenian ethnic area, in places such as Trenta, Breginj and Livško, as well as in the Natisone valleys of the Italian Slavia Veneta. Their tales are usually tied to real places that can be traced through place names, and their dwellings tend to be forbidding or inaccessible terrain: caves, rock shelters, steep ravines and streams.

short_description.id: Lobisomem adalah manusia serigala dalam cerita rakyat Brasil; anak lelaki ketujuh dapat menjadi lobisomem dan berubah pada malam bulan purnama.
short_description.en: The lobisomem is the werewolf of the folklore of Brazil; a seventh son may become one and transform on full-moon nights.

long_description.id: Lobisomem adalah makhluk dalam cerita rakyat Amerika Selatan yang di Brasil biasanya dianggap manusia serigala. Dalam beberapa versi ia berupa bola api atau babi besar. Dalam wujud manusia ia tampak biasa kecuali telinga agak runcing dan kulit pucat kekuningan. Namanya berasal dari kata Portugis lobo, "serigala", dan homem, "manusia".
long_description.en: The lobisomem is a creature of South American folklore, in Brazil usually thought of as a werewolf. In some versions it is a ball of fire or a huge pig. In human form it looks normal except for slightly pointed ears and pale yellowish skin. Its name comes from Portuguese lobo, "wolf", and homem, "man".

long_description.id: Anak lelaki ketujuh dapat menjadi lobisomem kecuali seorang kakaknya menjadi ayah baptisnya; anak lelaki pertama setelah tujuh anak perempuan berubah pertama kali pada usia tiga belas tahun. Ia berubah pada malam bulan purnama, menurut sebagian orang hanya pada hari Jumat, dan menyerang pejalan serta hewan di jalan.
long_description.en: A seventh son can become a lobisomem unless an elder brother becomes his godfather; the first son after seven daughters first transforms at thirteen. It transforms on full-moon nights, some say only on Fridays, and attacks travellers and animals on the road.

long_description.id: Di sebagian Amazon dipakai sebutan Cumacanga, yang mungkin versi perempuan lobisomem.
long_description.en: In parts of the Amazon the term Cumacanga is used, possibly for a female lobisomem.

long_description.id: Di Portugal, makhluk ini dicatat sebagai lobishomem dalam sebuah kumpulan lama takhayul rakyat Portugis, yang menyebut takhayul ini dikenal di seluruh Eropa. Mengutip Herculano, lobis-homens adalah orang yang bernasib harus menanggalkan pakaian pada malam hari di tengah jalan. Di Kepulauan Azores, anak bungsu dari tujuh anak lelaki berturut-turut berubah setiap malam menjadi babi, keledai, atau hewan lain, dan orang yang menemuinya dapat melukainya sampai berdarah. Di S. Christovam de Mafamude, ia berkeliaran antara pukul sebelas dan tengah malam, dan cahaya membuatnya marah.
long_description.en: In Portugal the creature is recorded as the lobishomem in an old collection of Portuguese popular superstitions, which says the superstition is common to all of Europe. Quoting Herculano, the lobis-homens are those fated to undress at night in the middle of a road. In the Azores the youngest of seven sons in a row turns each night into a pig, a donkey or another animal, and whoever meets it may wound it and draw blood. In S. Christovam de Mafamude it roams between eleven and midnight, and light enrages it.

short_description.id: Oki atau Okeus adalah makhluk spiritual berpengaruh dalam agama tradisional bangsa Powhatan di kawasan Virginia Tidewater [okeus-c01].
short_description.en: Oki or Okeus is a spiritual entity in the traditional religion of the Powhatan people of Virginia Tidewater [okeus-c01].

long_description.id: Oki, yang dalam catatan kolonial ditulis Okeus atau Okee, adalah makhluk spiritual yang kuat dalam agama tradisional bangsa Powhatan di kawasan Virginia Tidewater. Ia dikaitkan dengan kekuatan alam, tempat-tempat keramat, dan daya yang menghidupkan dunia.
long_description.en: Oki, written Okeus or Okee in colonial records, is a mighty spirit-being of the Powhatan people's traditional religion in the Virginia Tidewater. He was linked to the forces of nature, to holy places, and to the power that gives the world life.

long_description.id: Persembahan kepada oki lazim, terutama sebelum menyeberangi sungai, memasuki hutan, atau memanen. Oki dapat melindungi atau menghukum, bergantung pada terjaga tidaknya keselarasan dengan dunia alam dan dunia roh.
long_description.en: Offerings to oki were common, above all before crossing rivers, entering forests or harvesting. Oki could protect or punish, depending on whether harmony with the natural and spiritual world was kept.

long_description.id: Catatan John Smith pada awal masa Jamestown menyebut Okee sebagai "Iblis", dewa utama yang dilayani lebih karena takut daripada cinta. Arcanya di kuil diukir, dicat, dihiasi rantai tembaga dan manik-manik, lalu ditutupi kulit. Orang yang melewati kuil utama di Uttamussack melemparkan tembaga, manik-manik putih, atau pocones ke sungai agar Okee tidak tersinggung, dan bila upacara tertentu dilalaikan, Okee dipercaya akan menahan rusa, kalkun, jagung, dan ikan.
long_description.en: John Smith's account from the early Jamestown years calls Okee "the Devil", the chief god served more from fear than love. His temple image was carved, painted, hung with copper chains and beads and covered with a skin. People passing the principal temple at Uttamussack cast copper, white beads or pocones into the river so that Okee would not be offended, and if a certain ceremony were neglected, Okee was believed to withhold deer, turkeys, corn and fish.

long_description.id: Strachey juga menggambarkan Okeus sebagai semacam iblis yang disembah agar murkanya terhindar, berlawanan dengan Ahone yang dianggap baik. Para sarjana seperti Helen C. Rountree dan Ives Goddard menilai gambaran semacam itu sebagai penyederhanaan kasar dan proyeksi dualisme Kristen.
long_description.en: Strachey likewise described Okeus as a kind of devil worshipped to avert his wrath, set against a supposedly benevolent Ahone. Scholars such as Helen C. Rountree and Ives Goddard regard such portrayals as gross oversimplifications that project Christian dualism.

short_description.id: Pixiu adalah makhluk campuran mitologis Tiongkok yang menyerupai singa bersayap.
short_description.en: Pixiu are Chinese mythological composite creatures resembling winged lions.

long_description.id: Pixiu adalah makhluk campuran mitologis Tiongkok yang menyerupai singa bersayap. Pixiu dianggap pelindung yang membawa keberuntungan dan kekayaan.
long_description.en: Pixiu are Chinese mythological composite creatures resembling winged lions. Pixiu are regarded as protectors bringing good fortune and wealth.

long_description.id: Salah satu pembagian membedakan Bixie bertanduk dua dan Tianlu bertanduk satu. Patungnya digunakan dalam feng shui untuk menarik kekayaan. Xu Ke menggambarkan pixiu menyerupai harimau atau beruang dengan bulu putih kelabu. Penggambarannya menggabungkan kepala naga Tiongkok dengan tubuh singa.
long_description.en: One division distinguishes two-antlered Bixie from single-antlered Tianlu. Their statues are used in feng shui to attract wealth. Xu Ke describes pixiu as tiger- or bear-like creatures with ashen-white fur. Their portrayal combines a Chinese dragon's head with a lion's body.

long_description.id: Sebuah kompilasi klasik mengumpulkan kutipan klasik tentang pi (貔), unsur pertama nama Pixiu. Pi dicatat sebagai binatang buas golongan macan tutul dari negeri He, juga disebut Zhiyi dan rubah putih, atau menyerupai harimau dan beruang. Shiji dikutip menyebut Huangdi melatih pixiu bersama beruang dan harimau untuk berperang melawan Kaisar Yan, sedangkan Liji dikutip menyebut pixiu dibawa ketika ada binatang buas di depan.
long_description.en: A classical compilation gathers classical quotations about the pi (貔), the first element of the name Pixiu. The pi is recorded as a fierce beast of the leopard kind from the state of He, also called Zhiyi and white fox, or as resembling a tiger and a bear. The Shiji is quoted as saying the Yellow Emperor trained pixiu with bears and tigers to fight the Yan Emperor, and the Liji as saying the pixiu is carried when fierce beasts lie ahead.

role.id: Disebut sebagai salah satu binatang yang dilatih untuk berperang
role.en: Named among the beasts trained for battle

summary.id: Shiji dikutip menyebut Huangdi melatih beruang, beruang cokelat, pixiu, chu, dan harimau untuk berperang melawan Kaisar Yan di padang Banquan.
summary.en: The Shiji is quoted as saying the Yellow Emperor trained bears, brown bears, pixiu, chu and tigers to fight the Yan Emperor in the wilds of Banquan.

statement.en: The same entry quotes the Shiji (Wudi Benji): the Yellow Emperor of the You Xiong clan trained bears, brown bears, pixiu (貔貅), chu (貙) and tigers to fight the Yan Emperor in the wilds of Banquan.

statement.en: The entry also quotes the Liji (Quli): "if there are fierce beasts ahead, carry the pixiu"; the commentary says fierce beasts are of the tiger and wolf kind, the pixiu are also fierce, and this is raised so that people know to be prepared.

claims.quote: 貔似虎，或曰似熊，一名「執夷」，一名「白狐。」其子為 遼 東人謂之「白羆。」
claims.locator: Gujin Tushu Jicheng, Qinchong dian juan 67, bagian 貔貅部

statement.id: Dalam kutipan dari Maoshi Lushu Guangyao, pi digambarkan menyerupai harimau atau, menurut sebagian orang, beruang; juga disebut Zhiyi dan rubah putih, dan orang Liaodong menyebut anaknya "beruang putih" (白羆).
statement.en: In the quotation from the Maoshi Lushu Guangyao, the pi is said to resemble a tiger or, as some say, a bear; it is also called Zhiyi and white fox, and the people of Liaodong call its young "white bear" (白羆).

short_description.id: Piztia (La Pistia dalam bahasa Spanyol) adalah binatang buas legendaris dari hutan sekitar Domaikia di Zuia, Álava. Konon ia tinggal di gua di gunung Carrascal, menghilangkan anak dan ternak, dan melahap apa pun pada malam hari.
short_description.en: The Piztia (La Pistia in Spanish) is a legendary wild beast of the woods around Domaikia in Zuia, Álava. It is said to live in a cave on Mount Carrascal, make children and livestock vanish, and devour everything at night.

long_description.id: Piztia atau La Pistia adalah binatang liar legendaris yang berkeliaran di hutan sekitar Domaikia, Zuia (Álava). Ia konon tinggal di gua di tebing Iruratxi, gunung Carrascal, dan membuat anak-anak serta ternak menghilang. Siang hari ia tidak berbahaya, tetapi malam hari ia melahap apa pun yang ditemuinya. Kisah-kisah lokal menyebut ia keluar dari sarangnya pada malam badai atau salju untuk menyerang ternak dan orang yang melintasi lembah menuju Jugo dan Murguia.
long_description.en: The Piztia or La Pistia is a legendary wild beast roaming the woods around Domaikia in Zuia (Álava). It is said to live in a cave on the Iruratxi crag of Mount Carrascal and to make children and livestock vanish. It is harmless by day, but at night it devours everything it finds. Local tales say it left its lair on stormy or snowy nights to attack livestock and people crossing the valley towards Jugo and Murguia.

long_description.id: Rupa dan hakikat makhluk ini tidak jelas. Sebagian orang menyebutnya bermata satu, sebagian raksasa, dan sebagian naga. Ada pula dugaan bahwa legenda ini berasal dari hewan liar nyata, misalnya beruang, atau bahwa ia versi lokal mitos Tartalo atau Anxo. Satu sumber menambahkan bahwa "pistia" adalah istilah di Tanah Basque untuk binatang yang tidak dikenal.
long_description.en: Its appearance and nature are unclear. Some call it one-eyed, some a giant, and some a dragon. Others suspect a real wild animal, such as a bear, gave rise to the legend, or that it is a local variant of the Tartalo or Anxo myth. One source adds that "pistia" is a Basque Country term for an unknown animal.

long_description.id: Pada abad ke-18 warga Domaikia memohon kepada Bunda Maria dari Oro agar teror Pistia berakhir, dan dari peristiwa itu lahir "Lagu Pistia" yang masih ada sampai sekarang. Menurut Julián de Olabarría, pastor Domaikia sendiri meninggalkan Murguia sebelum malam agar tidak bertemu Pistia dari Carrascal. Pada masa kini warga Domaikia mementaskan sandiwara "perburuan Piztia" untuk menjaga legenda ini tetap hidup.
long_description.en: In the 18th century the people of Domaikia prayed to Our Lady of Oro to end the Pistia's terror, giving rise to the "Song of the Pistia" that survives today. According to Julián de Olabarría, the priest of Domaikia himself left Murguia before nightfall so as not to meet the Pistia of Carrascal. Today the people of Domaikia stage a theatrical "hunt for Piztia" to keep the legend alive.

short_description.id: Poubi Lai adalah naga piton dalam mitologi dan cerita rakyat Meitei yang menghuni Danau Loktak di Manipur. Dalam kisahnya ia menyerang permukiman Moirang sebelum dibunuh oleh seorang maiba.
short_description.en: Poubi Lai is a dragon python of Meitei mythology and folklore that dwelled in Manipur's Loktak Lake. In the tale it attacks the settlements of Moirang before a maiba slays it.

long_description.id: Poubi Lai adalah naga piton purba dalam mitologi dan cerita rakyat Meitei yang menghuni Danau Loktak di Manipur. Ia juga disebut 'Loch Ness Monster of Manipur'. Dalam satu kisah, rohnya terbangun oleh kegiatan nelayan Moirang; ia marah, merusak banyak permukiman, dan membunuh banyak orang.
long_description.en: Poubi Lai is an old dragon python from Meitei myth that lived in Loktak Lake, Manipur, and is nicknamed the 'Loch Ness Monster of Manipur'. In one tale its spirit is awakened by the fishing of Moirang's fishermen; angered, it destroys many human habitats and kills many people.

long_description.id: Ia mengancam raja Moirang dan menuntut satu keranjang beras dan satu manusia setiap hari. Ketika giliran seorang pemuda tiba, ia meminta pertolongan Kabui Salang Maiba, seorang maiba sekaligus raja suku Kabui. Sang maiba mengubah tanaman Tou menjadi 'Long', lembing bermata sembilan, lalu membunuh Poubi Lai dengannya.
long_description.en: It threatens the king of Moirang and demands a basket of rice and one human every day. When it is a young man's turn, he seeks help from Kabui Salang Maiba, a maiba and king of the Kabui tribe. The maiba transforms a Tou plant into a 'Long', a nine-pointed javelin, and slays Poubi Lai with it.

long_description.id: Versi lain menempatkan Poubi Lai (Paobirai) di pulau Karang Hill di Danau Loktak, tempat ia memangsa nelayan Moirang dan menyerang permukiman. Sebuah naskah Meitei kuno bernama Khongul Lirakpa menyebut Poubi Lai.
long_description.en: Another version places Poubi Lai (Paobirai) on the isle of Karang Hill in Loktak Lake, where it hunts the fishermen of Moirang and attacks human settlements. An ancient Meitei manuscript called Khongul Lirakpa mentions Poubi Lai.

long_description.id: Pada 2002, menurut sebuah laporan berita, pemahat kayu Karam Dineshwar Singh mewujudkan patung sepanjang 21 kaki yang bermula dari mimpinya tentang Poubi Lai. Patung itu selesai dalam enam bulan, pertama dipamerkan di Museum Negara Bagian Manipur di Imphal, dan pernah dibawa ke Prancis untuk pameran. Pada 21 Juli 2015, pameran satu objek tentang Poubi Lai diresmikan di Museum Nasional, New Delhi.
long_description.en: According to a news report, in 2002 the wood-carver Karam Dineshwar Singh made a 21-foot-long sculpture that began with a dream of Poubi Lai. The work was finished in six months, first shown at the Manipur State Museum in Imphal, and later travelled to France for an exhibition. On 21 July 2015 a single-object exhibition about Poubi Lai was opened at the National Museum in New Delhi.

short_description.id: Pukwudgie adalah makhluk kerdil mirip manusia dalam cerita rakyat penduduk asli Amerika, yang jahil atau mengancam. Ia dikenal dalam cerita Wampanoag di Massachusetts, tetapi aslinya berasal dari dongeng Ojibwe di wilayah Great Lakes.
short_description.en: The Pukwudgie is a dwarfish, human-like being of Native American lore, either mischievous or menacing. It is best known from Wampanoag folklore in Massachusetts but began in an Ojibwe folktale of the Great Lakes region.

long_description.id: Pukwudgie adalah makhluk kerdil mirip manusia yang jahil atau mengancam dalam cerita penduduk asli Amerika. Dalam wujud aslinya ia konon setinggi lutut, berkulit abu-abu, dengan hidung, telinga, dan jari yang sangat besar, dan dapat berubah menjadi binatang berbahaya atau muncul dan menghilang sesuka hati. Mereka juga mungkin dapat mencelakai orang hanya dengan menatapnya.
long_description.en: The Pukwudgie is a dwarfish, human-like being in Native American lore, either mischievous or menacing. In its native form it is said to be knee-high and gray-skinned, with very large noses, ears and fingers, and it can turn into dangerous beasts or come and go as it pleases. Reportedly they can also hurt people just by glaring at them.

long_description.id: Pukwudgie dikenal dalam cerita Wampanoag di Massachusetts, meski awalnya merupakan bagian dari dongeng Ojibwe di wilayah Great Lakes. Menurut mitos Wampanoag, mereka semula roh penolong yang berniat baik tetapi ceroboh dan akhirnya menjadi musuh pahlawan budaya, raksasa Maushop dan istrinya. Orang Ojibwe cenderung menganggap mereka penjahil saja, sedangkan Wampanoag memperingatkan bahwa mereka dapat menembakkan panah beracun, memancing korban mati di hutan, mendorong orang dari tebing, menyulut api, dan menculik anak-anak.
long_description.en: The Pukwudgie is known from Wampanoag folklore in Massachusetts, though it was originally part of an Ojibwe folktale of the Great Lakes region. According to the Wampanoag myth they were originally well-intentioned but bungling helper spirits and became enemies of the culture heroes, the giant Maushop and his wife. The Ojibwe tend to see them as mere pranksters, while the Wampanoag warn that they may fire poisoned arrows, lure victims to their deaths in the forest, push people off cliffs, start fires and kidnap children.

long_description.id: Dongeng Ojibwa "Puck Wudj Ininee" dalam Algic Researches karya Schoolcraft (1839) menceritakan asal-usul orang kecil itu dari seorang anak yatim yang dapat menjadi tak terlihat. Longfellow memakai Puk-Wudjies dalam The Song of Hiawatha (1855), tempat mereka bersekongkol membunuh Kwasind dengan kerucut pinus. Nama Pukwudgie kemudian "diimpor ke Massachusetts", dan orang Wampanoag sengaja meminjamnya untuk menumbuhkan kesadaran budaya Indian.
long_description.en: The Ojibwa folktale "Puck Wudj Ininee" in Schoolcraft's Algic Researches (1839) tells of the origin of the little people from an orphaned boy who could become invisible. Longfellow used the Puk-Wudjies in The Song of Hiawatha (1855), where they conspire to kill Kwasind with pine-cones. The name Pukwudgie was later "imported to Massachusetts", and Wampanoag natives deliberately borrowed it for the purpose of Indian cultural awareness.

cultural_context.id: Penduduk Wampanoag sengaja meminjam "Pukwudgie" dalam cerita mereka demi menumbuhkan kesadaran budaya Indian, dan nama asli kaum kecil itu dalam bahasa-bahasa New England disebut hilang ditelan sejarah.
cultural_context.en: Wampanoag natives deliberately borrowed the "Pukwudgie" in their tales for the purpose of Indian cultural awareness, and the original name of the little people in New England languages is said to be lost to history.

statement.en: The term Pukwudgie is not attested as old usage in the Massachusetts area; the local natives did preserve folklore about the little people, but the original name they used in their New England languages is lost to history.

claims.quote: No man could compete with Kwasind. But the mischievous Puk-Wudjies, They the envious Little People, They the fairies and the pygmies, Plotted and conspired against him.

statement.id: Dalam puisi itu, Puk-Wudjies disebut jahil dan iri, "Orang Kecil", peri dan kurcaci, yang bersekongkol melawan Kwasind, yang tak tertandingi.
statement.en: In the poem the Puk-Wudjies are called mischievous and envious "Little People", fairies and pygmies, who plotted and conspired against Kwasind, whom no man could match.

claims.quote: In his birch canoe came Kwasind, ... Underneath the war encampment Of the pygmies, the Puk-Wudjies. There they stood, all armed and waiting, Hurled the pine-cones down upon him, Struck him on his brawny shoulders, On his crown defenceless struck him.

claims.quote: Now this wondrous strength of Kwasind In his crown alone was seated ... Even there the only weapon That could wound him, that could slay him, Was the seed-cone of the pine-tree, Was the blue cone of the fir-tree.

statement.id: Dalam puisi itu, satu-satunya senjata yang dapat melukai dan membunuh Kwasind adalah kerucut biji pohon pinus dan kerucut biru pohon cemara.

short_description.id: Qallupilluit adalah makhluk pantai Arktik dalam mitologi Inuit yang menculik anak-anak yang terlalu dekat dengan air [qallupilluit-c01].
short_description.en: The Qallupilluit are Arctic shore creatures of Inuit mythology that steal children who stray too near the water [qallupilluit-c01].

long_description.id: Qallupilluit atau Qalupalik adalah makhluk yang hidup di pantai Arktik dekat bongkahan es dan menculik anak-anak yang terlalu dekat dengan air [qallupilluit-c01]. Mereka digambarkan berkulit hijau berlendir dan berkuku panjang [qallupilluit-c03], dan mengenakan parka amautik [qallupilluit-c04]. Mitos ini diyakini melindungi anak-anak dari bahaya es laut [qallupilluit-c02].
long_description.en: The Qallupilluit or Qalupalik live along Arctic shores near ice floes and steal children who come too close [qallupilluit-c01]. They have green, slimy skin and long nails [qallupilluit-c03] and wear an amautik parka [qallupilluit-c04]. The myth is thought to protect children from sea-ice dangers [qallupilluit-c02].

long_description.id: Catatan etnografi lama yang memakai ejaan Kalopaling menggambarkan makhluk ajaib yang hidup di laut, bertubuh seperti manusia, dan berpakaian kulit bebek eider [qallupilluit-c05]. Jaketnya berkerudung besar yang ditakuti orang Inuit, dan pendayung kayak yang tenggelam konon dimasukkan ke dalamnya [qallupilluit-c06]. Kakinya sangat besar, tampak seperti pelampung kulit anjing laut [qallupilluit-c07], dan orang Inuit percaya jumlah makhluk semacam ini dulu banyak tetapi kini tinggal sedikit [qallupilluit-c08].
long_description.en: An old ethnographic account using the spelling Kalopaling describes a fabulous being that lives in the sea, with a human-like body, wearing eider duck skins [qallupilluit-c05]. Its jacket has an enormous hood feared by the Inuit, and a drowned kayaker is said to be put into it [qallupilluit-c06]. Its feet are very large, like inflated sealskin floats [qallupilluit-c07], and the Inuit believe such beings were once many but are now few [qallupilluit-c08].

long_description.id: Dalam sebuah tradisi tua, seorang nenek yang marah memanggil Kalopaling untuk membawa cucunya, yang dimasukkan ke dalam kerudung besar dan hampir seketika lenyap [qallupilluit-c09]. Halaman yang menyajikan kisah yang sama menamai tokoh itu Qallupilluk [qallupilluit-c10].
long_description.en: In an old tradition, an angry grandmother called Kalopaling to take her grandson, who was put into the large hood and almost immediately disappeared [qallupilluit-c09]. A page presenting the same tale names the being Qallupilluk [qallupilluit-c10].

cultural_context.id: Mitos Qallupilluit berfungsi menjauhkan anak-anak dari es laut yang berbahaya [qallupilluit-c02].
cultural_context.en: The myth keeps children away from dangerous sea ice [qallupilluit-c02].

claims.quote: In Inuit mythology, the Qallupilluit or Qalupalik are creatures that live along Arctic shorelines near ice floes. They are said to steal children that wander too close to the water.

statement.id: Dalam mitologi Inuit, Qallupilluit atau Qalupalik adalah makhluk penghuni pantai Arktik dekat bongkahan es yang konon menculik anak-anak yang terlalu dekat dengan air.
statement.en: In Inuit mythology, the Qallupilluit or Qalupalik live along Arctic shores near ice floes and steal children who stray too close to the water.

claims.quote: This myth is believed to serve the purpose of protecting children from a dangerous environment, such as keeping them from playing on hazardous sea ice.

statement.id: Mitos ini diyakini berfungsi melindungi anak-anak dari lingkungan berbahaya, seperti bermain di atas es laut.
statement.en: The myth is thought to protect children from dangers such as playing on hazardous sea ice.

claims.quote: The Qallupilluit is often described as having green, slimy skin, long hair, and long fingernails.

statement.id: Qallupilluit sering digambarkan berkulit hijau berlendir, berambut panjang, dan berkuku panjang.
statement.en: It is often described with green, slimy skin, long hair and long fingernails.

claims.quote: It wears an amautik, an Inuit parka mostly worn by women.

statement.id: Ia mengenakan amautik, parka Inuit yang kebanyakan dipakai perempuan.
statement.en: It wears an amautik, an Inuit parka mostly worn by women.

claims.quote: Kalopaling is a fabulous being that lives in the sea. His body is like that of a human being and he wears clothing made of eider ducks’ skins.

statement.id: Dalam teks etnografi ini, Kalopaling adalah makhluk ajaib yang hidup di laut, bertubuh seperti manusia, dan berpakaian kulit bebek eider.
statement.en: In this ethnographic text, Kalopaling is a fabulous being that lives in the sea, with a human-like body, wearing clothing made of eider duck skins.

claims.quote: His jacket has an enormous hood, which is an object of fear to the Inuit. If a kayak capsizes and the boatman is drowned Kalopaling puts him into this hood.

statement.id: Jaketnya berkerudung besar yang ditakuti orang Inuit; jika kayak terbalik dan pendayungnya tenggelam, Kalopaling memasukkannya ke dalam kerudung itu.
statement.en: His jacket has an enormous hood, feared by the Inuit; if a kayak capsizes and the boatman drowns, Kalopaling puts him into this hood.

claims.quote: His feet are very large and look like inflated sealskin floats.

statement.id: Kakinya sangat besar dan tampak seperti pelampung kulit anjing laut yang digembungkan.
statement.en: His feet are very large and look like inflated sealskin floats.

claims.quote: The Inuit believe that in olden times there were a great number of Kalopalit, but gradually their number diminished and there are now very few left.

statement.id: Orang Inuit percaya bahwa dahulu ada banyak Kalopalit, tetapi jumlahnya berangsur berkurang dan kini tinggal sedikit.
statement.en: The Inuit believe there were once a great number of Kalopalit, but their number gradually diminished and very few are left.

claims.quote: The grandmother told him to be quiet, but as he did not obey she became angry and called Kalopaling to come and take him away. He entered at once and the woman put the boy into the large hood, in which he disappeared almost immediately.

statement.id: Dalam sebuah tradisi tua, seorang nenek yang marah memanggil Kalopaling untuk membawa cucunya; makhluk itu masuk dan memasukkan anak itu ke dalam kerudung besarnya, tempat anak itu hampir seketika lenyap.
statement.en: In an old tradition, an angry grandmother called Kalopaling to take her grandson; it entered and put the boy into its large hood, where he almost immediately disappeared.

claims.quote: called Qallupilluk to come and take him away. He entered at once and the woman put the boy into the large hood

statement.id: Pada halaman yang menyajikan kisah yang sama, tokoh itu dinamai Qallupilluk: sang nenek memanggilnya untuk membawa si anak, yang lalu dimasukkan ke kerudung besar.
statement.en: On the page presenting the same tale, the being is named Qallupilluk: the grandmother called it to take the boy, who was put into the large hood.

claims.quote: While some interpretations include the pronoun 'he', the Qallupilluit is predominantly described in a feminine manner.

statement.id: Beberapa tafsir memakai kata ganti "dia laki-laki", tetapi Qallupilluit terutama digambarkan secara feminin.
statement.en: Some interpretations use the pronoun "he", but the Qallupilluit is predominantly described in a feminine manner.

long_description.en: Qiongqi is a mythological creature in Chinese classics counted among the Four Perils. Its name is interpreted as exhaustively strange.

long_description.id: Catatan Sejarawan Agung menggambarkannya sebagai anak Shaohao yang tidak setia dan berbohong. Shanhaijing memberikan dua gambaran Qiongqi yang saling bertentangan.
long_description.en: The Records of the Grand Historian portrays it as Shaohao's child acting disloyally and lying. The Shanhaijing gives two conflicting descriptions of Qiongqi.

long_description.id: Shanhaijing memberi dua gambaran. Dalam Xi shan jing, Qiongqi di Gunung Gui berbentuk seperti sapi berbulu landak, bersuara seperti anjing menggonggong, dan memakan orang. Dalam Hainei beijing, ia berbentuk seperti harimau bersayap, memakan orang mulai dari kepala, dan tinggal di sebelah utara Taoquan. Versi lain dalam teks itu menyebut ia mulai dari kaki.
long_description.en: The Shanhaijing gives two descriptions. In the Xi shan jing, the Qiongqi on Mount Gui is shaped like an ox with hedgehog bristles, cries like a barking dog and eats people. In the Hainei beijing it is shaped like a winged tiger, eats people from the head and lives north of Taoquan. Another version in that text says it starts from the feet.

long_description.id: Zuo Zhuan menyatakan Qiongqi menjunjung dusta, menyebarkan tuduhan palsu, dan diam sebelum memfitnah. Biografi-biografi itu menyebut Qiongqi tinggal di Yunmeng di Negara Chu. Book of Gods and Strange Things menambahkan bahwa ia memahami bahasa manusia: ia memakan pihak yang benar dalam pertengkaran, memakan hidung orang yang setia, dan membunuh binatang untuk diberikan kepada orang jahat. Dalam budaya populer modern, Qiongqi tampil sebagai iblis yang dapat direkrut dalam gim Shin Megami Tensei.
long_description.en: The Zuo Zhuan states that Qiongqi elevated lies, spread false accusations and stayed quiet before slandering people. The biographies place Qiongqi at Yunmeng in the State of Chu. The Book of Gods and Strange Things adds that it understands human speech: it eats the one in the right in a quarrel, eats the nose of the loyal, and kills a beast to feed the wicked. In modern popular culture, Qiongqi appears as a recruitable demon in the Shin Megami Tensei games.

short_description.id: Harimau Queensland, juga disebut yarri oleh penduduk Pribumi, adalah makhluk bergaris seukuran anjing dalam cerita rakyat Australia timur; para pengamat tidak sepakat apakah ia hewan tak dikenal, thylacine, thylacoleo, atau kucing liar.
short_description.en: The Queensland tiger, also called yarri by Indigenous people, is a striped, dog-sized creature of eastern Australian folklore; observers disagree on whether it is an unknown animal, a thylacine, a thylacoleo or a feral cat.

long_description.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Australia, harimau Queensland adalah makhluk yang konon hidup di wilayah Queensland di Australia timur. Penduduk Pribumi menyebutnya yarri, dan ia digambarkan sebagai kucing bergaris seukuran anjing dengan ekor panjang, gigi depan menonjol, dan watak ganas. Laporan saksi yang terdokumentasi paling awal berasal dari 1871, dan tradisi Pribumi tentang yarri mendahuluinya.
long_description.en: Australian folklore places the Queensland tiger, a creature of legend, in the Queensland region of eastern Australia. Indigenous people call it yarri, and it is pictured as a striped feline the size of a dog with a long tail, prominent front teeth and a violent temper. The earliest documented witness reports date from 1871, and Indigenous traditions of the yarri came before them.

long_description.id: Dalam catatan Lumholtz, penduduk setempat menggambarkan yarri sebagai hewan seukuran dingo berkaki lebih pendek dan berekor panjang, sangat ganas, yang memanjat pohon bila dikejar dan menggeram serta menggigit tangan. Tempat berlindung berbatu adalah habitat favoritnya dan makanan utamanya sejenis wallaby cokelat kecil. Dagingnya tidak terlalu disukai, dan bila tak sengaja membunuh yarri mereka memberikannya kepada para perempuan tua. Menurut takhayul, "air besar akan naik" bila seorang pemuda memungut yarri yang mati.
long_description.en: Lumholtz's account has local people picturing the yarri as dingo-sized, shorter in the leg and long in the tail, very savage, taking to the trees when chased and snarling and biting at hands. Rocky refuges suited it best and it fed mainly on a small brown wallaby. People did not much value its meat and passed any yarri they happened to kill to the old women. A superstition held that "a great water will rise" should a young man lift a dead yarri.

long_description.id: Lumholtz kemudian memperoleh seekor yarri muda dan mengenalinya sebagai Dasyurus maculatus, sambil menulis bahwa yarri adalah nama yang dipakai untuk seluruh satu famili; namun ia yakin masih ada hewan besar sejenis yang belum ditemukan. Ia juga mendengar di Queensland Barat tentang hewan yang tampaknya identik.
long_description.en: Lumholtz later obtained a young yarri and identified it as Dasyurus maculatus, writing that yarri is a name applied to a whole family; yet he was convinced that a large animal of the kind remained undiscovered. In Western Queensland he also heard of an animal that seemed identical.

long_description.id: Berbagai penjelasan diajukan. Pada 1926 A. S. le Souef menggambarkan "kucing berkantung bergaris", dan Ellis Troughton pada 1965 mengusulkan bahwa harimau Queensland adalah varian daratan thylacine. Ada pula hipotesis bahwa ia penyintas Thylacoleo atau kucing liar besar, dan usul bahwa penampakan adalah kanguru pohon Lumholtz atau Bennett. Penampakan modern yang diselidiki selalu dipersempit menjadi kucing liar. Pada 1970-an Janeice Plunkett mengumpulkan lebih dari 100 laporan "harimau", dan teori kelangsungan hidup Thylacoleo dan thylacine pernah diulas di televisi.
long_description.en: Several explanations have been offered. In 1926 A. S. le Souef described a "Striped marsupial cat", and in 1965 Ellis Troughton proposed that the Queensland tiger was a mainland variant of the thylacine. Others hypothesise a surviving Thylacoleo or a large feral cat, and some suggest the sightings are Lumholtz's or Bennett's tree-kangaroos. Modern sightings that were investigated were always narrowed down to feral cats. In the 1970s Janeice Plunkett gathered over 100 reports of "tigers", and the survival theories for Thylacoleo and the thylacine have been covered on television.

short_description.id: Raijū adalah yōkai Jepang berwujud hewan yang dikaitkan dengan kilat, guntur, dan dewa Raijin.
short_description.en: Raijū is a Japanese yōkai in animal form, linked to lightning, thunder and the god Raijin.

long_description.id: Raijū (雷獣, secara harfiah "binatang guntur") adalah makhluk legenda dan yōkai yang dikaitkan dengan kilat dan guntur serta dewa Raijin. Konon ia muncul bersama sambaran petir. Tubuhnya digambarkan tersusun dari kilat atau diselubungi kilat, dan ia disebut pendamping Raijin, dewa kilat Shinto.
long_description.en: The raijū (雷獣, "thunder beast") is a yōkai, a legendary creature tied to lightning, thunder, and the god Raijin. It is said to appear with lightning strikes. Its body is described as composed of, or wrapped in, lightning, and it is called the companion of Raijin, the Shinto god of lightning.

long_description.id: Raijū digambarkan sebagai perwujudan kilat dalam bentuk hewan, dengan cakar panjang yang tajam dan wajah garang. Umumnya ia dianggap mirip serigala, anjing, tanuki, atau bahkan musang dan kucing. Legendanya ada di seluruh Jepang, terutama di Jepang bagian timur, dan namanya sering muncul dalam esai zaman Edo serta bahan folklor modern.
long_description.en: The raijū is described as the embodiment of lightning in animal form, with long sharp claws and ferocious faces. It was generally thought to resemble wolves, dogs, tanuki, or even weasels or cats. Legends of it exist throughout Japan, centered mainly in East Japan, and the name turns up often in essays from the Edo period and in modern folklore sources.

long_description.id: Raijū disebut hidup di langit, dunia yang sebelum abad ke-20 sama sekali tak terjangkau manusia, dan menunggangi sambaran kilat turun ke bumi saat guntur menggelegar. Pada masa lampau ia dipandang sebagai binatang ilahi yang setara dengan dewa-dewa guntur. Raijū kecil disebut menyusup ke pusar manusia untuk bersembunyi dari dewa guntur yang murka. Dalam cerita, raijū biasanya muncul sebagai binatang yang harus dibunuh, seperti oni.
long_description.en: Raijū are said to live in the sky, a world totally off limits to humans before the 20th century, and to ride bolts of lightning to earth when thunder claps. Long ago they were seen as divine beasts, akin to the thunder gods. Small raijū are said to burrow into human belly buttons to hide from angry thunder gods. In stories, raijū usually appear as beasts to be slain, like oni.

long_description.id: Pada zaman Edo, sisa-sisa kucing, monyet, dan anjing yang dimumikan atau diawetkan dipamerkan sebagai raijū dalam pertunjukan keliling. Pada zaman Meiji, yōkai seperti raijū termasuk korban pertama modernisasi akibat masuknya sains dan teknologi asing.
long_description.en: Mummified and taxidermied remains of cats, monkeys, and dogs were presented as raijū in traveling shows. In the Meiji period, yōkai like raijū were among the first victims of modernization brought by foreign science and technology.

did_you_know.id: Takhayul Jepang untuk menutupi pusar saat mendengar guntur berasal dari kepercayaan bahwa raijū kecil menyusup ke pusar manusia untuk bersembunyi dari dewa guntur.
did_you_know.en: The Japanese superstition of covering the belly button when thunder is heard comes from the belief that small raijū burrow into human belly buttons to hide from angry thunder gods.

short_description.id: Red Ghost adalah sosok cerita rakyat Arizona berupa unta merah besar dengan kerangka manusia di punggungnya [red-ghost-folklore-c01, red-ghost-folklore-c02].
short_description.en: The Red Ghost is an Arizona folklore figure: a large red camel with a human skeleton on its back [red-ghost-folklore-c01, red-ghost-folklore-c02].

long_description.id: Red Ghost adalah sosok cerita rakyat Arizona yang konon berkeliaran pada akhir abad ke-19 [red-ghost-folklore-c01], berupa unta merah besar dengan kerangka manusia di punggungnya [red-ghost-folklore-c02]. Latar belakangnya adalah eksperimen Camel Corps yang disetujui pada tahun 1855 [red-ghost-folklore-c03].
long_description.en: The Red Ghost is an Arizona folklore figure said to have roamed in the late 19th century [red-ghost-folklore-c01], a large red camel with a human skeleton on its back [red-ghost-folklore-c02]. Its background is the Camel Corps experiment approved in 1855 [red-ghost-folklore-c03].

long_description.id: Legenda bermula pada tahun 1883 dekat Eagle Creek [red-ghost-folklore-c04], ketika seorang perempuan ditemukan tewas terinjak-injak [red-ghost-folklore-c05].
long_description.en: The legend began in 1883 near Eagle Creek [red-ghost-folklore-c04], when a woman was found trampled to death [red-ghost-folklore-c05].

long_description.id: Pada 1893, The Mohave County Miner memberitakan Red Ghost sebagai unta mengamuk dengan mayat terikat di punggungnya [red-ghost-folklore-c06]. Seorang pemburu disebut melihatnya dari jauh dan mengira benda di punggung itu mayat [red-ghost-folklore-c07]. Berbagai kisah beredar: ia membunuh dan memakan beruang grizzly, atau lenyap ke udara saat dikejar, dan kerangka di punggungnya menjadi unsur umum [red-ghost-folklore-c14]. Pada satu penampakan ia digambarkan setinggi 30 kaki dan menggulingkan dua gerobak [red-ghost-folklore-c15].
long_description.en: In 1893, The Mohave County Miner reported the Red Ghost as a rampant camel with a dead man strapped to its back [red-ghost-folklore-c06]. A hunter was said to have seen it from afar and thought the thing on its back was a corpse [red-ghost-folklore-c07]. Various tales circulated: it killed and ate a grizzly bear, or vanished into thin air when chased, and the skeleton on its back was a common element [red-ghost-folklore-c14]. In one sighting it was described as 30 feet tall, knocking over two wagons [red-ghost-folklore-c15].

long_description.id: Legenda ini berakhir pada 1893 ketika Mizoo Hastings menembak makhluk itu [red-ghost-folklore-c09], dan ternyata seekor unta berikat tali kulit mentah di punggungnya [red-ghost-folklore-c08]. Mengapa ada jenazah di punggungnya tidak diketahui; ada yang menduga seorang pendulang yang mengikat dirinya, ada yang menyebut seorang prajurit yang sedang belajar menunggang unta [red-ghost-folklore-c13]. Unta memang sempat berkeliaran di Arizona setelah Camel Corps dibubarkan pada 1863 [red-ghost-folklore-c11], dan penulis menduga Red Ghost bisa jadi sisa rencana pemerintah yang dibubarkan atau harapan usaha dagang [red-ghost-folklore-c12], meski tidak ada jejak laporan sebelum 1893 [red-ghost-folklore-c10].
long_description.en: The legend ended in 1893 when Mizoo Hastings shot the creature [red-ghost-folklore-c09], and it turned out to be a camel with rawhide straps on its back [red-ghost-folklore-c08]. Why a dead man was on its back is unknown; some suggest a prospector who tied himself on, others a soldier learning to ride a camel [red-ghost-folklore-c13]. Camels did roam Arizona after the Camel Corps was dissolved in 1863 [red-ghost-folklore-c11], and the author suggests the Red Ghost may well have been a remnant of dissolved government plans or business enterprise hopes [red-ghost-folklore-c12], although there is no trace of reports before 1893 [red-ghost-folklore-c10].

short_description.id: Ro-langs adalah mayat bangkit dalam cerita rakyat Tibet.
short_description.en: Ro-langs are risen corpses in Tibetan folklore.

long_description.id: Ro-langs adalah mayat bangkit dalam cerita rakyat Tibet. Namanya secara harfiah bermakna mayat yang telah bangkit.
long_description.en: Ro-langs are risen corpses in Tibetan folklore. The name literally means a corpse that has risen.

long_description.id: Ro-langs biasanya dibangkitkan oleh roh gdon atau ahli sihir. Makhluk ini tidak dapat berbicara atau membungkuk dan bergerak dengan sendi kaku. Jenis tantrik dibangkitkan melalui ritual untuk keperluan orang yang melakukan pemanggilan. Jenis demonik digambarkan mandiri dan berusaha mencemari manusia lain.
long_description.en: Ro-langs are usually raised by a gdon spirit or a sorcerer. The creature cannot speak or bend over and moves with stiff joints. The tantric type is raised through ritual for the purposes of the person performing it. The demonic type is described as independent and intent on contaminating other humans.

long_description.id: Ro-lang secara harfiah berarti mayat yang bangkit dan sering dibandingkan dengan zombi voodoo, walaupun kemiripannya dangkal. Berbeda dengan zombi budaya populer yang menggigit, ro-lang menyerang dengan menaruh telapak tangannya di kepala korban. Karena ro-lang dipercaya tidak dapat membungkuk, banyak bangunan Tibet dibuat dengan pintu atau langit-langit rendah. Dalam catatan Fosco Maraini, asisten lokalnya percaya bahwa melempar sepatu dapat mengalahkan ro-lang.
long_description.en: Ro-lang literally means risen corpse and is often compared with the voodoo zombie, though the resemblance is superficial. Unlike popular-culture zombies, which bite, the ro-lang attacks by placing its palm on the victim's head. Because ro-lang were believed unable to bend, many Tibetan buildings had low doorways or ceilings. In Fosco Maraini's account, his local assistant believed that throwing a shoe could defeat a ro-lang.

description.id: Karena ro-langs dipercaya tidak dapat membungkuk, bangunan dibuat dengan pintu dan langit-langit rendah.
description.en: Because ro-langs were believed unable to bend, buildings were made with low doorways and ceilings.

sources.title: The Long View: Tantric Rituals and Tibetan Zombies?

claims.quote: A ro-langs (Tibetan: རོ་ལང) is a zombie-like creature from Tibetan folklore.  Ro is the word for corpse and Langs is the perfect tense of "to rise up", so Ro-Langs literally means "a risen corpse".  A ro-langs is usually created by a gdon spirit, or a sorcerer.   A ro-langs cannot speak or bend over, it signals its victims by wagging its tongue back and forth.

A ro-langs cannot speak or bend over, it signals its victims by wagging its tongue back and forth.

statement.id: Ro-langs biasanya dibangkitkan oleh roh gdon atau ahli sihir.
statement.en: Ro-langs are usually raised by a gdon spirit or a sorcerer.

claims.quote: A ro-langs cannot speak or bend over, it signals its victims by wagging its tongue back and forth.  They can not bend any joints, which makes them walk with a stiff-armed lurch.

statement.id: Makhluk ini tidak dapat berbicara atau membungkuk dan bergerak dengan sendi kaku.
statement.en: The creature cannot speak or bend over and moves with stiff joints.

claims.quote: The tantric types of ro-langs are raised from the dead through a ritual for personal reasons, such as to serve a necromancer and satisfy his lust for the power of the occult.  A religious  history  written  by  Kun-dga'- snying-po contains one example.  Na-ra-da gained mystical powers and set off to raise a ro-langs.  He enlisted the help of a Buddhist Votary.

statement.id: Jenis tantrik dibangkitkan melalui ritual untuk keperluan orang yang melakukan pemanggilan.
statement.en: The tantric type is raised through ritual for the purposes of the person performing it.

claims.quote: Demonic ro-langs are created by an evil spirit with the goal of contaminating other humans; they are independent, and do not serve a master. They are created by either a gdon spirit that has broken its oath and become evil, or a bgegs spirit, which is already evil.  Once the consciousness has left the body, the evil spirit enters the body before it is buried.

statement.id: Jenis demonik digambarkan mandiri dan berusaha mencemari manusia lain.
statement.en: The demonic type is described as independent and intent on contaminating other humans.

claims.quote: The Tibetan ro-lang (རོ་ལང) literally translates as risen corpse. It bears an obvious superficial similarity to the voodoo zombie, in that it is the corpse of a dead human being, animated through spiritual practice/intervention.

statement.id: Ro-lang Tibet secara harfiah berarti mayat yang bangkit; ia mirip secara dangkal dengan zombi voodoo karena berupa jasad manusia yang dihidupkan lewat praktik atau campur tangan spiritual.
statement.en: The Tibetan ro-lang literally means risen corpse; it superficially resembles the voodoo zombie in being a dead human body animated through spiritual practice or intervention.

claims.quote: In contrast to the zombies one finds in modern popular culture which usually carry out this process with a bite, the ro-lang carries out its attack by placing its palm on their head.

statement.id: Berbeda dengan zombi dalam budaya populer modern yang biasanya menggigit, ro-lang menyerang dengan menaruh telapak tangannya di kepala korban.
statement.en: Unlike zombies of modern popular culture, which usually bite, the ro-lang attacks by placing its palm on the victim's head.

claims.quote: Many buildings were constructed with low ceilings — as many people believed that the ro-lang was incapable of bending down.
claims.locator: So is a ro-lang a zombie?

statement.id: Banyak bangunan dibuat dengan langit-langit rendah karena orang percaya ro-lang tidak dapat membungkuk.
statement.en: Many buildings were built with low ceilings because people believed the ro-lang could not bend down.

claims.quote: By contrast, in photographer Fosco Maraini’s account of his journey through Tibet he describes that his local assistant stated that ‘oddly shaped rocks’ bore some resemblance to ro-lang. His defensive weapon of choice was a shoe, believing that throwing a shoe at a ro-lang would defeat it.

statement.id: Dalam catatan perjalanan fotografer Fosco Maraini di Tibet, asisten lokalnya berkata bahwa batu berbentuk aneh mirip ro-lang, dan ia percaya melempar sepatu ke ro-lang dapat mengalahkannya.
statement.en: In photographer Fosco Maraini's account of his journey through Tibet, his local assistant said that oddly shaped rocks resembled ro-lang and believed that throwing a shoe at a ro-lang would defeat it.

claims.quote: Ro-langs are unable to bend at the waist; to exploit this weakness, many buildings in early Tibetan architecture were built with very low door frames.

statement.id: Ro-langs tidak dapat membungkuk di pinggang; untuk memanfaatkan kelemahan ini, banyak bangunan Tibet awal dibuat dengan kusen pintu yang sangat rendah.
statement.en: Ro-langs cannot bend at the waist; to exploit this weakness, many early Tibetan buildings had very low door frames.

short_description.id: Sankai adalah yōkai "monster kelahiran" dalam cerita rakyat Jepang yang konon lahir dari seorang perempuan; di berbagai daerah dikenal sebagai oketsu, kekkai, atau kekke.
short_description.en: The sankai is a "birth monster" yōkai of Japanese folklore said to be born to a woman; in different regions it is known as oketsu, kekkai or kekke.

long_description.id: Sankai adalah monster kelahiran dalam cerita rakyat Jepang. Mitos menghubungkan kelahirannya dengan kurangnya perawatan selama kehamilan. Sebuah penjelasan menyebut bahwa janin hasil keguguran serta bayi cacat atau prematur dahulu dipandang sebagai yōkai semacam ini.
long_description.en: The sankai is a birth monster in Japanese folklore. The myth connects its birth with insufficient care during pregnancy. One explanation says that fetuses lost to miscarriage, and deformed or premature infants, were formerly regarded as yōkai of this kind.

long_description.id: Versi dari Okayama disebut oketsu. Ia menyerupai kura-kura dengan rambut di punggung dan konon merangkak ke bawah rumah segera setelah lahir. Bila tidak segera ditangkap dan dibunuh, ia konon merangkak ke bawah ibu yang tidur dan membunuhnya.
long_description.en: The version from Okayama is called oketsu. It resembles a turtle with hair on its back and is said to crawl beneath the house immediately after birth. If it is not captured and killed right away, it is said to crawl under the sleeping mother and kill her.

long_description.id: Wilayah lain memakai nama seperti kekkai dan kekke. Kekkai konon menyerupai sapi berbulu dan menggali ke bawah rumah untuk membunuh ibunya; catatan lain menyebut dua lidah dan bulu yang tumbuh terbalik. Di Urawa, sekat byōbu dipasang di sekeliling bagian bawah rumah saat persalinan, dan di wilayah Ashigara seseorang menjaga perapian dengan shamoji.
long_description.en: Other regions use names such as kekkai and kekke. The kekkai is said to look like hairy cattle and to bury under the house to kill its mother; another account gives two tongues and hair growing backwards. In Urawa, byōbu screens were set around the bottom of the house during childbirth, and in the Ashigara region someone guarded the hearth with a shamoji.

long_description.id: Folklorawan Iwao Hino kemudian menduga kekkai yang ia lihat di pertunjukan keanehan semasa kecil adalah monyet malam yang dijinakkan. Kamus Digital Daijisen mencatat "kekkai" sebagai nama populer loris yang dipertontonkan pada zaman Edo.
long_description.en: The folklorist Iwao Hino later believed that the kekkai he saw at a freak show as a child must have been a trained night monkey. The Digital Daijisen dictionary records "kekkai" as a popular name for a loris exhibited in the Edo period.

literal_meaning.id: Secara harfiah "monster kelahiran"; untuk nama kekkai, ada teori asal dari kekkai (結界), kawasan yang dibatasi karena alasan keagamaan.
literal_meaning.en: Literally "birth monster"; for the name kekkai, one theory derives it from kekkai (結界), an area restricted for religious reasons.

origin.id: Menurut mitos, ia muncul bila perawatan selama kehamilan tidak memadai.

description.id: Oketsu konon merangkak ke bawah ibu yang tidur dan membunuhnya bila tidak segera dibunuh; kekkai konon menggali ke bawah rumah untuk membunuh ibunya.
description.en: The oketsu is said to crawl under the sleeping mother and kill her if not killed right away; the kekkai is said to bury under the house to kill its mother.

description.id: Dalam kisah oketsu, makhluk itu harus ditangkap dan dibunuh segera; bila tidak, ia konon membunuh ibunya.

description.id: Di wilayah Ashigara, seseorang berjaga di irori, biasanya dengan shamoji, agar kekkai tidak lolos dan perempuan itu tidak meninggal.
description.en: In the Ashigara region someone guarded the irori, typically with a shamoji, so that the kekkai would not escape and the woman would not die.

statement.en: Legends about the kekkai's appearance are sparse, but it is said to look like cattle and to be hairy; it is also said to bury under the house to kill its mother.

claims.quote: In Urawa, a practice existed of surrounding the bottom of a house with byōbu during childbirth to prevent this maneuver.

statement.id: Di Urawa pernah ada kebiasaan mengelilingi bagian bawah rumah dengan byōbu (sekat lipat) saat persalinan untuk mencegah gerakan itu.
statement.en: In Urawa, a practice existed of surrounding the bottom of the house with byōbu (folding screens) during childbirth to prevent this maneuver.

claims.quote: In the Ashigara region of Kanagawa Prefecture, the sankai is said to move immediately while still bloody, the jizaikagi of an irori, or hearth. If the kekkai successfully escapes, the woman was believed to die. In order to prevent this, someone would have to guard the irori, typically equipped with a shamoji.

statement.id: Di wilayah Ashigara, Prefektur Kanagawa, sankai konon bergerak segera selagi masih berlumuran darah; bila kekkai berhasil kabur, sang perempuan dipercaya meninggal, sehingga seseorang harus menjaga irori (perapian), biasanya dengan memegang shamoji.
statement.en: In the Ashigara region of Kanagawa Prefecture the sankai is said to move at once while still bloody; if the kekkai escaped, the woman was believed to die, so someone had to guard the irori (hearth), typically equipped with a shamoji.

claims.quote: It is theorized that the etymology may derive from kekkai (結界), meaning an area restricted for religious reasons.

statement.id: Ada teori bahwa nama kekkai mungkin berasal dari kekkai (結界), yakni kawasan yang dibatasi karena alasan keagamaan.
statement.en: It is theorized that the name kekkai may derive from kekkai (結界), meaning an area restricted for religious reasons.

claims.quote: Folklorist Iwao Hino recalls spotting a kekkai at a freak show during childhood. The show stated that it was given birth by a woman at a University hospital, however Hino later believed that it must have been a trained night monkey.

statement.id: Folklorawan Iwao Hino mengingat pernah melihat kekkai di pertunjukan keanehan semasa kecil; pertunjukan itu menyebutnya dilahirkan seorang perempuan di rumah sakit universitas, tetapi Hino kemudian meyakini itu monyet malam yang dijinakkan.
statement.en: Folklorist Iwao Hino recalls seeing a kekkai at a freak show as a child; the show said a woman gave birth to it at a university hospital, but Hino later believed it must have been a trained night monkey.

claims.quote: そのために流産で産まれた胎児、早産などの異常出産で産まれた奇形児や未熟児が、これらのように妖怪視されたといわれる。

statement.id: Dikatakan bahwa janin hasil keguguran serta bayi cacat atau prematur dari kelahiran tidak normal seperti kelahiran dini dahulu dipandang sebagai yōkai semacam ini.
statement.en: It is said that fetuses lost to miscarriage, and deformed or premature infants born from abnormal births such as premature birth, were formerly regarded as yōkai of this kind.

claims.quote: 血塊(けっかい)は、埼玉県、神奈川県に伝わる妖怪。長野県ではケッケという。舌が二枚有り毛が逆さに生えている、または口や鼻が牛に似て毛むくじゃらの姿をしているといわれる。

statement.id: Kekkai, yōkai dari Prefektur Saitama dan Kanagawa (di Nagano disebut kekke), konon berlidah dua dengan bulu tumbuh terbalik, atau bermulut dan berhidung seperti sapi serta berbulu lebat.
statement.en: The kekkai, a yōkai of Saitama and Kanagawa Prefectures (called kekke in Nagano), is said to have two tongues and hair growing backwards, or a mouth and nose like a cow and a shaggy body.

claims.quote: 小学館のデジタル大辞泉は「けっかい」について「猿の一種、ロリスの俗称。江戸時代、見世物にされた。」としている。

statement.id: Kamus Digital Daijisen terbitan Shōgakukan menjelaskan "kekkai" sebagai nama populer untuk sejenis monyet, yaitu loris, yang pada zaman Edo dipertontonkan.
statement.en: The Digital Daijisen dictionary by Shōgakukan glosses "kekkai" as a popular name for the loris, a kind of monkey, which was exhibited as a spectacle in the Edo period.

topic.en: What the exhibited kekkai really was

summary.id: Pertunjukan menyebutnya dilahirkan seorang perempuan di rumah sakit universitas.
summary.en: The show stated that a woman gave birth to it at a university hospital.

summary.id: Hino kemudian meyakininya monyet malam yang dijinakkan; Digital Daijisen mencatat kekkai sebagai nama loris.
summary.en: Hino later believed it to be a trained night monkey; the Digital Daijisen records kekkai as a name for the loris.

short_description.id: Satyrus adalah kera legendaris dari bestiarium abad pertengahan yang selalu melahirkan kembar, dan pernah dimuat Linnaeus dalam Systema Naturae.
short_description.en: The satyrus is a legendary ape of medieval bestiaries that always bears twins, once included by Linnaeus in his Systema Naturae.

long_description.id: Satyrus adalah jenis kera dalam beberapa bestiarium abad pertengahan, lincah dan berwajah menyenangkan, yang selalu melahirkan anak kembar dan membenci salah satunya sementara menyayangi yang lain. Ia dimuat dalam edisi awal Systema Naturae karya Carl Linnaeus di bawah Animalia Paradoxa, dan Linnaeus menyebutnya berbulu, berjanggut, bertubuh mirip manusia, serta sejenis monyet bila memang pernah terlihat.
long_description.en: The satyrus is a kind of ape in some medieval bestiaries, lively and pleasant-faced, that always bears twins and hates one while loving the other. It appeared in early editions of Carl Linnaeus's Systema Naturae under Animalia Paradoxa, where Linnaeus called it hairy, bearded, manlike in body and a kind of monkey if ever one was seen.

long_description.id: Satyrus biasanya digambarkan sebagai sejenis kera, tetapi dalam ilustrasi lebih mirip manusia liar yang sering membawa gada. Kadang ia disebut salah satu ras manusia ajaib dari timur atau Ethiopia, dan sosok ini tidak banyak mirip dengan Satyr tradisional Romawi.
long_description.en: The satyrus is usually described as a kind of ape but in illustrations looks more like a club-carrying wild man. It is sometimes counted among the monstrous human races of the east or Ethiopia, and it bears little resemblance to the traditional Roman Satyr.

statement.en: The satyrus was among the folklore creatures in early editions of Carl Linnaeus's Systema Naturae, under the catch-all Animalia Paradoxa.

claims.quote: Linnaeus is quoted as saying that the satyrus is "hairy, bearded, with a manlike body, gesticulating much, very fallacious, is a species of monkey, if ever one has been seen."

statement.id: Linnaeus menyebut satyrus berbulu, berjanggut, bertubuh mirip manusia, banyak bergerak, sangat menipu, dan sejenis monyet bila memang pernah terlihat.
statement.en: Linnaeus described the satyrus as hairy, bearded, manlike in body, much gesticulating, very deceptive, and a kind of monkey if ever one was seen.

claims.quote: The satyr is usually described as a type of ape, but is often pictured as a wild man.

statement.en: The satyr is usually described as a kind of ape but is often pictured as a wild man.

claims.quote: They are usually shown as more man-like than ape-like, and often carry a club. They are sometimes said to be one of the monstrous human races that were thought to live in the east or in Ethiopia.

statement.en: In illustrations they look more human than ape and often carry a club; they are sometimes said to be one of the monstrous human races thought to live in the east or in Ethiopia.

claims.quote: The ape-satyr is not much like the traditional Roman Satyr.

statement.id: Satyrus-kera ini tidak banyak mirip dengan Satyr tradisional Romawi (Roman).

short_description.id: Seere adalah pangeran dalam Goetia yang tampil sebagai pria rupawan menunggang kuda bersayap dan dapat melintasi seluruh bumi dalam sekejap.
short_description.en: Seere is a prince in the Goetia who appears as a beautiful man on a winged horse and can cross the whole Earth in an instant.

long_description.id: Seere adalah roh ke-70 dalam Goetia, bergelar pangeran yang perkasa dan memimpin 26 legiun roh. Satu catatan menempatkannya di bawah Amaymon, Raja Timur.
long_description.en: Seere is the seventieth spirit in the Goetia, ranked as a mighty prince governing 26 legions of spirits. One account places him under Amaymon, King of the East.

long_description.id: Ia tampil sebagai pria rupawan menunggang kuda bersayap. Tugasnya pergi dan datang, mewujudkan banyak hal dengan tiba-tiba, dan membawa apa pun ke mana dikehendaki; ia dapat melintasi seluruh bumi dalam sekejap mata.
long_description.en: He appears as a beautiful man riding a winged horse. His office is to go and come, bring many things to pass suddenly, and carry anything wherever desired; he can cross the entire Earth in the blink of an eye.

long_description.id: Ia memberi laporan benar tentang pencurian dan harta tersembunyi, dan teks Goetia menyebutnya berwatak cenderung baik serta bersedia melakukan apa pun yang diinginkan sang pemanggil. Wikipedia menyebutnya bukan iblis jahat melainkan berwatak baik dan acuh pada kejahatan.
long_description.en: He gives a true account of theft and hidden treasure, and the Goetia text calls him of an indifferent good nature, willing to do anything the Exorcist desires. Wikipedia says he is not a demon of evil but of good nature, indifferent to evilness.

short_description.id: Seiryū Gongen adalah dewi penjaga Daigo-ji di Kyoto.
short_description.en: Seiryū Gongen is the guardian goddess of Kyoto’s Daigo-ji.

long_description.id: Seiryū Gongen adalah dewi penjaga Daigo-ji di Kyoto. Tradisi mengidentifikasikannya dengan Zennyo Ryūō dan putri raja naga Sāgara.
long_description.en: Seiryū Gongen is the guardian goddess of Kyoto’s Daigo-ji. Tradition identifies her with Zennyo Ryūō and a daughter of the dragon king Sāgara.

long_description.id: Kisah membawanya ke Jepang dengan kapal Kūkai untuk melindungi Buddhisme esoteris. Nama tertulisnya yang terkait air dijelaskan melalui penyeberangan laut itu.
long_description.en: The story brings her to Japan on Kūkai’s ship to protect esoteric Buddhism. Her water-associated written name is explained through that crossing of the sea.

long_description.id: Sebuah kamus biografi menggambarkannya sebagai dewi naga pelindung agama Buddha, putri ketiga raja naga Shakara, yang pemujaannya bermula ketika Kūkai mengundang dewa pelindung kuil Seiryū-ji di Chang'an ke Jepang. Ia dimohon dalam ritual meminta hujan dan juga disebut Seiryō Daimyōjin.
long_description.en: A biographical dictionary describes her as a female dragon deity guarding Buddhism, the third daughter of the dragon king Shakara, whose worship began when Kūkai invited the tutelary deity of Seiryū-ji in Chang'an to Japan. She is prayed to in rain rituals and is also called Seiryō Daimyōjin.

statement.id: Tradisi mengidentifikasikannya dengan Zennyo Ryūō dan putri raja naga Sāgara.
statement.en: Tradition identifies her with Zennyo Ryūō and a daughter of the dragon king Sāgara.

claims.quote: 後年、弘法大師空海が青龍寺を訪れ仏法を学んだ際、三昧耶戒を授けてほしいと空海に懇請したが許されなかった。空海が帰国する際に船中に現れて密教を守護することを誓ったため、京都洛西の高雄山麓に勧請された。

statement.id: Kisah membawanya ke Jepang dengan kapal Kūkai untuk melindungi Buddhisme esoteris.
statement.en: The story brings her to Japan on Kūkai’s ship to protect esoteric Buddhism.

claims.quote: その際、海を渡ったので龍の字に「さんずい」を加えて日本では「清瀧権現」と敬称するようになった。

statement.id: Nama tertulisnya yang terkait air dijelaskan melalui penyeberangan laut itu.
statement.en: Her water-associated written name is explained through that crossing of the sea.

claims.quote: 仏教の守護神。 娑竭羅(しゃから)竜王の3女にあたる女体の竜神。空海によって唐(中国)長安の青竜寺の鎮守神が日本に勧請(かんじょう)されたのがはじまり。

statement.id: Kamus biografi Kodansha menyebut Seiryū Gongen dewa pelindung agama Buddha, dewi naga putri ketiga raja naga Shakara (娑竭羅); pemujaannya bermula ketika Kūkai (空海) mengundang dewa pelindung kuil Seiryū-ji di Chang'an (長安), Tiongkok (唐), ke Jepang.
statement.en: The Kodansha biographical dictionary calls Seiryū Gongen a guardian deity of Buddhism, a female dragon deity who is the third daughter of the dragon king Shakara (娑竭羅); her worship began when Kūkai (空海) invited the tutelary deity of Seiryū-ji in Chang'an (長安), China (唐), to Japan.

claims.quote: 雨ごいをおこなう場合はこの竜神にいのる。清滝(せいりょう)大明神ともいわれる。

statement.en: This dragon deity is prayed to when rain rituals are held, and she is also called Seiryō Daimyōjin (清滝大明神).

short_description.id: Serpente regolo adalah ular besar berkepala sebesar kepala anak dalam tradisi Toskana dan Umbria, yang namanya berarti "raja kecil".
short_description.en: The serpente regolo is a big serpent with a child-sized head in Tuscan and Umbrian tradition, its name meaning "little king".

long_description.id: Regolo adalah hewan ajaib dalam tradisi Toskana, Umbria, Abruzzo, Lazio, dan Marche: ular besar berkepala sebesar kepala anak kecil yang hidup di semak, ladang, dan jurang pegunungan. Namanya berarti "raja kecil" karena termasuk tradisi basilisk di Mediterania.
long_description.en: The regolo is a fantastic animal of Tuscan, Umbrian, Abruzzese, Lazian and Marchigian tradition: a big serpent with a head as large as a child's, living in thickets, fields and mountain gorges. Its name means "little king", as it belongs to the Mediterranean basilisk tradition.

long_description.id: Kesaksian tentang dewa bernama Serpente Regolo konon berasal dari zaman Romawi, dan Dio Cassius serta Plinius Tua menceritakan pertemuan pasukan Atilius Regulus dengan reptil raksasa di Afrika pada Perang Punik Pertama.
long_description.en: Testimonies of a deity called Serpente Regolo supposedly go back to Roman times, and Cassius Dio and Pliny the Elder told of Atilius Regulus's army meeting a huge reptile in Africa during the First Punic War.

long_description.id: Di Toscana regolo dibayangkan sebagai reptil besar bersisik berkilau seperti logam dengan dua sayap kecil, dan menurut tradisi daerah ia lahir dari telur ayam jantan tua yang dierami katak, kodok, atau ular di atas tumpukan pupuk. Salah satu dari sedikit penggambarannya yang asli terdapat di Pieve di Corsignano dekat Pienza.
long_description.en: In Toscana the regolo is pictured as a large reptile with metallic shining scales and two small wings, and regional traditions have it hatch from an old cockerel's egg brooded by a toad, frog or snake on a dung heap. One of its few original depictions is at the Pieve di Corsignano near Pienza.

statement.id: Penulis seperti Dio Cassius dan Plinius Tua menceritakan pertemuan pasukan Atilius Regulus dengan reptil raksasa di Afrika dekat Sungai Bagrada pada Perang Punik Pertama.
statement.en: Writers such as Cassius Dio and Pliny the Elder described the encounter of Atilius Regulus's army with a huge reptile in Africa by the Bagrada river during the First Punic War.

claims.quote: si ritrova in varie versioni in Umbria, Lazio, Marche e ovviamente Toscana, dove la tradizione lo vuole come un grosso rettile con squame luminose come di metallo e con due piccole ali.

statement.id: Legenda ini ditemukan dalam berbagai versi di Umbria, Lazio, Marche, dan Toscana; di Toscana tradisi menggambarkannya sebagai reptil besar bersisik berkilau seperti logam dengan dua sayap kecil.
statement.en: The legend appears in various versions in Umbria, Lazio, Marche and Toscana, where tradition pictures it as a large reptile with scales shining like metal and two small wings.

claims.quote: all’epoca della costruzione della Pieve di Corsignano di Pienza, dove troviamo una delle poche rappresentazioni del serpente Regolo arrivate “originali” fino a noi.

statement.en: According to regional traditions, the regolo is born from the egg of a seven- or fourteen-year-old cockerel, laid on a dung heap and hatched by a toad, a frog or a snake.

short_description.id: Shen adalah monster laut Tiongkok yang dapat berubah wujud, berupa naga atau kerang, dan dipercaya menciptakan fatamorgana.
short_description.en: Shen is a shapeshifting Chinese sea monster taking dragon or shellfish forms, believed to create mirages.

long_description.id: Shen adalah monster laut Tiongkok yang dapat berubah wujud, berupa naga atau kerang. Makhluk ini dipercaya menciptakan fatamorgana. Teks Shiji menyebut uap 蜄 di tepi laut menyerupai menara dan panggung.
long_description.en: Shen is a shapeshifting Chinese sea monster taking dragon or shellfish forms. This creature is believed to create mirages. The Shiji text says the vapour of the 蜄 beside the sea resembles towers and terraces.

long_description.id: Dalam teks klasik, shen juga berarti kerang besar yang dikaitkan dengan pemakaman. Erya menjelaskan shen sebagai kerang yao yang besar. Eberhard mencatat ketidakpastian alasan kerang itu ditempatkan dalam makam. Shuowen Jiezi mendefinisikan 蜃 sebagai hasil perubahan pegar yang masuk laut.
long_description.en: In classical texts, shen also denotes large shellfish associated with funerals. The Erya explains shen as a large yao shellfish. Eberhard notes uncertainty about why those shellfish were placed in tombs. The Shuowen Jiezi defines 蜃 as what a pheasant becomes on entering the sea.

long_description.id: Menurut seorang pakar yang dikutip artikel, pada awal abad pertengahan shen menjadi monster yang bersembunyi di gua bawah laut dan kadang dilengkapi sifat naga, dan embusannya tampak bagi pelaut sebagai istana yang melayang di laut. Compendium of Materia Medica (1596) menguraikannya sebagai sejenis buaya berbentuk ular besar yang hidup dari burung layang-layang, menyemburkan uap, dan muncul saat akan hujan.
long_description.en: According to a scholar quoted in the article, by early medieval times the shen had become a monster lurking in submarine grottoes, sometimes with dragon attributes, whose exhalations appeared to mariners as mansions adrift on the sea. The Compendium of Materia Medica (1596) describes it as a kind of crocodile shaped like a huge serpent that lives on swallows, spurts vapour, and appears when rain is coming.

description.id: Shen adalah naga atau monster kerang yang dapat berubah wujud; Shuowen Jiezi menyebut pegar yang masuk laut menjadi 蜃.
description.en: The shen is a shapeshifting dragon or shellfish monster; the Shuowen Jiezi says a pheasant entering the sea becomes a 蜃.
