description.en: The shen is believed to create mirages; the Shiji text says the vapour of the 蜄 beside the sea resembles towers and terraces, and its exhalations appear to mariners as mansions adrift on the sea.

description.id: Menurut kutipan Compendium of Materia Medica, ia menyemburkan awan uap dalam lingkaran besar dan muncul saat akan hujan.
description.en: According to the quoted Compendium of Materia Medica passage, it spurts clouds of vapour in huge rings and appears when rain is coming.

claims.quote: In Chinese mythology, the shen or chen (Chinese: 蜃; pinyin: shèn/chèn; Wade–Giles: shen/ch'en; lit. 'large clam') is a shapeshifting dragon or shellfish-type sea monster believed to create mirages.

statement.id: Shen adalah monster laut Tiongkok yang dapat berubah wujud, berupa naga atau kerang.
statement.en: Shen is a shapeshifting Chinese sea monster taking dragon or shellfish forms.

claims.quote: In Chinese mythology, the shen or chen (Chinese: 蜃; pinyin: shèn/chèn; Wade–Giles: shen/ch'en; lit. 'large clam') is a shapeshifting dragon or shellfish-type sea monster believed to create mirages.

statement.id: Makhluk ini dipercaya menciptakan fatamorgana.
statement.en: This creature is believed to create mirages.

claims.quote: The Chinese classics use the word shèn to mean "a large shellfish" that was associated with funerals and "an aquatic monster" that could change its shape, which was later associated with "mirages".

statement.id: Dalam teks klasik, shen juga berarti kerang besar yang dikaitkan dengan pemakaman.
statement.en: In classical texts, shen also denotes large shellfish associated with funerals.

claims.quote: The word used to mean a shellfish, or mollusk, identified as an oyster, mussel, or giant clam such as the Pearl of Lao Tzu. While early Chinese dictionaries treat shèn as a general term for "mollusca", the Erya defines it as a large yáo (珧) "shellfish", "clam", "scallop", or "nacre".

statement.id: Erya menjelaskan shen sebagai kerang yao yang besar.
statement.en: The Erya explains shen as a large yao shellfish.

claims.quote: "It is not clear why these mussels were placed into the tombs," he admits

statement.id: Eberhard mencatat ketidakpastian alasan kerang itu ditempatkan dalam makam.
statement.en: Eberhard notes uncertainty about why those shellfish were placed in tombs.

claims.quote: 金寶之上，皆有氣，不可不察。海旁蜄氣象樓臺；廣野氣成宮闕然。雲氣各象其山川人民所聚積。

statement.id: Teks Shiji menyebut bahwa uap (氣) dari 蜄 di tepi laut menyerupai menara dan panggung, sedangkan uap di padang luas membentuk istana dan gerbang; uap-uap itu masing-masing menyerupai gunung, sungai, dan tempat berkumpulnya manusia.
statement.en: The Shiji text says the vapour (氣) of the 蜄 beside the sea resembles towers and terraces, while the vapour over broad plains forms palaces and gates; each vapour resembles the mountains, rivers and gatherings of people.

claims.quote: 蜃：雉入海，化爲蜃。从虫辰聲。 𧊧：蜃屬。有三，皆生於海。千歲化爲𧊧，秦謂之牡厲。又云百歲燕所化。魁𧊧，一名復累，老服翼所化。

statement.id: Kamus Shuowen Jiezi mendefinisikan 蜃: burung pegar masuk ke laut dan berubah menjadi 蜃; jenis-jenis 蜃 ada tiga, semuanya lahir di laut, dan terbentuk dari perubahan makhluk lain seperti burung layang-layang dan kelelawar tua.
statement.en: The Shuowen Jiezi dictionary defines 蜃: a pheasant enters the sea and transforms into a 蜃; the 蜃 kind has three types, all born in the sea, formed by the transformation of other creatures such as swallows and old bats.

claims.quote: Finally, by early medieval times, it had become a monster lurking in submarine grottoes, and was sometimes endowed with the attributes of a dragon – or, more likely, under Indian influence, a nāga. It expressed its artistic nature by belching up bubbles and frothy clots.

statement.id: Seorang pakar yang dikutip artikel ini menyatakan bahwa pada awal abad pertengahan shen menjadi monster yang bersembunyi di gua bawah laut, kadang dilengkapi sifat naga atau nāga, dan mengeluarkan gelembung dan gumpalan berbusa.
statement.en: A scholar quoted in the article says that by early medieval times the shen had become a monster lurking in submarine grottoes, sometimes endowed with dragon or nāga attributes, belching up bubbles and frothy clots.

claims.quote: The plastic exhalations of the clam-monster sometimes burst the film of surface tension and appeared to astonished mariners as stunning mansions adrift on the surface of the deep.

statement.id: Seorang pakar yang dikutip artikel ini menyatakan bahwa embusan lentur sang monster kerang kadang memecah selaput permukaan dan tampak bagi pelaut yang terkejut sebagai istana megah yang melayang di permukaan laut.
statement.en: A scholar quoted in the article states that the clam-monster's plastic exhalations sometimes burst the surface film and appeared to astonished mariners as stunning mansions adrift on the deep.

claims.quote: The 1596 Compendium of Materia Medica describes the shèn under the jiaolong entry with quotes from the Yueling and Lu Dian's Piya. ... A kind of crocodile shaped like a huge serpent. Horned like a dragon, with a red mane. Below the middle of the back it has scales inversely arranged. It lives on swallows. It spurts forth clouds of vapour in huge rings. It appears when it is going to rain.

statement.id: Menurut artikel ini, Compendium of Materia Medica (1596) menguraikan shen dalam entri jiaolong dengan kutipan: sejenis buaya berbentuk ular besar, bertanduk seperti naga, bersurai merah, bersisik terbalik di bawah tengah punggung, hidup dari burung layang-layang, menyemburkan awan uap dalam lingkaran besar, dan muncul saat akan hujan.
statement.en: According to the article, the 1596 Compendium of Materia Medica describes the shen under the jiaolong entry with a quote: a kind of crocodile shaped like a huge serpent, horned like a dragon with a red mane, scales inversely arranged below mid-back, living on swallows, spurting clouds of vapour in huge rings, and appearing when rain is coming.

claims.quote: According to Chinese folklore, swallows are a favorite food of both lóng 龍 and shèn 蜃 dragons.

statement.id: Menurut artikel ini, dalam cerita rakyat Tiongkok burung layang-layang adalah makanan kesukaan naga long (龍) dan naga shen (蜃).
statement.en: According to the article, in Chinese folklore swallows are a favorite food of both long (龍) and shen (蜃) dragons.

short_description.id: Shibaemon-tanuki adalah bake-danuki dari Pulau Awaji yang dihitung sebagai salah satu dari tiga tanuki terkenal Jepang; ia menyamar sebagai manusia, usil sekaligus suka menolong, dan akhirnya dipuja sebagai dewa.
short_description.en: Shibaemon-tanuki is a bake-danuki of Awaji Island counted among Japan's three famous tanuki; he disguises himself as a human, is both mischievous and kind, and came to be worshipped as a god.

long_description.id: Shibaemon-tanuki adalah tanuki gaib dari Pulau Awaji. Ia dihitung sebagai salah satu dari tiga tanuki terkenal Jepang. Kumpulan cerita bergambar zaman Edo mencatat sosoknya, dan konon ia tinggal di puncak Gunung Mikuma di belakang Kota Sumoto bersama istrinya, Omasu, serta menabuh perutnya pada malam berbulan yang cerah.
long_description.en: Shibaemon-tanuki is a supernatural tanuki from Awaji Island. He is counted among Japan's three famous tanuki. An Edo-period illustrated tale collection records him, and he is said to have lived at the summit of Mt. Mikuma behind the city of Sumoto with his wife Omasu, drumming his belly on fine moonlit nights.

long_description.id: Cerita-ceritanya memadukan tipuan, seperti menyamar sebagai manusia dan membuat daun tampak seperti emas, dengan bantuan bagi pelancong yang tersesat; orang yang pernah ditolongnya mempersembahkan sake. Ia pergi ke Osaka untuk menonton pertunjukan Nakaza dan di sana diserang anjing ketika menyamar sebagai manusia; ia kembali ke wujud tanuki dan dipukul hingga tewas. Rincian kisahnya berbeda menurut daerah dan sumber.
long_description.en: His stories combine tricks, such as disguising himself as a human and making leaves seem like gold, with help for lost travelers, and people he had helped made offerings of sake. He went to Osaka to see the Nakaza play and there was attacked by a dog while disguised as a human; he returned to his tanuki form and was hit and killed. The details of the tale differ by region and source.

long_description.id: Setelah ia mati, penonton Nakaza berkurang dan beredar kabar bahwa itu kutukan; ketika teater mendewakannya, penonton kembali dan banyak aktor memujanya. Kuilnya kini berada di dekat reruntuhan kastil Sumoto di puncak Gunung Mikuma, dan Shibaemon Daimyōjin yang didewakan di Nakaza kini dipuja di Kuil Hachiman Sumoto.
long_description.en: After his death, audiences at Nakaza fell and a rumor of a curse spread; when the theater deified him, audiences returned and many actors worshipped him. His shrine today sits close to Sumoto's castle ruins on the summit of Mt. Mikuma, and the Shibaemon Daimyōjin deified at Nakaza is now enshrined at Sumoto Hachiman Shrine.

long_description.id: Di Sumoto, patung-patung tanuki terinspirasi dari Shibaemon, dan "Sumoto Eight Tanuki Story" adalah rute wisata dengan delapan patung berdasarkan legendanya.
long_description.en: In Sumoto, tanuki statues are inspired by Shibaemon, and the "Sumoto Eight Tanuki Story" is a sightseeing route of eight statues based on his legends.

claims.quote: Shibaemon-tanuki, or Shibaemon-danuki (芝右衛門狸 or 柴右衛門狸) is a bake-danuki told in the legends of Awaji island, Hyōgo Prefecture.

statement.id: Shibaemon-tanuki adalah tanuki gaib dari Pulau Awaji.
statement.en: Shibaemon-tanuki is a supernatural tanuki from Awaji Island.

claims.quote: Along with Danzaburou-danuki of Sado island and the Yashima no Hage-tanuki of Kagawa Prefecture, he is counted among the "three famous tanuki of Japan." He is also written about in the colorful stories collection of the Edo period, the Ehon Hyaku Monogatari.

statement.id: Ia dihitung sebagai salah satu dari tiga tanuki terkenal Jepang.
statement.en: He is counted among Japan’s three famous tanuki.

claims.quote: Along with Danzaburou-danuki of Sado island and the Yashima no Hage-tanuki of Kagawa Prefecture, he is counted among the "three famous tanuki of Japan." He is also written about in the colorful stories collection of the Edo period, the Ehon Hyaku Monogatari.

statement.id: Kumpulan cerita bergambar zaman Edo mencatat sosoknya.
statement.en: An Edo-period illustrated tale collection records him.

claims.quote: While disguised as a human and in the middle of performing an act, he was attacked by a dog and killed, but the details of the tale differ depending on region and literature.

statement.id: Satu cerita menggambarkan anjing membunuhnya ketika ia menyamar sebagai manusia.
statement.en: A tale describes a dog killing him while he is disguised as a human.

claims.quote: Mikuma (三熊山) behind the city of Sumoto, Awaji island, he lived with his wife Omasu (お増) and on moonlight nights with good weather, he drummed his belly.

statement.id: Satu kisah menyebut istrinya bernama Omasu.
statement.en: One account names his wife Omasu.

claims.quote: He performed mischief such as disguising himself as a human and making tree leaves seem like gold and sell them, but at the same time he did kind deeds such as guiding along humans who stumbled into the mountain while drunk, so nobody hated him.

statement.id: Cerita-ceritanya memadukan tipuan dengan bantuan bagi pelancong yang tersesat.
statement.en: His stories combine deceptive tricks with help for lost travelers.

claims.quote: While Shibaemon-tanuki was at the summit of Mt. Mikuma (三熊山) behind the city of Sumoto, Awaji island, he lived with his wife Omasu (お増) and on moonlight nights with good weather, he drummed his belly.
claims.locator: Section: Legend in the Hyōgo prefecture

statement.id: Shibaemon-tanuki tinggal di puncak Gunung Mikuma di belakang Kota Sumoto, Pulau Awaji, bersama istrinya Omasu, dan pada malam berbulan yang cerah ia menabuh perutnya.
statement.en: Shibaemon-tanuki lived at the summit of Mt. Mikuma behind the city of Sumoto on Awaji island with his wife Omasu, and on fine moonlit nights he drummed his belly.

claims.quote: The people he has been kind to made offerings of 1 sho bottles of sake to where he dwelled.
claims.locator: Section: Legend in the Hyōgo prefecture

statement.id: Orang-orang yang pernah ditolongnya mempersembahkan botol sake satu sho ke tempat tinggalnya.
statement.en: The people he had been kind to made offerings of one-shō bottles of sake at the place where he dwelled.

claims.quote: One time, Shibaemon heard that there was a very popular play called Nakaza that was being performed in Naniwa (now Osaka city) and disguised himself and Omasu both as humans to Osaka.
claims.locator: Section: Legend in the Hyōgo prefecture

statement.id: Suatu kali Shibaemon mendengar ada pertunjukan sangat populer bernama Nakaza di Naniwa (kini Kota Osaka), lalu ia dan Omasu menyamar sebagai manusia pergi ke Osaka.
statement.en: One time Shibaemon heard of a very popular play called Nakaza being performed in Naniwa (now Osaka city), and he and Omasu disguised themselves as humans and went to Osaka.

claims.quote: Shibaemon, who was stricken with grief, was about to return to Awaji, but decided to at least watch the play that Omasu wanted to see and used a technique to change tree leaves into gold and went to the theater.
claims.locator: Section: Legend in the Hyōgo prefecture

statement.id: Shibaemon yang berduka hendak kembali ke Awaji, tetapi memutuskan menonton pertunjukan yang diinginkan Omasu dan memakai teknik mengubah daun pohon menjadi emas lalu pergi ke teater.
statement.en: Stricken with grief, Shibaemon was about to return to Awaji but decided to watch the play Omasu had wanted to see, and used a technique to change tree leaves into gold to go to the theater.

claims.quote: However, at the theater, there were tree leaves that were mixed in with the admission fees, so they suspected that a bake-danuki has slipped in among the guests and a guard dog was put on alert.
claims.locator: Section: Legend in the Hyōgo prefecture

statement.id: Namun di teater ditemukan daun pohon bercampur dalam uang karcis, sehingga orang curiga ada bake-danuki menyelinap di antara penonton dan seekor anjing penjaga disiagakan.
statement.en: At the theater, tree leaves were found mixed in with the admission fees, so people suspected a bake-danuki had slipped in among the guests and a guard dog was put on alert.

claims.quote: Shibaemon hid his fear and passed through the entrance, but within a gap of his confidence, the dog rushed to attack. Shibaemon immediately returned to his appearance as a tanuki, was chased around by the people who brought the dog and finally hit in the head and killed.
claims.locator: Section: Legend in the Hyōgo prefecture

statement.id: Shibaemon menyembunyikan rasa takutnya dan melewati pintu masuk, tetapi saat kepercayaan dirinya lengah, anjing itu menerjang; ia segera kembali ke wujud tanuki, dikejar orang-orang yang membawa anjing, dan akhirnya dipukul di kepala hingga tewas.
statement.en: Shibaemon hid his fear and passed through the entrance, but when his confidence slipped the dog rushed to attack; he immediately returned to his tanuki form, was chased by the people with the dog and finally hit on the head and killed.

claims.quote: After Shibaemon's death, the people who came to see Nakaza decreased and there was a rumor that "it was a curse from having killed Shibaemon," so when the theater deified Shibaemon, the number of guests returned.
claims.locator: Section: Legend in the Hyōgo prefecture

statement.id: Setelah Shibaemon mati, penonton Nakaza berkurang dan beredar kabar bahwa itu kutukan karena membunuhnya; ketika teater itu mendewakan Shibaemon, jumlah penonton kembali.
statement.en: After Shibaemon's death, audiences at Nakaza fell and a rumor spread that it was a curse for having killed him; when the theater deified Shibaemon, the number of guests returned.

claims.quote: Afterwards, Shibaemon, as a popular god, was deeply worshipped by many actors such as Nakamura Ganjirou, Kataoka Nizaemon and Fujiyama Kanbi.
claims.locator: Section: Legend in the Hyōgo prefecture

statement.id: Kemudian Shibaemon, sebagai dewa yang populer, dipuja dengan sungguh-sungguh oleh banyak aktor seperti Nakamura Ganjirou, Kataoka Nizaemon, dan Fujiyama Kanbi.
statement.en: Afterwards Shibaemon, as a popular god, was deeply worshipped by many actors such as Nakamura Ganjirou, Kataoka Nizaemon and Fujiyama Kanbi.

claims.quote: Now, the Shrine of Shibaemon is near the castle ruins of Sumoto at the peak of Mt. Mikuma and due to the legend of Shibaemon, who liked theater, there are many performers who visit the shrine even now.
claims.locator: Section: Legend in the Hyōgo prefecture

statement.id: Kini kuil Shibaemon berada di dekat reruntuhan kastil Sumoto di puncak Gunung Mikuma, dan karena legenda Shibaemon yang menyukai teater, banyak pemain pertunjukan masih mengunjungi kuil itu.
statement.en: The Shrine of Shibaemon now stands near the castle ruins of Sumoto at the peak of Mt. Mikuma, and because of the legend of Shibaemon, who liked theater, many performers still visit it.

claims.quote: The Shibaemon Daimyoujin (柴右衛門大明神) that was deified in Nakaza also had a "return home" in the year 2000 and is now deified in the Sumoto Hachiman-jinja.
claims.locator: Section: Legend in the Hyōgo prefecture

statement.id: Shibaemon Daimyoujin yang didewakan di Nakaza juga "pulang kampung" pada tahun 2000 dan kini dipuja di Sumoto Hachiman-jinja.
statement.en: The Shibaemon Daimyoujin deified in Nakaza also had a "return home" in the year 2000 and is now deified in the Sumoto Hachiman-jinja.

claims.quote: The next morning, when the government officials visited to inspect again, the soldier's appearance turned into a bloodstained tanuki. It was Shibaemon-tanuki.
claims.locator: Section: Legend in the Tokushima prefecture

statement.id: Dalam satu legenda, keesokan paginya wujud prajurit itu berubah menjadi tanuki berlumuran darah, dan itu adalah Shibaemon-tanuki.
statement.en: In one legend, the next morning the soldier turned into a bloodstained tanuki, and it was Shibaemon-tanuki.

claims.quote: In the past, in Awaji, there was a peasant called Shibaemon, and an old tanuki came to him and requested for food scraps, and feeling pity, he expressly left some food for the tanuki.

statement.id: Dalam satu versi, di Awaji dahulu ada seorang petani bernama Shibaemon, dan seekor tanuki tua datang meminta sisa makanan; karena kasihan, ia sengaja menyisakan makanan untuknya.
statement.en: In one version, there was once a peasant called Shibaemon on Awaji, and an old tanuki came to ask for food scraps; feeling pity, he deliberately left some food for the tanuki.

claims.quote: There are theories that reality of the legend of Shibaemon-tanuki is that it was an excuse for the Kougo Jihen, a struggle that broke out between Sumoto and Awa

statement.id: Ada teori bahwa kenyataan di balik legenda Shibaemon-tanuki adalah dalih bagi Kougo Jihen, pergolakan antara Sumoto dan Awa.
statement.en: There are theories that the reality behind the legend of Shibaemon-tanuki was an excuse for the Kougo Jihen, a struggle that broke out between Sumoto and Awa.

claims.quote: In the Edo period, at the base of Mount Seimi (勢見山) in Awa Province (now Tokushima prefecture), there was a theater business at the grounds of Kan'on-ji, and it earned great popularity.
claims.locator: Section: Legend in the Tokushima prefecture

statement.id: Pada zaman Edo, di kaki Gunung Seimi di Provinsi Awa (kini Prefektur Tokushima), ada usaha teater di halaman Kuil Kan'on-ji yang sangat populer.
statement.en: In the Edo period, at the base of Mount Seimi in Awa Province (now Tokushima prefecture), there was a theater business at the grounds of Kan'on-ji that earned great popularity.

claims.quote: As you walk around Sumoto, you will come across charming tanuki statues in various places. These statues are inspired by Shibaemon, a tanuki who appears in a folk tale that has been passed down in Sumoto for generations.

statement.id: Patung-patung tanuki di berbagai tempat di Sumoto terinspirasi dari Shibaemon, tanuki dalam cerita rakyat yang diwariskan turun-temurun di Sumoto.
statement.en: Tanuki statues around Sumoto are inspired by Shibaemon, a tanuki in a folk tale passed down in Sumoto for generations.

claims.quote: The "Sumoto Eight Tanuki Story" is a sightseeing route featuring eight tanuki statues based on the legends of Shibaemon. Eight statues modeled on Shibaemon and his companions are located at various spots around the city. Each has its own name, blessing, and story.

statement.id: "Sumoto Eight Tanuki Story" adalah rute wisata dengan delapan patung tanuki berdasarkan legenda Shibaemon; tiap patung punya nama, berkat, dan kisahnya sendiri.
statement.en: The "Sumoto Eight Tanuki Story" is a sightseeing route with eight tanuki statues based on the legends of Shibaemon; each statue has its own name, blessing and story.

short_description.id: Shinchū adalah sosok menyerupai serangga dalam gulungan Hekija-e yang dipercaya mengusir bencana dan penyakit.
short_description.en: Shinchū is an insectlike figure in the Hekija-e scroll, believed to repel disasters and epidemics.

long_description.id: Shinchū adalah sosok menyerupai serangga dalam gulungan Hekija-e yang dipercaya mengusir bencana dan penyakit. Gulungan tersebut disimpan di Museum Nasional Nara. Ia digambarkan bertubuh seperti kumbang, berkaki delapan, dan menangkap sosok mirip oni.
long_description.en: Shinchū is an insectlike figure in the Hekija-e scroll, believed to repel disasters and epidemics. The scroll is held by the Nara National Museum. It is depicted with a beetlelike body and eight limbs, grasping an onilike figure.

long_description.id: Lukisan Hekija-e menghimpun dewa-dewa penolak kejahatan yang di Tiongkok dipercaya menghukum dan mengusir roh wabah; Shinchū muncul bersama Tenkeisei, Sendan Kendatsuba, Shōki, dan Bishamonten. Polanya diduga berasal dari Tiongkok, tetapi wujud Shinchū hanya dikenal dari lukisan ini, dan warna tubuhnya yang berat dinilai khas. Karya itu diperkirakan dibuat antara akhir zaman Heian dan awal zaman Kamakura.
long_description.en: The Hekija-e brings together evil-repelling deities believed in China to punish and expel plague demons; Shinchū appears alongside Tenkeisei, Sendan Kendatsuba, Shōki and Bishamonten. The designs are thought to derive from China, yet Shinchū's image is known only from this painting, and the heavy colouring of its body is considered distinctive. The work is dated to between the end of the Heian period and the start of the Kamakura period.

did_you_know.id: Shinchū dalam Hekija-e abad ke-12, sebuah Harta Nasional, disebut sebagai contoh paling jelas serangga yang diperbesar menjadi monster.
did_you_know.en: Shinchū in the 12th-century Hekija-e, a National Treasure, has been cited as the clearest example of an insect enlarged into a monster.

statement.id: Gulungan itu menghimpun dewa penolak kejahatan (hekija-shin) yang di Tiongkok (中国) dipercaya menghukum dan mengusir roh wabah; Shinchū (神虫) termasuk di antaranya bersama Tenkeisei, Sendan Kendatsuba, Shōki, dan Bishamonten, yang melukai atau memakan roh-roh wabah.
statement.en: The scroll gathers evil-repelling deities (hekija-shin) believed in China (中国) to punish and drive off plague demons; Shinchū (神虫) is among them alongside Tenkeisei, Sendan Kendatsuba, Shōki and Bishamonten, who wound or devour the plague demons.

claims.quote: 図様はいずれも中国から伝わったと考えられるが、天刑星と神虫は本図においてのみその像が知られるなど、内容は極めて特異性に富むといえよう。

statement.id: Pola gambarnya diduga berasal dari Tiongkok, tetapi wujud Tenkeisei dan Shinchū hanya dikenal dari lukisan ini.
statement.en: The designs are thought to have come from China, but the images of Tenkeisei and Shinchū are known only from this painting.

statement.id: Shinchū dalam lukisan Hekija-e (辟邪絵) abad ke-12, sebuah Harta Nasional (国宝), disebut contoh paling jelas dari serangga yang diperbesar menjadi monster.

short_description.id: Sukunabikona adalah kami Shinto bertubuh kecil, dewa onsen, pertanian, penyembuhan, sihir, pembuatan sake, dan pengetahuan, yang membantu Ōkuninushi membangun negeri.
short_description.en: Sukunabikona is a small-bodied Shinto kami of hot springs, agriculture, healing, magic, brewing sake and knowledge, who helped Ōkuninushi build the land.

long_description.id: Sukunabikona (少彦名神) adalah kami Shinto yang menguasai onsen, pertanian, penyembuhan, sihir, pembuatan sake, dan pengetahuan. Namanya berarti "tuan kecil yang termasyhur"; ia sering digambarkan sebagai kurcaci dan kerap dipasangkan dengan Ōkuninushi. Satu kisah bermula ketika Ōkuninushi melihat perahu kecil dari polong Metaplexis di Teluk Miho, dan di dalamnya ada kurcaci sebesar ibu jari.
long_description.en: Sukunabikona (少彦名神) is a Shinto kami whose domains include onsen, farming, healing, magic, sake brewing and knowledge. The name is glossed "the small lord of renown"; he is often pictured as a dwarf and often appears alongside Ōkuninushi. One tale begins when Ōkuninushi sees a small boat made of a Metaplexis pod at Miho Bay, with a dwarf no bigger than a thumb inside.

long_description.id: Dalam usaha membantu Ōkuninushi menyelesaikan pembangunan negeri, ia menciptakan obat dan penawar penyakit serta mantra pelindung, dan ia disebut ahli sihir. Ketika ia jatuh sakit, Ōkuninushi merendamnya di mata air panas dan ia terbangun dalam keadaan sembuh dan menari di atas batu. Beberapa sumber juga menganggapnya penemu sake yang mengajari orang membuatnya dari beras.
long_description.en: In helping Ōkuninushi complete the building of the land, he invented medicines, cures and protective spells, and he is called a master of magic. When he fell ill, Ōkuninushi put him in a hot spring and he awoke cured and danced on a stone. Some sources also credit him with inventing sake, teaching people to brew it from rice.

long_description.id: Menurut tradisi, ia meninggalkan dunia ini di Pulau Awaji dengan memanjat sebutir jawawut yang melentingkannya ke Tokoyo no Kuni, sehingga ia dikenal sebagai dewa pendatang yang datang dari seberang laut lalu pergi. Kamus Jepang menyebutnya anak 神産巣日神 dalam Kojiki dan anak 高皇産霊尊 dalam Nihon Shoki, serta dewa obat-obatan.
long_description.en: According to tradition he departed from Awaji Island by climbing a grain of millet that flung him away to Tokoyo no Kuni, so he is known as an immigrant deity who arrived from overseas and later left. A Japanese dictionary calls him a deity of medicine, a child of 神産巣日神 in the Kojiki and of 高皇産霊尊 in the Nihon Shoki.

short_description.id: Taotie adalah makhluk mitologis Tiongkok yang termasuk Empat Bahaya.
short_description.en: Taotie is a Chinese mythological creature counted among the Four Perils.

long_description.id: Taotie adalah makhluk mitologis Tiongkok yang termasuk Empat Bahaya. Motif pada bejana perunggu menampilkan topeng hewan simetris dengan mata menonjol.
long_description.en: Taotie is a Chinese mythological creature counted among the Four Perils. Bronze-vessel motifs depict a symmetrical animal mask with raised eyes.

long_description.id: Nama yang dipakai masyarakat Shang dan Zhou untuk motif tersebut tidak diketahui. Zuo Zhuan mengaitkan taotie dengan kerakusan: seorang anak tak berbakat dari keluarga Jinyun yang rakus makanan dan minuman disebut orang 饕餮, dan Shun kemudian mengusir empat kaum jahat, termasuk Taotie, ke tepi-tepi dunia. Kutipan Lüshi Chunqiu menggambarkan kepala tanpa tubuh pada perunggu Zhou.
long_description.en: The name used by Shang and Zhou people for the motif is unknown. The Zuo Zhuan associates taotie with gluttony: an untalented son of the Jinyun clan who was greedy for food and drink was called 饕餮 by the people, and Shun later banished four evil clans, Taotie among them, to the frontiers. A quoted Lüshi Chunqiu passage describes a head without a body on Zhou bronzes.

long_description.id: Li Zehou menafsirkan motif taotie sebagai komunikasi misterius antara manusia dan langit. Lüshi Chunqiu sendiri menyebut bahwa taotie pada tripod Zhou belum menelan manusia yang dimakannya tetapi sudah mencelakai tubuhnya sendiri.
long_description.en: Li Zehou interprets taotie imagery as mysterious communication between people and heaven. The Lüshi Chunqiu itself says that the taotie on the Zhou tripod harms its own body before it has swallowed the people it eats.

note.id: Termasuk Empat Bahaya bersama Hundun, Qiongqi, dan Taowu.
note.en: Counted among the Four Perils together with Hundun, Qiongqi and Taowu.

note.id: Termasuk Empat Bahaya bersama Hundun, Qiongqi, dan Taowu.
note.en: Counted among the Four Perils together with Hundun, Qiongqi and Taowu.

claims.quote: The taotie is an ancient Chinese mythological creature that was commonly emblazoned on bronze and other artifacts during the 1st millennium BCE. Taotie are one of the Four Perils in Chinese classics like the Classic of Mountains and Seas, alongside the Hundun, Qiongqi, and Taowu.

statement.id: Taotie adalah makhluk mitologis Tiongkok yang termasuk Empat Bahaya.
statement.en: Taotie is a Chinese mythological creature counted among the Four Perils.

claims.quote: The Taotie is often represented as a motif on dings, which are Chinese ritual bronze vessels from the Shang (c. 1600 – c. 1050 BCE) and Zhou dynasties (c. 1046 – 256 BCE). The design typically consists of a zoomorphic mask, described as being frontal, bilaterally symmetrical, with a pair of raised eyes and typically no lower jaw area.

statement.id: Motif pada bejana perunggu menampilkan topeng hewan simetris dengan mata menonjol.
statement.en: Bronze-vessel motifs depict a symmetrical animal mask with raised eyes.

claims.quote: Although modern scholars use the word taotie, it is actually not known what word the Shang and Zhou dynasties used to call the design on their bronze vessels; as American paleographer Sarah Allan notes, there is no particular reason to assume that the term taotie was known during the Shang period.

statement.id: Nama yang dipakai masyarakat Shang dan Zhou untuk motif tersebut tidak diketahui.
statement.en: The name used by Shang and Zhou people for the motif is unknown.

claims.quote: Within the Zuo Zhuan, taotie is used by the writer to imply gluttony.

claims.quote: Li Zehou, a Chinese scholar of philosophy and intellectual history, thinks the description of the taotie in the Lüshi Chunqiu has a much deeper meaning, and that "the meaning of taotie is not [about] 'eating people' but making a mysterious communication between people and Heaven (gods)."

statement.id: Li Zehou menafsirkan motif taotie sebagai komunikasi misterius antara manusia dan langit.

claims.quote: 縉雲氏有不才子，貪于飲食，冒于貨賄，侵欲崇侈，不可盈厭，聚斂積實，不知紀極，不分孤寡，不恤窮匱，天下之民，以比三凶，謂之饕餮
claims.locator: Zuo Zhuan, Wen 18 (bagian Jiu Fu Shu)

statement.id: Zuo Zhuan (春秋左氏傳) menyebut seorang anak tak berbakat (不才子) dari keluarga Jinyun (縉雲氏) yang rakus makanan dan minuman (貪于飲食) serta tamak harta (冒于貨賄); orang-orang di dunia membandingkannya dengan tiga keburukan (三凶) dan menyebutnya 饕餮.
statement.en: The Zuo Zhuan (春秋左氏傳) tells of an untalented son (不才子) of the Jinyun clan (縉雲氏) who was greedy for food and drink (貪于飲食) and covetous of goods (冒于貨賄); the people of the world compared him with the three ills (三凶) and called him 饕餮 (taotie).

claims.quote: 舜臣堯，賓于四門，流四凶族，渾敦，窮奇，檮杌，饕餮，投諸四裔，以禦螭魅

statement.id: Zuo Zhuan menyebut bahwa Shun (舜), sebagai menteri Yao (堯), mengusir empat kaum jahat (四凶族): Hundun (渾敦), Qiongqi (窮奇), Taowu (檮杌), dan Taotie (饕餮), melemparkan mereka ke empat penjuru tepi (四裔) untuk menangkal 螭魅.
statement.en: The Zuo Zhuan says that Shun (舜), as minister to Yao (堯), banished the four evil clans (四凶族): Hundun (渾敦), Qiongqi (窮奇), Taowu (檮杌) and Taotie (饕餮), casting them to the four frontiers (四裔) to ward off 螭魅.

claims.quote: 周鼎著饕餮，有首無身，食人未咽，害及其身，以言報更也。為不善亦然。

statement.id: Lüshi Chunqiu (呂氏春秋) menyebut bahwa pada tripod Zhou (周鼎) terukir (著) taotie (饕餮) yang berkepala tetapi tak bertubuh (有首無身); ia belum menelan manusia yang dimakannya (食人未咽) tetapi sudah mencelakai tubuhnya sendiri (害及其身). Kalimat berikutnya: berbuat tidak baik pun demikian (為不善亦然).
statement.en: The Lüshi Chunqiu (呂氏春秋) says that the Zhou tripod (周鼎) bears (著) a taotie (饕餮) with a head but no body (有首無身); before it has swallowed the people it eats (食人未咽) harm has reached its own body (害及其身). The next sentence says that doing wrong is likewise (為不善亦然).

short_description.id: Taowu adalah makhluk mitologis Tiongkok yang termasuk Empat Bahaya. Teks klasik menggambarkannya sebagai binatang berwajah manusia dan berkaki harimau.
short_description.en: Taowu is a Chinese mythological creature counted among the Four Perils. Classical texts describe it as a beast with a human face and tiger feet.

long_description.id: Taowu adalah makhluk mitologis Tiongkok yang termasuk Empat Bahaya. Unsur namanya dikaitkan dengan tunggul kayu dan bangku.
long_description.en: Taowu is a Chinese mythological creature counted among the Four Perils. Elements of its name are linked to a tree stump and a stool.

long_description.id: Maknanya berkembang dari makhluk tertentu menjadi makhluk mitologis dan orang keras kepala. Sima Qian menggambarkannya sebagai anak Zhuanxu yang memberontak dan merusak, dan teks Shiji menyebut anak itu tidak berbakat, tidak dapat dididik, dan tidak mengerti ucapan. Guoyu dan Shuo Yuan menempatkan Taowu di Gunung Pi pada zaman Shang.
long_description.en: Its meaning expanded from a particular beast to mythical beings and stubborn people. Sima Qian portrays it as a rebellious and destructive son of Zhuanxu, and the Shiji text calls that son untalented, unteachable and deaf to speech. The Guoyu and Shuo Yuan locate Taowu on Mount Pi during the Shang period.

long_description.id: Teks Shenyijing menggambarkan binatang di wilayah liar barat yang mirip harimau berbulu anjing, berwajah manusia, berkaki harimau, bermulut dan bertaring babi, dan berekor satu zhang delapan chi; namanya Taowu, juga disebut Aohen dan Nanxun. Menurut artikel ini, Kaisar Shun menerimanya bersama Empat Bahaya lain dan mengasingkan mereka ke pelosok kerajaan.
long_description.en: The Shenyijing text describes a beast in the western wilds like a dog-furred tiger with a human face, tiger feet, a pig's mouth and tusks and a tail one zhang eight chi long; it is named Taowu, also called Aohen and Nanxun. According to the article, Emperor Shun received it with the other Four Perils and banished them to the outer reaches of the kingdom.

description.id: Menurut artikel, Kaisar Shun menerima Taowu bersama Empat Bahaya lain dan mengasingkan mereka ke pelosok kerajaan.
description.en: According to the article, Emperor Shun received Taowu with the other Four Perils and banished them to the outer reaches of the kingdom.

role.en: Taowu is one of the four villains who are banished.

summary.en: According to the article, the trouble Taowu caused continued until Emperor Shun received him with the other Four Perils and banished them to the outer reaches of the kingdom.

statement.en: The Shiji text says Taowu belongs to the "three clans" that long troubled the world, and that Shun later banished the "four villain clans" (四凶族) to the four frontiers to ward off goblins (螭魅).

short_description.id: Tarkshya adalah makhluk Rigveda yang digambarkan sebagai kuda dengan sebutan arishta-nemi.
short_description.en: Tarkshya is a Rigvedic being described as a horse with the epithet arishta nemi.

long_description.id: Tarkshya adalah makhluk Rigveda yang digambarkan sebagai kuda dengan sebutan arishta-nemi. Tafsir alternatif menganggapnya burung.
long_description.en: Tarkshya is a Rigvedic being described as a horse with the epithet arishta nemi. An alternative interpretation regards him as a bird.

long_description.id: Mahabharata dan Harivamsha kemudian menyamakannya dengan Garuda. Bhagavata Purana juga mengaitkan nama itu dengan ayah Garuda. Mahabharata memasukkannya di antara keturunan Kashyapa. Sebutan arishta-nemi diterangkan berarti dengan pinggir roda yang utuh.
long_description.en: The Mahabharata and Harivamsha later identify him with Garuda. The Bhagavata Purana also associates the name with Garuda's father. The Mahabharata counts him among Kashyapa's offspring. The epithet arishta nemi is explained as with intact wheel rims.

long_description.id: Dalam terjemahan himne Rigveda yang dikutip di sini, Tarkshya diseru demi kesejahteraan: ia disifati perkasa, ditugaskan para dewa, pemenang, pelampaui kereta, dan penakluk pasukan, serta cepat, dan di himne lain disebut bersenjata tanpa cela. Komentar yang menyertai himne-himne itu menyamakannya dengan suparna, putra Trksa, yang ditugaskan membawa Soma dari surga, dan dengan Garuda; komentar itu juga menafsirkan nama Aristanemi sebagai bersenjata tak rusak atau tak terkalahkan, tidak sama dengan penjelasan "pinggir roda yang utuh" dari sumber lain.
long_description.en: In the translated Rigveda hymns quoted here, Tarkshya is invoked for welfare: he is described as mighty, commissioned by the gods, victorious, the outstripper of chariots, the overthrower of hosts and swift, and in another verse as having unblemished weapons. The commentary accompanying these hymns equates him with suparna, son of Trksa, commissioned to bring the Soma from heaven, and with Garuda; it also explains the name Aristanemi as having unharmed or irresistible weapons, unlike the "intact wheel-rims" explanation of another source.

short_description.id: Tenaga-Ashinaga adalah raksasa dalam sejumlah legenda daerah Jepang.
short_description.en: Tenaga-Ashinaga are giants in several Japanese regional legends.

long_description.id: Tenaga-Ashinaga adalah raksasa dalam sejumlah legenda daerah Jepang. Mereka muncul sebagai satu raksasa, pasangan menikah, atau saudara dengan anggota tubuh luar biasa panjang.
long_description.en: Tenaga-Ashinaga are giants in several Japanese regional legends. They appear as one giant, a married pair or siblings with unusually long limbs.

long_description.id: Kisah Gunung Chōkai menggambarkan serangan terhadap pelancong dan kapal. Kisah berbeda antara hilangnya mereka setelah doa dan penyerahan diri disertai penghentian kanibalisme.
long_description.en: Mount Chōkai accounts describe attacks on travelers and ships. Accounts differ between their disappearance after prayer and surrender with an end to cannibalism.

long_description.id: Kamus Digital Daijisen Plus mendefinisikannya sebagai yōkai raksasa bertangan atau berkaki luar biasa panjang dari wilayah Tōhoku dan Hokuriku. Dalam satu versi dari Yuza, raksasa ini menarik kapal dengan kakinya dari puncak Gunung Chōkai, sampai dewa langit meledakkan gunung itu dan puncaknya yang terlempar menjadi Pulau Tobishima.
long_description.en: The Digital Daijisen Plus dictionary defines it as a giant yōkai with extraordinarily long arms or legs from the Tōhoku and Hokuriku regions. In one version from Yuza, the giant raked in ships with its feet from the summit of Mount Chōkai until the god of heaven blew the mountain apart, and the summit that flew off became Tobishima.

long_description.id: Sebuah kamus biografi menyajikan tenaga-ashinaga sebagai sosok legenda Tiongkok yang tercatat dalam Shanhaijing sebagai orang berlengan panjang dan berpaha panjang. Menurut kamus itu, setelah masuk ke Jepang mereka dianggap makhluk abadi yang mendoakan umur panjang kaisar dan dilukis sebagai hiasan istana.
long_description.en: A biographical dictionary presents tenaga-ashinaga as legendary figures of China, recorded in the Shanhaijing as the long-armed and long-legged people. According to that dictionary, after entering Japan they were regarded as immortal beings invoked for the emperor's longevity and painted as palace decoration.

description.id: Tempat tinggal raksasa dalam legenda Akita dan Yamagata.
description.en: Home of the giant in Akita and Yamagata legends.

sources.title: 手長足長（大友義助・武田正「最上川物語」）（怪異・妖怪伝承データベース 0590051）

claims.quote: 手長足長（てながあしなが）は、秋田県、山形県、福島県、長野県、福井県などに伝わる伝説・昔話に登場する巨人。

statement.id: Tenaga-Ashinaga adalah raksasa dalam sejumlah legenda daerah Jepang.
statement.en: Tenaga-Ashinaga are giants in several Japanese regional legends.

claims.quote: その特徴は｢手足が異常に長い巨人｣で各地の伝説は共通しているが、手足の長い一人の巨人、または夫の足（脚）が異常に長く妻の手（腕）が異様に長い夫婦、または兄弟の巨人とも言われ、各地で細部は異なることもある。

statement.id: Mereka muncul sebagai satu raksasa, pasangan menikah, atau saudara dengan anggota tubuh luar biasa panjang.
statement.en: They appear as one giant, a married pair or siblings with unusually long limbs.

claims.quote: 秋田では鳥海山に棲んでいたとされ、山から山に届くほど長い手足を持ち、旅人をさらって食べたり、日本海を行く船を襲うなどの悪事を働いていた。

statement.id: Kisah Gunung Chōkai menggambarkan serangan terhadap pelancong dan kapal.
statement.en: Mount Chōkai accounts describe attacks on travelers and ships.

claims.quote: それでも手長足長の悪行は続いたため、後にこの地を訪れた慈覚大師が吹浦（山形県鳥海山大物忌神社）で百日間祈りを捧げた末、鳥海山は吹き飛んで手長足長が消え去ったという。また消えたのではなく、大師の前に降参して人を食べなくなったともいわれ、大師がこの地を去るときに手長足長のために食糧としてタブノキの実を撒いたことから、現在でも三崎山（にかほ市小砂川地域）にはタブノキが茂っているのだという。

statement.id: Kisah berbeda antara hilangnya mereka setelah doa dan penyerahan diri disertai penghentian kanibalisme.
statement.en: Accounts differ between their disappearance after prayer and surrender with an end to cannibalism.

claims.quote: 日本の妖怪。秋田県、山形県、福島県、長野県、福井県など東北・北陸地方に伝承がある、手や足が異様に長い巨人。
claims.locator: デジタル大辞泉プラス

statement.id: Digital Daijisen Plus mendefinisikannya sebagai yōkai Jepang, raksasa bertangan atau berkaki luar biasa panjang yang diceritakan di wilayah Tōhoku dan Hokuriku, seperti Akita, Yamagata, Fukushima, Nagano dan Fukui.
statement.en: Digital Daijisen Plus defines it as a Japanese yōkai, a giant with extraordinarily long arms or legs told of in the Tōhoku and Hokuriku regions, such as Akita, Yamagata, Fukushima, Nagano and Fukui.

claims.quote: 中国の伝説上の人。 手あるいは足が異様にながいとされる。古代中国の地理書「山海経(せんがいきょう)」に長臂人,長股人とある。
claims.locator: デジタル版 日本人名大辞典+Plus

statement.id: Kamus biografi Kodansha menyebut tenaga-ashinaga sosok legenda Tiongkok (中国) bertangan atau berkaki luar biasa panjang, yang dalam kitab geografi kuno Shanhaijing (山海経) disebut orang berlengan panjang dan orang berpaha panjang (長臂人, 長股人).
statement.en: The Kodansha biographical dictionary calls tenaga-ashinaga legendary figures of China (中国) with extraordinarily long arms or legs, recorded in the ancient geography Shanhaijing (山海経) as the long-armed and long-legged people (長臂人, 長股人).

claims.quote: 日本にはいって名をかえ,天皇の長寿と朝廷の永久性をねがう不老長寿の神仙としてあつかわれ,宮中の装飾画にえがかれた。
claims.locator: デジタル版 日本人名大辞典+Plus

statement.id: Setelah masuk ke Jepang (日本) dengan nama lain, mereka diperlakukan sebagai makhluk abadi yang mendoakan umur panjang kaisar (天皇) dan kelanggengan istana, serta dilukis sebagai hiasan di istana.
statement.en: After entering Japan (日本) under a new name, they were treated as immortal beings invoked for the emperor's (天皇) longevity and the permanence of the court, and were painted as decoration in the palace.

claims.quote: この魔物はものすごく大きく、鳥海山の頂上にいながら沖合の船を足でかき寄せて乗員を喰っていた。天の神がこれを怒り、鳥海山を爆発させたとき飛んでいった頂上の一部が飛島である。

statement.id: Dalam versi Yuza (Yamagata) yang dicatat basis data Nichibunken, makhluk raksasa ini duduk di puncak Gunung Chōkai (鳥海山), menarik kapal di lepas pantai dengan kakinya dan memakan awaknya; dewa langit marah dan meledakkan Gunung Chōkai, dan bagian puncak yang terlempar menjadi Pulau Tobishima (飛島).
statement.en: In a Yuza (Yamagata) version recorded in the Nichibunken database, this huge monster sat on the summit of Mount Chōkai (鳥海山), raking in ships offshore with its feet and eating their crews; the god of heaven grew angry and blew up Mount Chōkai, and the part of the summit that flew off became Tobishima (飛島).

short_description.id: Tentōki dan Ryūtōki adalah sepasang sosok mirip iblis dalam tradisi Jepang.
short_description.en: Tentōki and Ryūtōki are a pair of demonlike figures in Japanese tradition.

long_description.id: Tentōki dan Ryūtōki adalah sepasang sosok mirip iblis dalam tradisi Jepang.
long_description.en: Tentōki and Ryūtōki are a pair of demonlike figures in Japanese tradition.

long_description.id: Penampilan oni kecil mereka melambangkan kemenangan Empat Raja Langit atas kejahatan. Patung karya Kōben di Kōfuku-ji membawa lentera persembahan bagi Buddha.
long_description.en: Their small-oni appearance symbolizes the Four Heavenly Kings’ victory over evil. Kōben’s statues at Kōfuku-ji carry lantern offerings for the Buddha.

long_description.id: Kamus Jepang mencatat Tentōki sebagai patung oni dari kayu rakitan yang diwarnai, karya Kōben tahun 1215, yang menopang lentera dengan bahu dan tangan kiri; patung ini juga disebut Tōdaiki dan berstatus Harta Nasional.
long_description.en: Japanese dictionaries record Tentōki as a painted joined-wood oni statue made by Kōben in 1215, supporting a lantern with its left shoulder and hand; it is also called Tōdaiki and is a National Treasure.

long_description.id: Pasangannya, Ryūtōki, dililit seekor naga dan membawa lentera di atas kepala, dengan tangan bersilang dan mata melirik ke atas. Secarik kertas di dalam patung itu mencatat bahwa ia dibuat oleh Kōben pada bulan keempat tahun Kenpō 3.
long_description.en: Its partner, Ryūtōki, has a dragon coiled around it and carries a lantern on its head, with crossed hands and upward-glancing eyes. A slip of paper inside the statue records that it was made by Kōben in the fourth month of Kenpō 3.

description.id: Kuil tempat kedua patung disimpan.
description.en: Temple housing both statues.

description.id: Kōben membuat patung Tentōki dan Ryūtōki di Kōfuku-ji.
description.en: Kōben made the Tentōki and Ryūtōki statues at Kōfuku-ji.

claims.quote: Tentōki and Ryūtōki (木造天燈鬼立像 mokuzō tentōki ritsuzō) and (木造竜燈鬼立像 mokuzō ryūtōki ritsuzō) are a pair of demon-like creatures in Japanese folklore.

statement.id: Tentōki dan Ryūtōki adalah sepasang sosok mirip iblis dalam tradisi Jepang.
statement.en: Tentōki and Ryūtōki are a pair of demonlike figures in Japanese tradition.

claims.quote: They are usually depicted as small oni, and symbolize the power of the Shitennō to repel and defeat evil.

statement.id: Penampilan oni kecil mereka melambangkan kemenangan Empat Raja Langit atas kejahatan.
statement.en: Their small-oni appearance symbolizes the Four Heavenly Kings’ victory over evil.

claims.quote: Kōben sculpted notable statues of Tentōki and Ryūtōki, each considered a National Treasure of Japan, carrying lanterns as offering to the Historical Buddha at Kōfuku-ji in Nara.

statement.id: Patung karya Kōben di Kōfuku-ji membawa lentera persembahan bagi Buddha.
statement.en: Kōben’s statues at Kōfuku-ji carry lantern offerings for the Buddha.

claims.quote: 奈良興福寺所蔵の鬼の姿の彫像。寄せ木造り。着色。建保3年（1215）康弁作。竜灯鬼と一対をなし、左肩と左手で灯籠を支え持つ。国宝。

statement.id: Menurut Digital Daijisen, Tentōki adalah patung berwujud oni milik Kōfuku-ji (興福寺) di Nara, dari kayu rakitan dan diwarnai, karya Kōben (康弁) tahun 1215; berpasangan dengan Ryūtōki, menopang lentera dengan bahu dan tangan kiri, dan berstatus Harta Nasional (国宝).
statement.en: According to Digital Daijisen, Tentōki is an oni-shaped statue owned by Kōfuku-ji (興福寺) in Nara, of joined wood and painted, made by Kōben (康弁) in 1215; it pairs with Ryūtōki, supports a lantern with its left shoulder and hand, and is a National Treasure (国宝).

claims.quote: 彫刻。木造。建保三年（一二一五）、康弁(こうべん)作。肩と左手で灯籠(とうろう)を支えている鬼の立像。龍灯鬼と二体一対をなす。奈良興福寺蔵。国宝。灯台鬼。
claims.locator: 精選版 日本国語大辞典

statement.id: Nihon Kokugo Daijiten mencatat patung oni berdiri ini juga dengan nama Tōdaiki (灯台鬼), membentuk pasangan dua patung dengan Ryūtōki.
statement.en: The Nihon Kokugo Daijiten also records this standing oni statue under the name Tōdaiki (灯台鬼), forming a two-figure pair with Ryūtōki.

claims.quote: 奈良興福寺所蔵の、天灯鬼と一対をなす彫像。寄せ木造り。着色。建保3年（1215）康弁作。胴体に竜がからみ、頭上に灯籠をのせる。

statement.id: Ryūtōki adalah patung di Kōfuku-ji yang berpasangan dengan Tentōki, karya Kōben tahun 1215; seekor naga melilit tubuhnya dan ia membawa lentera di atas kepala.
statement.en: Ryūtōki is a statue at Kōfuku-ji paired with Tentōki, made by Kōben in 1215; a dragon coils around its body and it carries a lantern on its head.

claims.quote: 足を踏まえ、手を前に組んで口をへの字に結び、上目をしている。胎内(たいない)に建保三年卯月廿六日法橋康弁作と書かれた紙片が納められていた。
claims.locator: 精選版 日本国語大辞典

statement.id: Ryūtōki berdiri menjejakkan kaki, tangan bersilang di depan, mulut terkatup melengkung ke bawah, dan mata melirik ke atas; di dalam patung ditemukan secarik kertas bertuliskan bahwa patung itu dibuat oleh Hokkyō Kōben (法橋康弁) pada hari ke-26 bulan keempat tahun Kenpō 3 (建保三年).
statement.en: Ryūtōki stands with feet planted, hands crossed in front, mouth pressed into a downturned line and eyes glancing upward; a slip of paper inside the statue states that it was made by Hokkyō Kōben (法橋康弁) on the 26th day of the fourth month of Kenpō 3 (建保三年).

short_description.id: Thayé adalah arwah orang jahat yang telah mati dalam mitologi Myanmar, digambarkan bertubuh mengerikan sebesar raksasa dan dikaitkan dengan penyakit seperti kolera dan cacar.
short_description.en: In Burmese mythology the thayé are the spirits of dead evil people, pictured as hideous giants and linked with diseases such as cholera and smallpox.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi Myanmar, thayé, yang juga dieja tasei, adalah orang jahat yang telah mati dan dihukum menjadi roh tanpa tubuh. Taw Sein Ko menggolongkannya ke dalam kelas kelima roh Burma, yakni roh tanpa tubuh yang pengaruhnya dianggap jahat: Thaye dan Thabet adalah roh orang yang mati dengan kematian kekerasan, perempuan yang meninggal saat melahirkan, atau orang yang hidup jahat dan penuh dosa; tase sendiri adalah istilah umum bagi semua roh tanpa tubuh yang dahulu manusia.
long_description.en: In Burmese mythology the thayé, also spelled tasei, are wicked people who after death were condemned to be disembodied spirits. Taw Sein Ko places them in the fifth class of Burmese spirits, bodiless beings whose influence is thought malignant: the Thaye and Thabet are the ghosts of people killed violently, women lost in childbirth, or those who led sinful lives; tase itself is the general word for every bodiless spirit that was once human.

long_description.id: Dalam cerita rakyat, roh-roh ini memusuhi manusia dan digambarkan bertubuh mengerikan sebesar raksasa dengan lidah panjang, besar, dan berlendir seperti belalai gajah. Encyclopedia Mythica menyebut jari atau lidah mereka panjang berlendir, dan menggolongkan mereka sebagai roh orang yang mati dengan kematian kekerasan serta memusuhi manusia. Menurut Taw Sein Ko, kegemaran khusus mereka adalah menyebabkan kematian manusia.
long_description.en: In folk tales these spirits are hostile to people and pictured with hideous, giant-sized bodies and long, huge, slimy tongues like an elephant's trunk. Encyclopedia Mythica says their fingers or tongues are long and slimy and counts them as disembodied spirits of people who died violent deaths and are hostile to mankind. According to Taw Sein Ko, their special delight is to cause human deaths.

long_description.id: Thayé memasuki kota pada tengah hari atau malam hari, dan di pedesaan Myanmar penduduk mengatakan mereka menyebabkan penyakit seperti kolera dan cacar. Taw Sein Ko mencatat bahwa roh-roh ini dipercaya berkeliaran saat matahari terbenam mencari mangsa dan sangat aktif pada masa wabah, sehingga orang mengusirnya dengan memukul dinding, pintu, ketel, nampan, atau simbal; terkejut atau jatuh mendadak dipercaya mempermudah pengaruh buruk mereka.
long_description.en: Thayé enter towns at noon or at night, and in rural Myanmar villagers say they cause illness such as cholera and smallpox. Taw Sein Ko records that these spirits are believed to roam at sunset in search of prey and to be especially active in epidemics, so people scare them off by beating walls, doors, kettles, trays or cymbals; a sudden fright or fall is believed to ease their baneful influence.

long_description.id: Menurut Taw Sein Ko, roh jahat ini kadang dikatakan memasuki tubuh buaya atau harimau dan menghasutnya menimbulkan banyak korban jiwa. Sebuah ensiklopedia mitologi vampir menyebut thaye tase tercipta ketika seseorang mati dengan kematian kekerasan, kembali sebagai raksasa buruk rupa yang menyebabkan wabah kolera dan cacar, dan senang mendatangi ranjang orang yang sekarat serta menertawakan penderitaan mereka.
long_description.en: Taw Sein Ko adds that such malevolent spirits are at times said to take over alligators or tigers and drive them to kill many people. An encyclopedia of vampire mythology says the thaye tase is created when a person dies a violent death, returns as an ugly giant causing cholera and smallpox outbreaks, and likes to visit the bedsides of the dying and laugh at their misery.

short_description.id: Kura-kura dan labi-labi berkaki tiga merupakan hewan mitos dari Tiongkok.
short_description.en: Three-legged turtles and softshell turtles are mythical animals from China.

long_description.id: Kura-kura dan labi-labi berkaki tiga merupakan hewan mitos dari Tiongkok. Erya memberi nama Fen untuk kura-kura bercangkang keras dan Nai untuk labi-labi.
long_description.en: Three-legged turtles and softshell turtles are mythical animals from China. The Erya names the hard shelled turtle Fen and the softshell turtle Nai.

long_description.id: Terjemahan Shan Hai Jing menyebut kura-kura berkaki tiga di River Mad pada Mount Bigbitter. Kisah lain menempatkan labi-labi berkaki tiga dengan ekor bercabang di River Trailer.
long_description.en: A translation of the Shan Hai Jing places three-footed turtles in River Mad on Mount Bigbitter. Another passage places three-footed softshell turtles with branching tails in River Trailer.

long_description.id: Teks-teks lama menambahkan beberapa rincian. Catatan pada Erya menyebut kura-kura berkaki tiga di 大苦山 dan labi-labi berkaki tiga di 從山, serta di kolam di 君山, tempat juga muncul kura-kura bermata enam. Komentar Erya menjelaskan bahwa hewan berkaki tiga diberi nama berbeda karena kura-kura dan labi-labi biasanya berkaki empat. Kisah dalam 《庚巳編》 menyebut seorang pria yang lenyap setelah memakan labi-labi berkaki tiga, dan nelayan yang mencarinya lebih dulu menjaring gumpalan daging berbentuk manusia.
long_description.en: Older texts add further details. The Erya annotation mentions three-legged turtles on Mount 大苦山, three-legged softshell turtles on Mount 從山, and a pond on Mount 君山 that also yields six-eyed turtles. The Erya commentary explains that the three-footed animals get distinct names because turtles and softshell turtles ordinarily have four feet. A tale in the 《庚巳編》 describes a man who vanished after eating a three-legged softshell turtle, and fishermen searching for one first netted a human-shaped lump of flesh.

claims.quote: Three-legged turtle (simplified Chinese: 三足龟; traditional Chinese: 三足龜; pinyin: Sānzúguī) and Three-legged softshell turtle (simplified Chinese: 三足鳖; traditional Chinese: 三足鱉; pinyin: Sānzúbiē) are mythical turtles from China.

statement.id: Kura-kura dan labi-labi berkaki tiga merupakan hewan mitos dari Tiongkok.
statement.en: Three-legged turtles and softshell turtles are mythical animals from China.

claims.quote: According to the ancient dictionary Erya, the former (pertaining to hardshell turtles including tortoises) is properly called Fen (simplified Chinese: 贲; traditional Chinese: 賁; pinyin: Fén), and the latter, Nai (Chinese: 能; pinyin: Nái).

statement.id: Erya memberi nama Fen untuk kura-kura bercangkang keras dan Nai untuk labi-labi.
statement.en: The Erya names the hard shelled turtle Fen and the softshell turtle Nai.

claims.quote: ...On the south face of Mount Bigbitter the River Mad rises and flows southwest to empty into the River Person. Three-footed turtles are numerous in the River Mad. Those who eat it won't have a serious illness, and it can be taken to cure a swelling.

statement.id: Terjemahan Shan Hai Jing menyebut kura-kura berkaki tiga di River Mad pada Mount Bigbitter.
statement.en: A translation of the Shan Hai Jing places three-footed turtles in River Mad on Mount Bigbitter.

claims.quote: ...The River Trailer rises on its summit and runs a hidden course to its base. This river contains many three-footed [softshell] turtles with a branching tail. If you eat it, you won't succumb to the plague of the malign force.

statement.id: Kisah lain menempatkan labi-labi berkaki tiga dengan ekor bercabang di River Trailer.
statement.en: Another passage places three-footed softshell turtles with branching tails in River Trailer.

claims.quote: 《山海經》曰：從山多三足鱉，大苦山多三足龜。今吳興郡陽羨縣君山上有池，池中出三足鱉，又有六眼龜。
claims.locator: 釋魚, 鱉三足，能。龜三足，賁 (annotation)

statement.id: Catatan pada Erya mengutip 《山海經》: banyak labi-labi berkaki tiga di gunung 從山 dan kura-kura berkaki tiga di gunung 大苦山; catatan itu menambahkan bahwa di kolam di gunung 君山 di Kabupaten 陽羨 (Wuxing) muncul labi-labi berkaki tiga dan juga kura-kura bermata enam.
statement.en: The annotation to the Erya quotes the 《山海經》: three-legged softshell turtles are plentiful on Mount 從山 and three-legged turtles on Mount 大苦山; it adds that a pond on Mount 君山 in Yangxian County (吳興郡陽羨縣) yields three-legged softshell turtles and also six-eyed turtles.

claims.quote: 鱉、龜皆四足，三足者異，故異其名。鱉之三足者名能，龜之三足者名賁也。

statement.id: Komentar pada Erya menjelaskan bahwa labi-labi dan kura-kura umumnya berkaki empat, sehingga yang berkaki tiga diberi nama berbeda: 能 untuk labi-labi dan 賁 untuk kura-kura.
statement.en: The commentary to the Erya explains that softshell turtles and turtles ordinarily have four feet, so the three-footed ones are given different names: 能 for the softshell turtle and 賁 for the turtle.

claims.quote: 庚午夏，太倉州有百姓道見漁者，持一鱉而三足，買歸令婦炰之。既熟，呼婦共餐，婦不欲食，出坐門外。久之不聞其夫聲，入視已失所在，地上止存發一縷，衣服冠履，事事皆在，如蛻形者。

statement.id: Dalam 《庚巳編》 diceritakan seorang warga 太倉州 membeli labi-labi berkaki tiga dari nelayan dan istrinya memasaknya; setelah ia memakannya sendiri, sang istri masuk dan hanya menemukan seuntai rambut serta pakaian suaminya di lantai, seolah ia telah meluruhkan wujudnya.
statement.en: The 《庚巳編》 tells of a commoner of 太倉州 who bought a three-legged softshell turtle from a fisherman and had his wife cook it; after he ate it, his wife found only a lock of hair and his clothes on the ground, as if he had shed his form.

claims.quote: 群漁云：初被命，網於川，舉網驚其太重，及岸視之，乃一肉塊如人形，五官俱具而無手足，閉目蠢動。漁大驚怕，擲之水中

statement.id: Para nelayan dalam kisah itu mengatakan bahwa ketika diperintahkan menangkap labi-labi berkaki tiga, mereka lebih dulu menjaring benda yang sangat berat berupa gumpalan daging berbentuk manusia, berwajah lengkap tetapi tanpa tangan dan kaki, bergerak-gerak dengan mata terpejam, lalu melemparnya kembali ke air.

short_description.id: Tiga Kami Perintis (開拓三神) adalah sebutan kolektif untuk tiga kami, yaitu Ōkunitama, Ōnamuchi, dan Sukunahikona, yang dipuja di Hokkaidō Jingū dan kuil-kuil baru di wilayah ekspansi Jepang.
short_description.en: The Three Pioneer Kami (開拓三神) is the collective name for three kami, Ōkunitama, Ōnamuchi and Sukunahikona, enshrined at Hokkaidō Jingū and at new shrines in territories of Japanese expansion.

long_description.id: Tiga Kami Perintis (開拓三神, kaitaku-sanshin) adalah nama kolektif untuk tiga kami yang dipuja di kuil-kuil seperti Hokkaidō Jingū, yaitu kuil yang baru didirikan di wilayah yang dimasuki bangsa Yamato sejak zaman pramodern dan modern, bukan di daratan utama Jepang. Ketiganya adalah Ōkunitama, Ōnamuchi, dan Sukunahikona.
long_description.en: The Three Pioneer Kami (開拓三神, kaitaku-sanshin) is a collective name for three kami enshrined at shrines such as Hokkaidō Jingū, that is, shrines newly built in regions the Yamato people entered from the early modern and modern periods rather than on the Japanese mainland. The three are Ōkunitama, Ōnamuchi and Sukunahikona.

long_description.id: Ōkunitama digambarkan sebagai roh negeri itu sendiri, Ōnamuchi sebagai dewa pembentuk negeri, dan Sukunahikona sebagai dewa yang membantunya. Menurut artikel jurnal Suga Kōji, ketiganya dipilih dari kelompok kunitsu-kami (地祇) dalam mitologi klasik Jepang dan dimohonkan sebagai penjaga pembukaan lahan (kaitaku, 開拓) di tiap wilayah.
long_description.en: Ōkunitama is described as the spirit of the land itself, Ōnamuchi as the land-making deity, and Sukunahikona as the deity who helped him. According to Suga Kōji's journal article, the three were chosen from the kunitsu-kami (地祇) of Japanese classical mythology and invoked as guardians of pioneering (kaitaku, 開拓) in each region.

long_description.id: Menurut Encyclopedia of Shinto, Sukunahikona adalah kami mungil yang jatuh dari sela jari induknya dan membantu Ōnamuchi membentuk negeri; di hampir semua versi kisah keduanya tampil berpasangan dan bekerja sama mengembangkan negeri serta menciptakan obat-obatan. Ōnamuchi biasanya dianggap nama lain Ōkuninushi, meski beberapa karya menggambarkannya sebagai kami pembentuk negeri.
long_description.en: According to the Encyclopedia of Shinto, Sukunahikona is a tiny kami who fell from between his parent's fingers and helped Ōnamuchi form the land; in almost all versions of the story the two appear as a pair and cooperate in developing the land and inventing medicines. Ōnamuchi is usually considered another name of Ōkuninushi, although some works describe him as a land-forming kami.

long_description.en: Tōdaiki is a figure in a tale recorded in Heike Monogatari and other classical works. In Toriyama Sekien's depiction, the figure wears Chinese-style clothes and carries a lamp on the head; the underlying figure is human.

long_description.id: Kisahnya menceritakan Karu no Otodo yang hilang setelah pergi sebagai utusan ke Tiongkok. Anaknya, Hitsu no Saishō, pergi mencarinya dan menjumpai manusia yang dijadikan penyangga lilin. Anak tersebut kemudian mengenali sosok itu sebagai ayahnya. Folkloris Yoshiyuki Iikura menolak menganggap kemiripan dengan legenda urban modern sebagai bukti garis pewarisan cerita.
long_description.en: The tale tells of Karu no Otodo, who disappears after travelling as an envoy to China. His son Hitsu no Saishō searches for him and encounters a man turned into a candle stand. The son then recognizes the figure as his father. Folklorist Yoshiyuki Iikura rejects treating resemblance to a modern urban legend as proof of narrative transmission.

long_description.id: Kamus modern menggolongkannya sebagai yōkai dan meringkas kisahnya: seorang utusan ke Tiongkok dipakukan kandil di kepalanya lalu diubah menjadi oni. Contoh tertua nama itu yang dikutip kamus berasal dari Hōbutsushū sekitar tahun 1179, yang menyebut lampu dipasang di kepala dan tubuh yang dilukisi.
long_description.en: Modern dictionaries class it as a yōkai and summarise the tale: an envoy to China had a candlestand nailed to his head and was turned into an oni. The earliest example of the name cited by the dictionary is the Hōbutsushū of about 1179, which mentions a lamp fixed on the head and a painted body.

short_description.id: Tokoloshe adalah roh air bertubuh kecil dalam mitologi Nguni dan Zulu. Menurut kepercayaan, ia nakal dan jahat, dapat menjadi tak terlihat, dan dipanggil orang berniat jahat untuk mencelakai orang lain.
short_description.en: The tokoloshe is a small water spirit in Nguni and Zulu mythology. According to belief it is mischievous and evil, can become invisible, and is called upon by malevolent people to harm others.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi Nguni, tokoloshe digambarkan sebagai roh air yang bertubuh seperti kurcaci, juga dikenal dengan nama seperti tikoloshe dan hili. Kamus pada sumber kedua mendefinisikannya sebagai peri air atau goblin berbulu yang nakal. Sebuah kutipan dalam kamus itu menyebut makhluk ini tinggal di kolam dalam dan di antara alang-alang di tepi sungai.
long_description.en: In Nguni mythology the tokoloshe is described as a dwarf-like water spirit, also known by names such as tikoloshe and hili. The dictionary in the second source defines it as a mischievous hairy water-sprite or goblin. One citation in that dictionary says these beings live in deep pools and among the reeds along river banks.

long_description.id: Menurut kepercayaan, tokoloshe dapat menjadi tak terlihat dengan meminum air atau menelan batu. Kutipan lain menyebutnya makhluk kecil berbulu berwajah mirip babun dan berbentuk seperti manusia, sedangkan kutipan ketiga menyebutnya roh jahat berwujud lelaki kecil.
long_description.en: According to belief the tokoloshe can become invisible by drinking water or swallowing a stone. Another citation calls it a small hairy being with a baboon-like face and the form of a man, while a third citation calls it an evil spirit in the shape of a small man.

long_description.id: Orang berniat jahat disebut memanggil tokoloshe untuk menimbulkan masalah bagi orang lain. Paling ringan, ia dipakai untuk menakuti anak-anak; kekuatannya disebut dapat menyebabkan penyakit atau bahkan kematian. Salah satu uraian menyebut dukun jahat menciptakannya dari mayat melalui cara-cara tertentu.
long_description.en: Malevolent people are said to call on the tokoloshe to cause trouble for others. At its mildest it is used to scare children; its power is said to extend to illness or even death. One account says a malevolent witch doctor creates it from a dead body by certain methods.

long_description.id: Sebagai perlindungan, tempat tidur dinaikkan dari tanah, misalnya dengan menaruh bata di bawah tiap kakinya. Perlindungan juga dicari dari tokoh spiritual seperti pendeta bertitel apostolik dan sangoma.
long_description.en: As protection, beds are raised off the ground, for example by putting bricks under each leg. Protection is also sought from spiritual figures such as pastors with an apostolic calling and sangomas.

statement.en: In Nguni mythology, the tokoloshe (also tikoloshe, tikolosh, tonkolosh, tonkolosi, tokolotshe, thokolosi or hili) is a dwarf-like water spirit.

statement.en: Protection against it includes traditional methods such as raising beds off the ground and the intervention of spiritual figures such as pastors with an apostolic calling or traditional healers (sangomas).

statement.en: In the account of its creation, the witch doctor finds a dead body to possess, pierces the eye sockets and brain with a hot iron rod so the body cannot think for itself, and sprinkles it with a special powder that shrinks the body.

claims.quote: According to legend, the only way to keep the tokoloshe away at night is to put a few bricks beneath each leg of one's bed.

statement.en: According to legend, the only way to keep the tokoloshe away at night is to put a few bricks beneath each leg of one's bed.

statement.en: The dictionary defines the tokoloshe in African folklore as a mischievous and lascivious hairy water-sprite or goblin, also called hili.

short_description.id: Trucafort adalah raksasa setinggi gunung dalam mitologi Katalan yang membawa dua batu dan menjatuhkan yang terberat kepada anak-anak nakal.
short_description.en: Trucafort is a mountain-tall giant of Catalan mythology who carries two stones and drops the heavier one on naughty children.

long_description.id: Trucafort adalah tokoh mitologi Katalan: lelaki setinggi gunung dengan janggut begitu panjang hingga terinjak saat berjalan. Ia membawa dua batu, satu di atas kepala dan satu lagi sepuluh kali lebih berat yang dijatuhkannya kepada anak-anak nakal. Menurut Joan Amades, ia lazim dalam cerita anak di Castellar de n'Hug.
long_description.en: Trucafort is a figure of Catalan mythology: a man as tall as a mountain with a beard so long he treads on it. He carries two stones, one on his head and another ten times heavier that he drops on naughty children. According to Joan Amades he was common in children's stories at Castellar de n'Hug.

long_description.id: Antara 1970 dan 1990 ia tokoh umum dalam dongeng Katalan, bahkan di sekolah dasar. Sisinya sebagai bandit dikaitkan dengan bandit nyata Gabriel Torrent de la Goula, meski legenda menampilkannya jauh lebih romantis.
long_description.en: Between 1970 and 1990 he was a common figure in Catalan tales, even in primary schools. His bandit side is linked to the real bandit Gabriel Torrent de la Goula, though the legend paints him far more romantically.

long_description.id: Ciri utamanya adalah batu besar yang dipakainya di atas kepala seperti topi. Lolongan kesakitannya, karena terus menginjak janggutnya sendiri, konon mengguncang gunung dan terdengar hingga tujuh jam jauhnya. Ia juga disebut membawa gada batu raksasa untuk meremukkan anak-anak nakal.
long_description.en: His main feature was a huge rock worn on his head like a hat. His howls of pain from treading on his own beard were said to shake the mountains and be heard seven hours away. He was also said to carry a huge stone mace to crush bad children.

long_description.id: Banyak yang berpendapat tokoh ini mungkin berasal dari tokoh sejarah, atau setidaknya berbagi julukan dengannya.
long_description.en: Many suggest the figure may stem from a historical person, or at least a shared nickname.

short_description.id: Turtle Lake Monster adalah makhluk dalam cerita rakyat Kanada yang konon menghuni Turtle Lake, Saskatchewan [turtle-lake-monster-c01].
short_description.en: The Turtle Lake Monster is a Canadian folklore creature said to inhabit Turtle Lake, Saskatchewan [turtle-lake-monster-c01].

long_description.id: Turtle Lake Monster konon menghuni Turtle Lake di Saskatchewan [turtle-lake-monster-c01]. Ia digambarkan sepanjang 3 hingga 9 meter dengan kepala mirip anjing, kuda laut, atau babi [turtle-lake-monster-c02]. Orang Cree punya legenda tentang orang yang hilang di wilayahnya [turtle-lake-monster-c03]. Penampakannya mungkin ikan sturgeon besar [turtle-lake-monster-c04].
long_description.en: The Turtle Lake Monster reportedly inhabits Turtle Lake in Saskatchewan [turtle-lake-monster-c01]. It is described as 3 to 9 m long with a dog, seahorse or pig head [turtle-lake-monster-c02]. The Cree told of people vanishing in its territory [turtle-lake-monster-c03]. Sightings may be of a large sturgeon [turtle-lake-monster-c04].

long_description.id: Turtle Lake berjarak sekitar 100 km di utara North Battleford [turtle-lake-monster-c05]. Sebagian saksi menyebut panjang monster itu sekitar tiga hingga sembilan meter, kulitnya halus atau bersisik, dan kepalanya mirip kuda atau anjing [turtle-lake-monster-c06]. Seorang pria mengenang bahwa pada 1985, saat masih anak-anak, ia dan saudaranya melihat makhluk besar mirip ikan sepanjang kira-kira tujuh hingga sepuluh kaki [turtle-lake-monster-c07].
long_description.en: Turtle Lake is about 100 km north of North Battleford [turtle-lake-monster-c05]. Some witnesses put the monster at about three to nine metres, with smooth or scaly skin and a horse-like or dog-like head [turtle-lake-monster-c06]. One man recalled that as a child in 1985 he and his brother spotted a large fishlike creature about seven to ten feet long [turtle-lake-monster-c07].

long_description.id: Seorang perempuan First Nation yang diwawancarai mengenang bahwa orang menyuruhnya menjauhi tepi timur danau, dekat titik terdalam tempat monster itu tinggal [turtle-lake-monster-c10]. Kaum skeptis menduga makhluk itu seekor moose yang berenang [turtle-lake-monster-c08], dan staf perikanan mengatakan pengukuran kedalaman tidak menunjukkan adanya monster [turtle-lake-monster-c09].
long_description.en: A First Nation woman who was interviewed recalled being told to stay away from the eastern shore of the lake, near the deepest points where the monster lived [turtle-lake-monster-c10]. claims.quote: In Canadian folklore, the Turtle Lake Monster is an entity purportedly inhabiting Turtle Lake, in West Central Saskatchewan, Canada.

statement.id: Dalam cerita rakyat Kanada, Turtle Lake Monster adalah makhluk yang konon menghuni Turtle Lake di Saskatchewan barat-tengah.
statement.en: In Canadian folklore, the Turtle Lake Monster reportedly inhabits Turtle Lake in West Central Saskatchewan.

claims.quote: The monster is usually described as a creature 3–9 m (9.8–29.5 ft) long, scaly or smooth, with no dorsal fin, and a head resembling either a dog, a seahorse, or a pig.

statement.id: Monster ini biasanya digambarkan sepanjang 3 hingga 9 meter, tanpa sirip punggung, dengan kepala mirip anjing, kuda laut, atau babi.
statement.en: It is usually described as 3 to 9 m long, with no dorsal fin and a head like a dog, seahorse or pig.

claims.quote: Reports date back to pre-settlement days when the local Cree had a legend about people who ventured into the Turtle Lake Monster's territory and vanished without a trace.

statement.id: Laporannya sudah ada sebelum masa pemukiman, ketika orang Cree punya legenda tentang orang yang masuk wilayahnya dan hilang tanpa jejak.
statement.en: Reports go back to pre-settlement days, when the Cree told of people who entered its territory and vanished.

claims.quote: There is speculation that the monster sightings may be attributed to sightings of an unusually large lake sturgeon, or a relict population of prehistoric plesiosaurs.

statement.id: Ada dugaan penampakannya adalah ikan sturgeon danau yang sangat besar atau sisa populasi plesiosaurus.
statement.en: Sightings may be of an unusually large lake sturgeon, or relict plesiosaurs.

claims.quote: Turtle Lake is about 100 km north of North Battleford.

statement.id: Turtle Lake berjarak sekitar 100 km di utara North Battleford.
statement.en: Turtle Lake is about 100 km north of North Battleford.

claims.quote: Some people who have seen the TLM say it’s about three to nine metres long. Some say it’s smooth-skinned. Others say it’s scaly. Witnesses also say it has a horse-like or dog-like head.

statement.id: Sebagian orang yang pernah melihatnya menyebut panjangnya sekitar tiga hingga sembilan meter; ada yang menyebut kulitnya halus, ada yang bersisik, dan saksi juga menyebut kepalanya mirip kuda atau anjing.
statement.en: Some people who have seen it say it is about three to nine metres long, some say smooth-skinned and others scaly, and witnesses also say it has a horse-like or dog-like head.

claims.quote: recalling how as a child in 1985, he and his brother spotted the TLM. ... it was a large fishlike creature, perhaps seven to 10 feet long.

statement.id: Seorang pria yang menulis kepada penerbit artikel mengenang bahwa pada 1985, saat masih anak-anak, ia dan saudaranya melihat monster itu, yang ia gambarkan sebagai makhluk besar mirip ikan, mungkin sepanjang tujuh hingga sepuluh kaki.
statement.en: A man who wrote to the article's publisher recalled that as a child in 1985 he and his brother spotted the monster, which he described as a large fishlike creature perhaps seven to 10 feet long.

claims.quote: Skeptics think it could be a moose out for a swim.

statement.id: Kaum skeptis menduga makhluk itu mungkin seekor moose yang sedang berenang.
statement.en: Skeptics think it could be a moose out for a swim.

claims.quote: The fisheries staff said they did depth soundings of Turtle Lake and never saw anything that suggested a monster lived there.

statement.id: Staf perikanan mengatakan mereka melakukan pengukuran kedalaman Turtle Lake dan tidak pernah melihat apa pun yang menunjukkan adanya monster di sana.
statement.en: Fisheries staff said they did depth soundings of Turtle Lake and never saw anything that suggested a monster lived there.

claims.quote: an 84-year-old First Nation woman interviewed for the article recalled ... Later when she moved to Turtle Lake, people told her to stay away from the Eastern shore, near the deepest points of the lake where the monster lived.

statement.id: Seorang perempuan First Nation berusia 84 tahun yang diwawancarai untuk sebuah artikel mengenang bahwa setelah pindah ke Turtle Lake, orang-orang menyuruhnya menjauhi tepi timur, dekat titik terdalam danau tempat monster itu tinggal.
statement.en: An 84-year-old First Nation woman interviewed for an article recalled that after she moved to Turtle Lake, people told her to stay away from the eastern shore, near the deepest points of the lake where the monster lived.

claims.quote: The initial purpose of these stories, regardless of continental origin, is to teach children to respect the water as dangerous.

short_description.id: Ulmecatl adalah salah satu dari enam raksasa putra Mixcoatl dan Tlaltecuhtli dalam mitologi Aztek, pendiri Cuetlachoapan [ulmecatl-c01, ulmecatl-c02].
short_description.en: Ulmecatl is one of the six giant sons of Mixcoatl and Tlaltecuhtli in Aztec mythology, founder of Cuetlachoapan [ulmecatl-c01, ulmecatl-c02].

long_description.id: Ulmecatl adalah salah satu dari enam raksasa putra Mixcoatl dan Tlaltecuhtli yang menghuni Bumi setelah Air Bah [ulmecatl-c01]. Sebagai putra ketiga, ia mendirikan Cuetlachoapan, tempat kota Puebla kini berada [ulmecatl-c02].
long_description.en: Ulmecatl is one of the six giant sons of Mixcoatl and Tlaltecuhtli who populated the Earth after the Great Flood [ulmecatl-c01]. The third son, he founded Cuetlachoapan, where Puebla now stands [ulmecatl-c02].

long_description.id: Dalam puisi kosmogoni Nahoa beserta catatan kakinya, keenam bersaudara itu lahir dari persatuan "ular ganas dari awan putih" dengan pasangannya, lalu tinggal di bumi dan menjadi sumber banyak bangsa [ulmecatl-c03]. Puisi itu menyebut Ulmécatl sebagai salah satunya, di samping Xélhua si sulung, Tenoch, Xicaláncatl, Mixtécatl, dan Otómitl [ulmecatl-c05].
long_description.en: In the Nahoa cosmogony poem with its footnotes, the six brothers are born of the union of the "ferocious serpent of white cloud" with his mate, and they dwell on the earth and become the source of many races [ulmecatl-c03]. The poem names Ulmécatl as one of them, alongside Xélhua the firstborn, Tenoch, Xicaláncatl, Mixtécatl and Otómitl [ulmecatl-c05].

long_description.id: Catatan kaki buku itu menyebut bahwa Cuetlaxcoapan adalah tempat kota Puebla kini berada, dan bahwa Ulmécatl mendirikan tempat-tempat lain di samping itu [ulmecatl-c06]. Catatan kaki lain menjelaskan kepercayaan orang Indian bahwa bumi mula-mula dihuni raksasa yang disebut quinametzin, dengan tulang fosil besar sebagai sisa-sisa mereka [ulmecatl-c04].
long_description.en: A footnote in the book says Cuetlaxcoapan was the place where the city of Puebla stands today, and that Ulmécatl founded other places besides it [ulmecatl-c06]. Another footnote explains the Indian belief that the earth was first inhabited by giants called quinametzin, with large fossilized bones as their remains [ulmecatl-c04].
