short_description.id: Umi zatō adalah yōkai raksasa berwujud biksu buta bertongkat di atas laut yang digambarkan dalam Gazu Hyakki Yagyō dan gulungan Hyakki Yagyō. Sedikit yang diketahui tentangnya; menurut sebagian kisah ia membalikkan kapal.
short_description.en: The umi zatō is a giant yōkai depicted as a blind, rod-carrying monk figure above the sea in the Gazu Hyakki Yagyō and Hyakki Yagyō scrolls. Little is known about it; some tales say it capsizes ships.

long_description.id: Umi zatō (海座頭) adalah yōkai Jepang dalam Gazu Hyakki Yagyō karya Toriyama Sekien dan berbagai gulungan seperti Hyakki Yagyō Emaki milik Matsui Library. Ia digambarkan seperti biwa hōshi raksasa yang berdiri di atas laut, memegang tongkat di tangan kanan dan membawa pipa di punggung. Tidak ada teks penjelas pada gambar-gambar awal itu, sehingga tidak diketahui yōkai macam apa yang dimaksud.
long_description.en: The umi zatō (海座頭) is a Japanese yōkai found in Toriyama Sekien's Gazu Hyakki Yagyō and in several scrolls such as the Matsui Library's Hyakki Yagyō Emaki. Pictures show it as a huge biwa hōshi standing over the sea, a rod in its right hand and a pipa on its back. The early pictures come with no explanatory text, so what kind of yōkai it was meant to be is unknown.

long_description.id: Menurut Yokai.com ia raksasa yang mengembara di laut pada malam hari dan mengetuk ombak dengan tongkat; biasanya dianggap tidak berbahaya, tetapi dalam sebagian kisah ia memanggil kapal lalu membalikkannya dan kadang menelan perahu utuh. Bila orang di kapal menjawab dengan sopan, ia lenyap. Wikipedia mencatat ia berjalan di atas air dan muncul ketika umibōzu tidak muncul, sering pada akhir bulan.
long_description.en: According to Yokai.com it is a giant that wanders the seas at night tapping the waves with a cane; it is usually considered harmless, but in some tales it beckons ships and flips them over and occasionally swallows boats whole. If the people aboard answer politely, it vanishes. Wikipedia notes it walks on top of the water and appears when umibōzu no longer do, often at the end of the month.

long_description.id: Seorang peneliti menganggapnya yōkai yang hanya ada dalam lukisan, dan Yokai.com menduga ia rekaan seniman zaman Edo untuk menghias gulungan. Dalam buku pascaperang ia ditafsirkan sejenis umibōzu.
long_description.en: A researcher considers it a yōkai that existed only in paintings, and Yokai.com suspects it was invented by Edo-period artists to decorate scrolls. In postwar books it is interpreted as a kind of umibōzu.

short_description.id: Underwater panther atau Mishipeshu ("Lynx Besar") adalah makhluk air mitos terpenting bagi bangsa Anishinaabeg dan tetangganya di Great Lakes. Ia lebih sering dipandang jahat dan perlu ditenangkan, tetapi sebagian tradisi meyakininya juga melindungi.
short_description.en: The underwater panther or Mishipeshu ("the Great Lynx") is a key mythical water being of the Anishinaabeg and neighbours around the Great Lakes. It was more often seen as malevolent and in need of placating, though some traditions held it could also protect.

long_description.id: Underwater panther adalah salah satu makhluk air mitos terpenting di wilayah Great Lakes, terutama bagi Anishinaabeg. Namanya, Mishipeshu, berarti "Lynx Besar"; ia berkepala dan bercakar kucing raksasa, bersisik, dan berduri di punggung serta ekornya. Ia tinggal di Pulau Michipicoten, Danau Superior, dan bagi orang Algonquin adalah makhluk dunia bawah yang paling kuat. Kamus Ojibwe mengartikan kata mishibizhii sebagai singa atau panter dan sebagai underwater panther.
long_description.en: The underwater panther is a leading mythical water being of the Great Lakes region, especially for the Anishinaabeg. Its name, Mishipeshu, means "the Great Lynx"; it has a giant cat's head and paws, scales, and spikes down its back and tail. It lives on Michipicoten Island in Lake Superior, and for the Algonquins it ranked as the strongest underworld being. An Ojibwe dictionary glosses the word mishibizhii as a lion or panther and as an underwater panther.

long_description.id: Menurut kepercayaan itu, Mishipeshu hidup di bagian terdalam danau dan sungai, tempat ia dapat menimbulkan badai, jeram, dan arus, menenggelamkan kano, dan menewaskan orang, sering anak-anak. Ia juga dikenal sebagai penjaga tembaga di Danau Superior dan wilayah Great Lakes, dan manito air ini memberi hadiah tembaga. Ia dipandang berseberangan dengan thunderbird, penguasa kekuatan udara, dalam konflik abadi namun saling melengkapi.
long_description.en: In these beliefs, Mishipeshu lives in the deepest parts of lakes and rivers, where it can stir up storms, rapids and currents, sink canoes and drown people, often children. It is also known as the keeper of the copper of Lake Superior and the Great Lakes region, and this water manito made gifts of copper. It is seen as opposed to the thunderbirds, masters of the powers of the air, in an eternal yet complementary conflict.

long_description.id: Sebagian tradisi meyakini underwater panther dapat menjadi makhluk penolong dan pelindung: ia dipercaya melindungi dan memberi makan orang yang jatuh menembus es, dan memberi kekuatan penyembuhan kepada dukun yang menerima perlindungannya. Namun lebih sering ia dipandang sebagai binatang jahat yang membawa kematian dan kemalangan dan perlu ditenangkan. Mengambil tembaga sangat tabu, terlebih dari Pulau Michipicoten, dan hingga tahun 1950-an Prairie Band of Potawatomi Indians masih menggelar upacara untuk menenangkannya.
long_description.en: Some traditions held the underwater panther to be a helpful, protective being: it was believed to shelter and feed those who fell through the ice, and to give medicinal power to shamans who accepted its guardianship. Yet more often it was viewed as a malevolent beast bringing death and misfortune, in need of placating. Taking copper was highly taboo, above all from Michipicoten Island, and as late as the 1950s the Prairie Band of Potawatomi Indians held a ceremony to calm it.

cultural_context.id: Mengambil tembaga dari wilayah itu sangat tabu bagi bangsa Ojibwe, terlebih dari rumah Mishipeshu di Pulau Michipicoten.
cultural_context.en: Taking copper from the region was extremely taboo for the Ojibwe, above all from Mishipeshu's home on Michipicoten Island.

long_description.id: Ura adalah oni kuno dari daerah Kibi di Okayama selatan. Tradisi menjadikannya penguasa Kibi yang dikalahkan Kibitsuhiko.

long_description.id: Kibitsuhiko melukai mata kirinya dengan menembakkan dua anak panah bersama. Pengejaran mereka berubah dari burung pegar dan elang menjadi ikan mas dan burung kormoran sebelum Ura menyerah.
long_description.en: Kibitsuhiko wounds his left eye by shooting two arrows together. Their pursuit changes from pheasant and hawk to carp and cormorant before Ura surrenders.

long_description.id: Dalam versi yang diringkas basis data Nichibunken, Ura adalah roh jahat dari Baekje yang menjarah Kibi pada masa Kaisar Suinin. Setelah ditangkap dan dipenggal, kepalanya terus meraung selama bertahun-tahun sampai rohnya dipuja untuk menenangkannya.
long_description.en: In a version summarized in the Nichibunken database, Ura is a demon from Baekje who plundered Kibi in the reign of Emperor Suinin. After his capture and beheading, his head kept roaring for years until his spirit was enshrined to pacify it.

long_description.id: Kepala itu dikatakan dikubur di bawah kuali di balai kuali Kibitsuhiko Jinja, dan bunyi kuali dalam ritual ramalan yang dipimpin miko dianggap sebagai teriakannya.
long_description.en: The head is said to be buried under the cauldron in the cauldron hall of Kibitsuhiko Shrine, and the sound of the cauldron in the divination led by a shrine maiden is regarded as its cry.

description.id: Kuil dengan balai kuali yang dikaitkan dengan kepala Ura.
description.en: Shrine with a cauldron hall linked to Ura's head.

note.id: Pangeran yang menumpas Ura.
note.en: The prince who subdued Ura.

claims.quote: 温羅（うら/おんら）は、岡山県南部の吉備地方に伝わる古代の鬼。

statement.id: Ura adalah oni kuno dari daerah Kibi di Okayama selatan.
statement.en: Ura is an ancient oni of the Kibi region in southern Okayama.

claims.quote: 温羅とは伝承上の鬼・人物で、古代吉備地方の統治者であったとされる。「鬼神」「吉備冠者（きびのかじゃ）」という異称があり、伝承によると吉備には吉備津彦命（きびつひこのみこと）が派遣され退治されたという。

statement.id: Tradisi menjadikannya penguasa Kibi yang dikalahkan Kibitsuhiko.
statement.en: Tradition makes him a Kibi ruler defeated by Kibitsuhiko.

claims.quote: 温羅に対して矢を1本ずつ射たが温羅はその都度石を投げて撃ち落とした。そこで命が2本同時に射たところ、1本は撃ち落とされたが、もう1本は温羅の左眼を射抜いた。

statement.id: Kibitsuhiko melukai mata kirinya dengan menembakkan dua anak panah bersama.
statement.en: Kibitsuhiko wounds his left eye by shooting two arrows together.

claims.quote: すると温羅は雉に化けて逃げたので、五十狭芹彦命は鷹に化けて追った。さらに温羅は鯉に身を変えて逃げたので、五十狭芹彦命は鵜に変化してついに捕らえたところ温羅は降参し「吉備冠者」の名を五十狭芹彦命に献上した。これにより五十狭芹彦命は吉備津彦命と呼ばれるようになった。

statement.id: Pengejaran mereka berubah dari burung pegar dan elang menjadi ikan mas dan burung kormoran sebelum Ura menyerah.
statement.en: Their pursuit changes from pheasant and hawk to carp and cormorant before Ura surrenders.

claims.quote: 垂仁天皇の時代、吉備国で略奪を繰り返す百済の鬼神、温羅を退治するため、イサセリヒコノミコトが派遣された。

statement.id: Menurut ringkasan di basis data Nichibunken, pada masa Kaisar Suinin (垂仁天皇) Isaserihiko no Mikoto dikirim untuk menumpas Ura, roh jahat (鬼神) dari Baekje (百済) yang terus menjarah negeri Kibi (吉備国).
statement.en: According to a summary in the Nichibunken database, in the reign of Emperor Suinin (垂仁天皇) Isaserihiko no Mikoto was sent to subdue Ura, a demon (鬼神) from Baekje (百済) who repeatedly plundered the land of Kibi (吉備国).

claims.quote: 雉や鯉に姿を変えて逃れる温羅を捕らえたミコトは、首を刎ねて曝したが、その首が何年も大声でうなり続けたため、温羅の霊を祀って鎮めた。

statement.id: Setelah menangkap Ura yang melarikan diri dengan berubah menjadi burung pegar dan ikan mas, sang pangeran memenggal dan memajang kepalanya; karena kepala itu terus meraung keras selama bertahun-tahun, roh Ura dipuja untuk menenangkannya.
statement.en: After catching Ura, who fled by turning into a pheasant and a carp, the prince beheaded him and displayed the head; because the head kept roaring loudly for years, Ura's spirit was enshrined to pacify it.

claims.quote: 吉備津彦神社にはお釜殿があり、吉凶を占いたければ阿曾女という巫女に請えば、巫女は柴をたき、供米を篩に入れて釜の湯気にかざす。

statement.id: Kibitsuhiko Jinja (吉備津彦神社) memiliki balai kuali (お釜殿); orang yang ingin meramal nasib meminta kepada miko bernama Asome (阿曾女), yang membakar ranting dan memegang beras persembahan dalam ayakan di atas uap kuali.
statement.en: Kibitsuhiko Shrine (吉備津彦神社) has a cauldron hall (お釜殿); those wishing to divine good or ill fortune ask a shrine maiden called Asome (阿曾女), who burns brushwood and holds offering rice in a sieve over the cauldron's steam.

claims.quote: これは昔、吉備津彦命が温羅の首をはねたときに、まだ生きているようだったので命はこれを釜の下に生められたため、その叫び声であるといわれている。

statement.id: Bunyi kuali itu dikatakan sebagai teriakan Ura, karena ketika Kibitsuhiko (吉備津彦命) memenggal kepalanya, kepala itu tampak masih hidup sehingga dikubur di bawah kuali.
statement.en: The cauldron's sound is said to be Ura's cry, because when Kibitsuhiko (吉備津彦命) cut off his head it still seemed alive, so it was buried under the cauldron.

summary.id: Ura menyerah dan menyerahkan gelarnya (吉備冠者) kepada sang pangeran.
summary.en: Ura surrenders and gives his title (吉備冠者) to the prince.

summary.id: Ura dipenggal dan kepalanya terus meraung.
summary.en: Ura is beheaded and his head keeps roaring.

short_description.id: Vadavagni adalah api bawah laut yang dipersonifikasikan sebagai makhluk merusak dalam mitologi Hindu.
short_description.en: Vadavagni is submarine fire personified as a destructive being in Hindu mythology.

long_description.id: Vadavagni adalah api bawah laut yang dipersonifikasikan sebagai makhluk merusak dalam mitologi Hindu. Wujudnya digambarkan berkepala kuda betina dan bertubuh nyala api. Ia mengembara di dasar laut dan memakan air sambil menunggu Pralaya, saat ia muncul untuk menghancurkan bumi.
long_description.en: Vadavagni is submarine fire personified as a destructive being in Hindu mythology. It is described as having a mare's head and a body of blazing flame. It wanders the seabed consuming water while awaiting the Pralaya, when it emerges to destroy the earth.

long_description.id: Ia dikatakan muncul dari mulut kuda betina bernama Vadavamukha. Vishnu Purana menempatkannya di bawah Kshira Sagara. Dalam satu kisah, api amarah Aurva yang dilepas ke samudra menjadi kepala kuda Vadavamukha yang melahap air samudra; dalam kisah lain ia lahir dari janin berapi kuda betina yang muncul dari paha Pippalada, atau dari amarah Siwa, dan Wisnu pun menyatakan dirinya sebagai Vadavagni.
long_description.en: It is said to emerge from the mouth of a mare called Vadavamukha. The Vishnu Purana places it beneath the Kshira Sagara. In one legend the wrathful fire of Aurva released into the ocean became the horse's head Vadavamukha that consumes the ocean's waters; in others it was born of the fiery foetus of a mare that emerged from Pippalada's thigh, or from Shiva's wrath, and Vishnu declares himself the Vadavagni.

long_description.id: Kisah pengekangannya berkaitan dengan turunnya Saraswati sebagai Sungai Sarasvati. Vadavagni mensyaratkan dibawa di tangan seorang perawan, dan Saraswati dipilih; kehadirannya mulai menguapkan air sehingga Wisnu membuat air itu abadi dan Saraswati menempatkan dirinya di sepanjang samudra untuk melindungi ciptaan.
long_description.en: Tales of its suppression concern the descent of Saraswati as the Sarasvati river. Vadavagni insisted on being carried by a virgin and Saraswati was chosen; as its mere presence began drying the waters, Vishnu made the waters everlasting and Saraswati took her place beside the ocean to guard creation.

summary.en: Vadavagni required to be carried by a virgin and Saraswati was chosen. He was taken to the ocean; his presence evaporated the waters so Vishnu rendered the waters perennial.

claims.quote: Vadavagni (Sanskrit: वाडवाग्नि, romanized: Vāḍavāgni, lit. 'mare-fire'), also referred to as Vadavanala (Sanskrit: वडवानल, romanized: Vaḍavānala) refers to a submarine fire embodied in the form of a destructive being in Hindu mythology. It is described to be a being that manifested with the head of a mare, but a body of blazing flame.

statement.id: Vadavagni adalah api bawah laut yang dipersonifikasikan sebagai makhluk merusak dalam mitologi Hindu.
statement.en: Vadavagni is submarine fire personified as a destructive being in Hindu mythology.

claims.quote: It is described to be a being that manifested with the head of a mare, but a body of blazing flame.

statement.id: Wujudnya digambarkan berkepala kuda betina dan bertubuh nyala api.
statement.en: It is described as having a mare's head and a body of blazing flame.

claims.quote: The Vadavagni is regarded to wander the seabed and consume its waters, awaiting the moment it could emerge and destroy the earth during the Pralaya, the dissolution of the earth at the end of an age. Various legends regarding the origin and suppression of the Vadavagni exist in Hindu literature, most prominently the descent of the goddess Saraswati as the Sarasvati river.

statement.id: Ia mengembara di dasar laut dan memakan air sambil menunggu Pralaya.
statement.en: It wanders the seabed consuming water while awaiting Pralaya.

claims.quote: Various legends regarding the origin and suppression of the Vadavagni exist in Hindu literature, most prominently the descent of the goddess Saraswati as the Sarasvati river.

statement.id: Kisah pengekangannya berkaitan dengan turunnya Saraswati sebagai Sungai Sarasvati.
statement.en: Tales of its suppression concern Saraswati's descent as the Sarasvati River.

claims.quote: The Vadavagni is described to emerge from the mouth of a mare called Vadavamukha (mare-face). This mare's mouth is sometimes described to be present under a sea at the South Pole. It is stated to remain under the sea until it finally erupts, leading to the destruction of the earth. It is stated to be a metaphor for insatiable energy.

statement.id: Ia dikatakan muncul dari mulut kuda betina bernama Vadavamukha.
statement.en: It is said to emerge from a mare's mouth called Vadavamukha.

claims.quote: The Vishnu Purana states that the Vadavagni is located beneath the Kshira Sagara, surrounded by seas of curds, ghee, sugarcane juice, wine, and sweet water.

statement.id: Vishnu Purana menempatkannya di bawah Kshira Sagara.
statement.en: The Vishnu Purana locates it beneath the Kshira Sagara.

claims.quote: Hearing these words of the Pitris, Aurva, O child, replied unto them to this effect: ... Like fire consuming dry woods, this rage of mine will certainly consume me if I do not accomplish my vow.

statement.id: Dalam teks ini, Aurva berkata bahwa amarahnya, bagai api yang melahap kayu kering, akan melahapnya bila ia tidak menunaikan sumpahnya.
statement.en: In this text Aurva says his rage, like fire consuming dry woods, will certainly consume him if he does not accomplish his vow.

claims.quote: If, therefore, thou desirest it, O Brahmana, let this fire born of thy wrath abide in the great ocean, consuming the waters thereof, for it hath been said that the worlds are made of water.

statement.id: Dalam teks ini, disarankan agar api yang lahir dari amarah itu bersemayam di samudra besar sambil melahap airnya, karena dikatakan dunia terbuat dari air.
statement.en: In this text it is advised that the fire born of the wrath abide in the great ocean, consuming its waters, for it is said the worlds are made of water.

claims.quote: Then, O child, Aurva cast the fire of his wrath into the abode of Varuna. And that fire which consumeth the waters of the great ocean, became like unto a large horse's head which persons conversant with the Vedas call by the name of Vadavamukha. And emitting itself from that mouth it consumeth the waters of the mighty ocean.

statement.id: Dalam teks ini, Aurva melemparkan api amarahnya ke kediaman Varuna; api yang melahap air samudra besar itu menjadi seperti kepala kuda besar yang oleh para ahli Weda disebut Vadavamukha, dan dari mulut itu ia melahap air samudra perkasa.
statement.en: In this text Aurva cast the fire of his wrath into the abode of Varuna; that fire which consumes the waters of the great ocean became like a large horse's head that persons conversant with the Vedas call Vadavamukha, and emitting from that mouth it consumes the waters of the mighty ocean.

claims.quote: When Aurva told them that he could not let the flames that had risen from his austerities to come to naught as that would burn him alive, his Pitrs suggested that he release his wrathful flame into the ocean. The sage obeyed, and the flame became the Vadavagni, a mare-faced inferno. Due to this reason, Vadavagni is also called Aurvanala.

statement.id: Ketika Aurva berkata ia tidak dapat membiarkan api pertapaannya sia-sia karena akan membakarnya hidup-hidup, para leluhurnya menyarankan agar ia melepas api amarahnya ke samudra; sang resi menurut, dan api itu menjadi Vadavagni, api neraka berwajah kuda betina, sehingga juga disebut Aurvanala.
statement.en: When Aurva said he could not let the flames risen from his austerities come to naught as they would burn him alive, his Pitrs suggested he release his wrathful flame into the ocean; the sage obeyed and the flame became the Vadavagni, a mare-faced inferno, which is why it is also called Aurvanala.

claims.quote: Furious, Pippalada performed a severe penance, seeking the destruction of the devas. After a year, a vadavā (a mare) emerged from his thigh. This mare gave birth to a fiery foetus from its womb, which became the Vadavagni (submarine fire), after which it disappeared from the scene.

statement.id: Dalam kisah lain, setelah setahun seekor kuda betina (vadavā) muncul dari paha Pippalada dan melahirkan janin berapi yang menjadi Vadavagni (api bawah laut), lalu menghilang.
statement.en: In another legend, after a year a mare (vadavā) emerged from Pippalada's thigh and gave birth to a fiery foetus that became the Vadavagni (submarine fire), after which the mare disappeared.

claims.quote: Vadavagni acquiesced, but required that he be carried in the hand of a virgin to be taken to his destination. Saraswati was chosen for this mission.

statement.id: Vadavagni setuju, tetapi mensyaratkan dibawa di tangan seorang perawan ke tempat tujuannya; Saraswati dipilih untuk tugas itu.
statement.en: Vadavagni acquiesced but required that he be carried in the hand of a virgin to his destination; Saraswati was chosen for this mission.

claims.quote: When Vadavagni started to cause the waters to evaporate by his very presence, Vishnu rendered the waters perennial, and Saraswati stationed herself along the ocean to protect creation.

statement.id: Ketika kehadiran Vadavagni mulai menguapkan air, Wisnu membuat air itu abadi, dan Saraswati menempatkan dirinya di sepanjang samudra untuk melindungi ciptaan.
statement.en: When Vadavagni's very presence started to evaporate the waters, Vishnu rendered the waters perennial and Saraswati stationed herself along the ocean to protect creation.

claims.quote: The Vadavagni is also described to be the product of Shiva's wrath that emerged from his third eye and annihilated Kamadeva to ash, when the latter attempted to arouse his desire towards Parvati.

statement.id: Vadavagni juga digambarkan sebagai hasil amarah Siwa yang keluar dari mata ketiganya dan membakar Kamadewa menjadi abu ketika Kamadewa mencoba membangkitkan hasratnya kepada Parwati.
statement.en: Vadavagni is also described as the product of Shiva's wrath that emerged from his third eye and reduced Kamadeva to ash when he tried to arouse Shiva's desire for Parvati.

claims.quote: In the Mahabharata, Vishnu declares that he is the Vadavagni, consuming the turbulent waters and disgorging them again.

statement.id: Dalam Mahabharata, Wisnu menyatakan bahwa dirinya adalah Vadavagni yang melahap air bergolak lalu memuntahkannya lagi.
statement.en: In the Mahabharata, Vishnu declares that he is the Vadavagni, consuming the turbulent waters and disgorging them again.

summary.id: Api amarah Aurva yang dilepas ke samudra atas saran para leluhur.
summary.en: The wrathful fire of Aurva released into the ocean on the advice of his ancestors.

summary.id: Janin berapi yang dilahirkan kuda betina yang muncul dari paha Pippalada.
summary.en: A fiery foetus born of the mare that emerged from Pippalada's thigh.

summary.id: Hasil amarah Siwa yang keluar dari mata ketiganya.
summary.en: The product of Shiva's wrath from his third eye.

summary.id: Wisnu menyatakan dirinya sebagai Vadavagni.
summary.en: Vishnu declares himself to be the Vadavagni.

short_description.id: Vákner adalah makhluk mitologi Galisia berwujud manusia serigala raksasa yang ditemui uskup Armenia Mártir dalam ziarahnya ke Fisterra.
short_description.en: The Vákner is a Galician mythical creature shaped like a huge werewolf, met by the Armenian bishop Mártir on his pilgrimage to Fisterra.

long_description.id: Vákner adalah tokoh mitologi Galisia, hewan ajaib yang biasanya berwujud manusia serigala raksasa. Kisahnya bermula dari Mártir, uskup Armenia dari Erzincan, yang memulai ziarah ke Roma pada Oktober 1485; ia tinggal 84 hari di Galisia pada 1492 dan menulis catatan singkat yang diterjemahkan ke bahasa Spanyol pada 1898.
long_description.en: The Vákner is a Galician mythological figure, a fantastic animal usually shaped like a huge werewolf. Its story starts with Mártir, an Armenian bishop from Erzincan, who set out for Rome in October 1485; he spent 84 days in Galicia in 1492 and wrote a brief account translated into Spanish in 1898.

long_description.id: Makhluk yang ditemui Mártir di jalan menuju Fisterra kini menjadi lambang ziarah Santiago ke Fisterra.
long_description.en: The being Mártir met on the road to Fisterra has become a symbol of the Way of St James to Fisterra.

long_description.id: Dalam catatan perjalanan itu, Vákner disebut binatang buas besar yang sangat berbahaya; orang heran ia selamat, sebab rombongan dua puluh orang pun tidak bisa lewat. Para ahli menduga makhluk ini serigala atau serigala rabies, manusia serigala, naga, atau makhluk jahat lain yang sarat simbol. Sebuah instalasi patung manusia serigala karya Cándido Pazos kemudian direncanakan di Camino.
long_description.en: In the travel account the Vákner is a large and very harmful wild beast; people marvelled that he survived, since companies of twenty could not pass. Specialists have suggested a wolf or rabid wolf, a werewolf, a dragon or another symbolic evil being. A werewolf sculpture by Cándido Pazos was later planned for the Camino.

short_description.id: Vegetable Man atau Veggie Man adalah makhluk mirip manusia dalam cerita rakyat West Virginia yang dilaporkan terlihat di Grant Town pada 1968. Kisahnya bertumpu pada satu saksi dan pertama dicetak oleh Gray Barker, pembuat hoaks yang dikenal.
short_description.en: The Vegetable Man, or Veggie Man, is a humanoid in West Virginia folklore reportedly seen in Grant Town in 1968. The story rests on a single witness and was first printed by Gray Barker, a known hoaxer.

long_description.id: Menurut penuturan penduduk setempat Jennings Frederick, pada Juli 1968 ia berburu marmut tanah di dekat Grant Town ketika bertemu makhluk yang kemudian dijuluki Vegetable Man. Ia menggambarkannya setinggi sekitar tujuh kaki, berwajah setengah manusia, bertubuh seperti tumbuhan, dengan lengan sangat kurus yang memegang pergelangan tangannya.
long_description.en: According to local resident Jennings Frederick, in July 1968 he was hunting groundhogs near Grant Town when he met the being later nicknamed the Vegetable Man. He described it as about seven feet tall, with semi-human facial features and a plant-like body, with extremely thin arms that gripped his wrist.

long_description.id: Makhluk itu pertama kali dilukiskan dalam cetakan oleh Gray Barker dalam buletin tahun 1976, yang menyebutnya makhluk kurus mirip tumbuhan bermata kuning, bertelinga runcing, dan berjari yang berujung seperti cawan isap berjarum. Barker menulis tentangnya dalam artikel 10 Maret 1976 berjudul "The Vegetable Man: A semi-abductee?". Tidak ada bukti penampakan itu yang terdokumentasi, dan tidak ada penampakan lanjutan.
long_description.en: Gray Barker was the first to describe the creature in print, in a 1976 newsletter that portrayed a slender, plant-like being with yellow eyes, pointed ears and fingers tipped with needle-like suction cups. Barker wrote about it in a March 10, 1976 article titled "The Vegetable Man: A semi-abductee?". No evidence of the sighting has been documented, and there have been no further sightings.

long_description.id: Peneliti Reed menulis bahwa kisah ini bertumpu pada kesaksian satu orang yang laporan tercatatnya disampaikan kepada seorang pembuat hoaks yang dikenal, dan banyak peneliti menyikapi penuturan Barker dengan hati-hati. Sejak 2024, Veggie Man Day diselenggarakan di Fairmont, West Virginia, dan makhluk itu pernah tampil dalam gim Fallout 76.
long_description.en: Researcher Reed writes that the story rests on the testimony of one person whose recorded report was made to a known hoaxer, and many researchers treat Barker's account with caution. Since 2024 a Veggie Man Day has been held in Fairmont, West Virginia, and the creature has appeared in the video game Fallout 76.

short_description.id: Veles, juga disebut Volos, adalah dewa dunia bawah dalam mitologi Slavia, dikenal dalam sumber lama sebagai dewa ternak.
short_description.en: Veles, also called Volos, is a chthonic god of the underworld in Slavic mythology, known in early sources as the cattle god.

long_description.id: Veles atau Volos adalah dewa dunia bawah dalam mitologi Slavia. Sumber sezaman menyebutnya dewa ternak, tetapi berbagai hipotesis memberinya wilayah kuasa yang lebih luas: kekayaan, alam orang mati yang dibayangkan sebagai padang rumput tempat jiwa-jiwa merumput, serta sihir, pengetahuan, ramalan, dan puisi. Sebagai penjaga batas antara dunia orang hidup dan orang mati, ia juga dewa alam liar, perburuan, dan hewan.
long_description.en: Veles or Volos is a chthonic god of the underworld in Slavic mythology. Contemporary sources call him the cattle god, but various hypotheses give him a wider domain: wealth, the realm of the dead imagined as a pasture where souls graze, and magic, knowledge, divination and poetry. Because he watched over the line separating living and dead, he also ruled the wild, the hunt and animals.

long_description.id: Ia menjamin sumpah dan menghukum pelanggarnya dengan membuat mereka "menguning". Dalam perjanjian dengan Bizantium, orang Rus bersumpah demi Perun dan demi Volos, dewa ternak, dan rela menjadi kuning seperti emas bila melanggar. Setelah dibaptis, Vladimir memerintahkan berhala Volos dilempar ke Sungai Pochaiv. Satu sumber menambahkan bahwa sesudah Kristenisasi Veles ditafsirkan ulang sebagai Iblis, dan peran pelindung ternaknya diambil alih Santo Blasius.
long_description.en: He guaranteed oaths and punished those who broke them by "turning them yellow". In treaties with Byzantium the Rus swore by Perun and by Volos, the cattle god, accepting to become yellow as gold if they failed. After his baptism Vladimir ordered the idol of Volos thrown into the Pochaiv River. One source adds that after Christianization Veles was reinterpreted as the Devil, and Saint Blasius took over his role as protector of cattle.

long_description.id: Ivanov dan Toporov merekonstruksi mitos tentang permusuhan Perun dan Veles: Veles sebagai ular merayap naik pohon dunia, diserang petir Perun, bersembunyi dengan berubah wujud, lalu dibunuh sehingga apa yang dicurinya jatuh sebagai hujan. Teori ini kemudian ditolak bahkan oleh Toporov sendiri, dan anggapan bahwa Veles adalah naga atau ular tidak lagi menjadi kesepakatan para ahli.
long_description.en: Ivanov and Toporov reconstructed a myth of enmity between Perun and Veles: Veles as a serpent climbs the world tree, is struck by Perun's lightning, hides by changing form, and is finally killed so that what he stole falls as rain. The theory was later rejected even by Toporov himself, and the view of Veles as a dragon or serpent is no longer scholarly consensus.

statement.en: Veles, also known as Volos, is a chthonic underworld god of Slavic mythology, called a cattle god (skotij bogъ) in contemporary sources, though various hypotheses give him a much broader sphere.

claims.quote: His function as protector of cattle may be connected to both wealth and rule of the underworld, which was imagined as a pasture where human souls grazed. Through comparative methods, he can be interpreted as a deity of magic, knowledge, divination, and poetry.

statement.id: Fungsinya sebagai pelindung ternak mungkin berkaitan dengan kekayaan dan kekuasaan atas dunia bawah, yang dibayangkan sebagai padang rumput tempat jiwa manusia merumput; lewat perbandingan, ia dapat ditafsirkan sebagai dewa sihir, pengetahuan, ramalan, dan puisi.
statement.en: His role as protector of cattle may link to wealth and rule of the underworld, imagined as a pasture where souls grazed; comparatively he can be read as a god of magic, knowledge, divination and poetry.

claims.quote: As the guardian of the boundary between the world of the living and the dead, he was also a god of the wilderness, hunting and animals. He was also a guarantor of oaths, punishing their violation by "turning them yellow"

statement.id: Sebagai penjaga batas antara dunia orang hidup dan orang mati, ia juga dewa alam liar, perburuan, dan hewan; ia menjamin sumpah dan menghukum pelanggarnya dengan "membuat mereka menguning".
statement.en: As guardian of the boundary between the living and the dead, he was also god of the wilderness, hunting and animals; he guaranteed oaths, punishing breakers by "turning them yellow".

claims.quote: He commanded that the idol of Volos, whom they called the cattle god, be thrown into the Pochaiv River

statement.id: Menurut Riwayat Vladimir, ia memerintahkan agar berhala Volos, yang disebut dewa ternak, dilempar ke Sungai Pochaiv.
statement.en: According to the Life of Vladimir, he ordered the idol of Volos, called the cattle god, thrown into the Pochaiv River.

claims.quote: Veles is sometimes incorrectly identified with a dragon or a serpent. This hypothesis, based on the reconstruction by Ivanov and Toporov and published in 1974

statement.id: Veles kadang keliru disamakan dengan naga atau ular; hipotesis ini berasal dari rekonstruksi Ivanov dan Toporov yang terbit pada 1974.
statement.en: Veles is sometimes wrongly identified with a dragon or serpent, a hypothesis from Ivanov and Toporov's reconstruction published in 1974.

claims.quote: They present Veles, in the form of a serpent, who slithers from the caves of the underworld and coils up the Slavic world tree towards Perun's heavenly domain. Perun attacks Veles with his lightning bolts. Veles flees, hiding or transforming himself into trees, animals or people. In the end, he is killed by Perun

statement.id: Dalam rekonstruksi itu, Veles berwujud ular merayap dari gua dunia bawah dan melilit naik pohon dunia Slavia menuju wilayah Perun; Perun menyerangnya dengan petir, Veles lari dengan bersembunyi atau berubah menjadi pohon, hewan, atau manusia, dan akhirnya dibunuh Perun.
statement.en: In that reconstruction Veles as a serpent slithers from underworld caves up the world tree toward Perun's domain; Perun strikes with lightning, Veles flees by hiding or turning into trees, animals or people, and is finally killed by Perun.

claims.quote: It was later rejected even by its own author Toporov. In terms of Slavic mythology, it conjectures the conflict between the two gods, Perun and Veles.

statement.id: Teori ini kemudian ditolak bahkan oleh pencetusnya sendiri, Toporov; dalam mitologi Slavia teori itu menduga adanya konflik antara Perun dan Veles.
statement.en: The theory was later rejected even by its author Toporov; for Slavic mythology it conjectures a conflict between Perun and Veles.

claims.quote: The constellation of the Pleiades is most likely connected with Veles in some Slavic languages, such as Old Russian Volosyni or Bulgarian Vlascite

statement.id: Gugus bintang Pleiades dalam beberapa bahasa Slavia kemungkinan besar berkaitan dengan Veles, misalnya Volosyni dalam bahasa Rusia Kuno atau Vlascite dalam bahasa Bulgaria.
statement.en: The Pleiades are most likely connected with Veles in some Slavic languages, e.g. Old Russian Volosyni or Bulgarian Vlascite.

claims.quote: His mythological nature and powers are similar, though not entirely identical, to those of Varuna, Velnias, Odin (marginally), Hermes, Afsati and Hades.

statement.id: Sifat dan kekuatan mitologisnya mirip, meski tidak sepenuhnya identik, dengan Varuna, Velnias, Odin (sedikit), Hermes, Afsati, dan Hades.
statement.en: His mythological nature and powers resemble, though not identically, those of Varuna, Velnias, Odin (marginally), Hermes, Afsati and Hades.

claims.quote: Veles wird als gehörnte Schlange mit einem langen Bart dargestellt.

statement.id: Veles digambarkan sebagai ular bertanduk dengan janggut panjang.
statement.en: Veles is depicted as a horned serpent with a long beard.

claims.quote: Nach der Christianisierung wurde Veles zum Teufel umgedeutet, sein Name taucht in dieser Funktion in Sprichwörtern auf. Die Rolle des Viehbeschützers übernahm, vermutlich aufgrund der Namensähnlichkeit, der Heilige Blasius.

statement.id: Setelah Kristenisasi, Veles ditafsirkan ulang sebagai Iblis (Teufel) dan namanya muncul dalam peribahasa; peran pelindung ternak diambil alih Santo Blasius, mungkin karena kemiripan nama.
statement.en: After Christianization Veles was reinterpreted as the Devil, appearing so in proverbs; Saint Blasius took over his role as cattle protector, probably due to the similar name.

claims.quote: may we be cursed by our god in whom we believe, by Perun and by Volos, the cattle god (skotij bogъ), and may we become yellow as gold

statement.id: Dalam perjanjian dengan Bizantium, orang Rus bersumpah: semoga kami dikutuk oleh dewa kami, oleh Perun dan oleh Volos, dewa ternak, dan menjadi kuning seperti emas bila melanggar.
statement.en: In the treaty with Byzantium the Rus swore to be cursed by Perun and by Volos, the cattle god, and become yellow as gold if they broke it.

summary.id: Satu sumber: ia digambarkan sebagai ular bertanduk berjanggut panjang.
summary.en: One source: he is depicted as a horned serpent with a long beard.

summary.id: Sumber lain: penyamaannya dengan naga atau ular keliru dan bukan lagi kesepakatan ilmiah.
summary.en: Another source: identifying him with a dragon or serpent is incorrect and no longer scholarly consensus.

short_description.id: Monster Danau Vorota adalah kriptid yang dilaporkan terlihat di Danau Vorota, Siberia timur, terutama oleh dua ahli geologi Soviet pada 1953.
short_description.en: The Vorota beast is a cryptid reported from Lake Vorota in eastern Siberia, notably by two Soviet geologists in 1953.

long_description.id: Monster Danau Vorota adalah monster danau yang dilaporkan terlihat di Danau Vorota, Siberia timur, Rusia. Danau ini salah satu dari beberapa danau di Dataran Tinggi Sordongnokh yang punya laporan penampakan serupa. Laporan dua ilmuwan Soviet tercatat dalam buku harian ekspedisi geologi Labynkyr yang disimpan di Akademi Ilmu Pengetahuan Rusia.
long_description.en: The Vorota beast is a lake monster reported from Lake Vorota in eastern Siberia, Russia. The lake is one of several on the Sordongnokh plateau with similar sighting reports. The account of two Soviet scientists is recorded in the diary of the Labynkyr geological expedition kept at the Russian Academy of Sciences.

long_description.id: Pada 30 Juli 1953, ahli geologi Viktor A. Tverdokhlebov dan Boris Bashkatov sedang meneliti di tepi danau. Mereka melaporkan tubuh lonjong abu-abu kehitaman yang muncul sedikit di permukaan, dengan dua titik terang seperti mata dan benda seperti tongkat yang mencuat. Kepalanya diperkirakan selebar 6 kaki, tubuhnya 30 sampai 40 kaki, dan di punuknya ada sirip besar. Pada 1960-an beberapa ahli geologi lain juga mengaku melihat makhluk abu-abu raksasa bersirip.
long_description.en: On 30 July 1953 the geologists Viktor A. Tverdokhlebov and Boris Bashkatov were working by the lake. They reported an oblong grey-black body showing slightly above the surface, with two eye-like bright spots and a stick-like protrusion. Its head was estimated at about 6 feet wide, its body at 30 to 40 feet, with a large fin on its hump. In the 1960s other geologists also claimed to have seen a huge grey finned creature.

long_description.id: Sebuah artikel berita menyebut bahwa selain cerita rakyat setempat tentang "Iblis" Danau Labynkyr, beberapa ilmuwan juga melaporkan makhluk aneh di Danau Vorota yang berdekatan; Tverdokhlebov menggambarkannya sebagai hewan besar seukuran orca yang berenang dekat permukaan. Artikel itu juga mencatat bahwa kabar tentang monster Vorota disambut skeptis karena tidak ada foto, video, atau bukti fisik yang dapat diverifikasi.
long_description.en: A news article notes that besides local folklore about the "Devil" of Lake Labynkyr, some scientists have also reported a strange creature in nearby Lake Vorota; Tverdokhlebov described a large animal the size of an orca swimming near the surface. The article also notes the considerable skepticism surrounding the Vorota monster, given the lack of verifiable photographs, video or physical evidence.

short_description.id: Wakka-us Kamuy adalah kamuy (dewi) air tawar dalam tradisi Ainu, yang digambarkan murah hati dan sering dimohon menjadi perantara bagi manusia.
short_description.en: Wakka-us Kamuy is the Ainu kamuy (goddess) of fresh water, described as benevolent and sometimes petitioned to intercede for humans.

long_description.id: Wakka-us Kamuy (ワッカウシカムイ) adalah kamuy, yaitu dewi, air tawar dalam tradisi Ainu. Ia juga dikenal dengan nama Petorush Mat, "Perempuan Tempat Air", dan digambarkan sebagai perempuan berambut panjang yang pandai menari dan menyanyi.
long_description.en: Wakka-us Kamuy (ワッカウシカムイ) is a goddess, or kamuy, in Ainu belief, and her domain is fresh water. A second name for her is Petorush Mat, meaning "Watering-place Woman". She is pictured as a woman with long hair who dances and sings well.

long_description.id: Dalam mitologi Ainu ia adalah dewi yang murah hati, mengawasi lembah-lembah sungai tempat permukiman Ainu berpusat dan bertanggung jawab atas semua air tawar. Ia berbelas kasih kepada manusia dan kadang dimohon menjadi perantara bagi mereka kepada kamuy lain.
long_description.en: Ainu myth treats her as a kindly goddess who watches over the river valleys where Ainu settlements gathered and who is in charge of all fresh water. She feels for humans and may be asked to speak for them to other kamuy.

long_description.id: Batchelor mencatat bahwa orang Ainu mengenal satu dewa utama atas semua sungai, danau, kolam, air terjun, dan mata air, yang disebut "dewa air" dan dikatakan berjenis kelamin perempuan; semula Batchelor mengira nama itu dipakai untuk semua dewa sungai, tetapi diberi tahu bahwa nama itu hanya untuk dewa sungai yang utama. Ia dan dewi api disebut sebagai dewa terutama dan terbaik di bumi, dan ia dipuja dengan persembahan inao dan sake serta didoakan terutama pada waktu sakit. Anak sungai dan cabang sungai kecil dikatakan sebagai keturunannya.
long_description.en: Batchelor records that the Ainu recognise one chief deity of all rivers, lakes, ponds, waterfalls and springs, called "the water god" and said to be of the feminine gender; he first supposed the name applied to all river deities but was assured it is the name of the chief river god only. She and the goddess of fire are said to be the chief and best deities on earth, and she is worshipped with offerings of inao and sake and especially prayed to in time of sickness. Small streams and river branches are said to be her offspring.

long_description.id: Satu mitos menceritakan bagaimana ia mengakhiri kelaparan atas permohonan Okikurmi. Ia dan Hasinaw-uk Kamuy melepaskan rusa dan salmon yang ditahan, lalu ia mengirim mimpi kepada Okikurmi untuk memperingatkannya agar ritual dijalankan dengan benar.
long_description.en: One myth tells how she ended a famine at the petition of Okikurmi. She and Hasinaw-uk Kamuy let loose the withheld deer and salmon, and she then sends Okikurmi a dream warning him to carry out the rituals properly.

cultural_context.id: Batchelor mencatat bahwa ia dipuja dengan persembahan inao dan sake dan terutama didoakan pada waktu sakit; ia juga digambarkan sebagai dewi air tawar yang mengawasi lembah-lembah sungai tempat permukiman Ainu berpusat.
cultural_context.en: Batchelor records that she is worshipped with offerings of inao and sake and especially prayed to in time of sickness; she is also described as the goddess in charge of fresh water who watches over the river valleys where Ainu settlements gathered.

literal_meaning.id: Batchelor menerjemahkan nama itu sebagai "dewa air".
literal_meaning.en: Batchelor glosses the name as "the water god".

famous_for.en: Ending a famine by letting loose the deer and salmon that the kamuy had withheld.

did_you_know.en: Batchelor records that small streams and river branches are called kamui-poteke, "god's little hands", and are said to be her offspring.

title.en: The famine and the feast of the kamuy

role.id: Ia mengundang para kamuy ke pesta, melepaskan rusa dan salmon, lalu memperingatkan Okikurmi lewat mimpi.
role.en: She invites the kamuy to a feast, lets the deer and salmon loose, then warns Okikurmi in a dream.

summary.id: Atas permohonan Okikurmi ia mengundang para kamuy ke pesta. Kamuy ikan dan kamuy binatang buruan mengaku menahan salmon dan rusa karena manusia tidak menjalankan ritual dengan benar. Ia dan Hasinaw-uk Kamuy melepaskan hewan-hewan itu sambil terus menari, lalu ia mengirim mimpi kepada Okikurmi agar ritual dijalankan dengan benar.
summary.en: At Okikurmi's petition she invites the kamuy to a feast. The fish and game kamuy say they have withheld the salmon and deer because humans were not performing the rituals properly. She and Hasinaw-uk Kamuy let the animals loose while continuing to dance, and she sends Okikurmi a dream telling him to see that the rituals are carried out properly.

claims.quote: Wakka-us Kamuy (Ainu ワッカウシカムイ) is the Ainu kamuy (goddess) of fresh water.

statement.id: Wakka-us Kamuy (ワッカウシカムイ) adalah kamuy (dewi) air tawar dalam tradisi Ainu.
statement.en: Wakka-us Kamuy (ワッカウシカムイ) is the Ainu kamuy (goddess) of fresh water.

claims.quote: She is also known as Petorush Mat (Watering-place Woman).

statement.id: Ia juga dikenal dengan nama Petorush Mat, yang diartikan "Perempuan Tempat Air".
statement.en: She is also known as Petorush Mat, glossed as "Watering-place Woman".

claims.quote: Wakka-us Kamuy is portrayed as a long-haired woman who is a skilled dancer and singer.

statement.id: Ia digambarkan sebagai perempuan berambut panjang yang pandai menari dan menyanyi.
statement.en: She is portrayed as a long-haired woman who is a skilled dancer and singer.

claims.quote: She is sympathetic to humanity, and is sometimes petitioned to intercede with other kamuy on their behalf.

statement.id: Ia berbelas kasih kepada manusia dan kadang dimohon menjadi perantara bagi manusia kepada kamuy lain.
statement.en: She is sympathetic to humanity and is sometimes petitioned to intercede with other kamuy on their behalf.

claims.quote: Wakka-us Kamuy and the sympathetic Hasinaw-uk Kamuy, while continuing to dance, send their souls to the storehouses and let the deer and salmon loose; in order to avoid making a scene, the other kamuy had no choice but to continue the feast.

statement.id: Dalam kisah kelaparan, ia dan Hasinaw-uk Kamuy yang berbelas kasih melepaskan rusa dan salmon dari lumbung para kamuy dengan mengirim jiwa mereka ke sana sambil terus menari, dan kamuy lain terpaksa melanjutkan pesta.
statement.en: In the famine story she and the sympathetic Hasinaw-uk Kamuy, still dancing, send their souls to the storehouses and let the deer and salmon loose, and the other kamuy have no choice but to continue the feast.

claims.quote: Afterward, Wakka-us Kamuy sends a dream to Okikurmi, telling him what had happened and why, and warning him to see that the rituals were carried out in proper fashion.

statement.id: Setelah itu ia mengirim mimpi kepada Okikurmi untuk menjelaskan apa yang terjadi dan memperingatkannya agar ritual dijalankan dengan benar.
statement.en: Afterward she sends Okikurmi a dream telling him what had happened and why, and warning him to see that the rituals are carried out properly.

claims.quote: In Ainu mythology, Wakka-us Kamuy is a benevolent goddess who oversees the river valleys around which Ainu communities centered and is responsible for all fresh water.

statement.id: Dalam mitologi Ainu ia adalah dewi yang murah hati, yang mengawasi lembah-lembah sungai tempat permukiman Ainu berpusat dan bertanggung jawab atas semua air tawar.
statement.en: In Ainu mythology she is a benevolent goddess who oversees the river valleys around which Ainu communities centered and is responsible for all fresh water.

claims.quote: One such myth tells how Wakka-us Kamuy ended a famine that had broken out. Petitioned by Okikurmi, the culture hero and sorcerer, she invites the kamuy of the rapids, the kamuy of fish, the kamuy of game, the goddess of the hunt Hasinaw-uk Kamuy, and the overseer of the land Kotan-kor Kamuy to a feast.

statement.id: Satu mitos menceritakan bagaimana ia mengakhiri kelaparan: atas permohonan Okikurmi, sang pahlawan budaya dan dukun, ia mengundang kamuy jeram, ikan, binatang buruan, dewi perburuan Hasinaw-uk Kamuy, dan pengawas tanah Kotan-kor Kamuy ke sebuah pesta.
statement.en: One myth tells how she ended a famine: petitioned by Okikurmi, the culture hero and sorcerer, she invites the kamuy of the rapids, of fish, of game, the goddess of the hunt Hasinaw-uk Kamuy and the overseer of the land Kotan-kor Kamuy to a feast.

claims.quote: The fish kamuy informs her that the humans were not killing fish in the proper ritual manner, so he has locked the salmon in his storehouse; the game kamuy says the same of the deer.

statement.id: Dalam pesta itu kamuy ikan memberitahunya bahwa manusia tidak membunuh ikan menurut cara ritual yang benar sehingga ia mengunci salmon di lumbungnya, dan kamuy binatang buruan berkata hal yang sama tentang rusa.
statement.en: At the feast the fish kamuy tells her the humans were not killing fish in the proper ritual manner, so he has locked the salmon in his storehouse, and the game kamuy says the same of the deer.

claims.quote: As Wakka-ush kamui is thus supposed to be essentially good, she is worshipped by having both inao and sake offered her, and is especially prayed to in time of sickness.

statement.id: Batchelor menulis bahwa Wakka-ush kamui dianggap pada dasarnya baik, sehingga ia dipuja dengan persembahan inao dan sake dan terutama didoakan pada waktu sakit.
statement.en: Batchelor writes that Wakka-ush kamui is thus supposed to be essentially good, and is worshipped with offerings of inao and sake and especially prayed to in time of sickness.

claims.quote: so there is supposed to be one chief deity of all the rivers, lakes, ponds, waterfalls and springs. ... the water god,’ and is said to be of the feminine gender.

statement.id: Batchelor mencatat bahwa orang Ainu mengenal satu dewa utama atas semua sungai, danau, kolam, air terjun, dan mata air, yang disebut "dewa air" dan dikatakan berjenis kelamin perempuan.
statement.en: Batchelor records that the Ainu recognise one chief deity of all rivers, lakes, ponds, waterfalls and springs, called "the water god" and said to be of the feminine gender.

claims.quote: I formerly supposed this was a name for all the river deities, but am assured that it is not so, but the name of the chief river god only.

statement.id: Batchelor semula mengira nama itu dipakai untuk semua dewa sungai, tetapi diberi tahu bahwa nama itu hanya untuk dewa sungai yang utama.
statement.en: Batchelor first supposed the name applied to all the river deities, but was assured it is the name of the chief river god only.

claims.quote: In fact, she and the goddess of fire are said to be the very chief and best deities upon the earth, and all others are subject to them as mere servants.

statement.id: Menurut Batchelor, ia dan dewi api dikatakan sebagai dewa terutama dan terbaik di bumi, dan semua dewa lain tunduk kepada mereka sebagai pelayan.
statement.en: According to Batchelor, she and the goddess of fire are said to be the very chief and best deities upon the earth, and all others are subject to them as mere servants.

claims.quote: All small streams and river branches are said to be her offspring, and are called kamui-poteke , ‘god’s little hands,’

statement.id: Menurut Batchelor, semua anak sungai dan cabang sungai kecil dikatakan sebagai keturunannya dan disebut kamui-poteke, "tangan-tangan kecil dewa".
statement.en: According to Batchelor, all small streams and river branches are said to be her offspring and are called kamui-poteke, "god's little hands".

claims.quote: The deity supposed to stand next in order to her is named Pet-otokmat , ‘ the female of the source of rivers.’

statement.id: Batchelor menyebut dewa yang dianggap berikutnya setelah dia sebagai Pet-otokmat, "perempuan sumber sungai".
statement.en: Batchelor names the deity supposed to stand next in order to her as Pet-otokmat, "the female of the source of rivers".

short_description.id: Juru adalah hewan mirip tikus yang dianggap pertanda perang dalam cerita Tiongkok.
short_description.en: Juru is a mouselike animal regarded as an omen of war in Chinese lore.

long_description.id: Juru adalah hewan mirip tikus yang dianggap pertanda perang dalam cerita Tiongkok. Telinga dan mulutnya digambarkan putih.
long_description.en: Juru is a mouselike animal regarded as an omen of war in Chinese lore. Its ears and mouth are described as white.

long_description.id: Artikel menghubungkan catatannya dengan bagian tengah kesebelas Shan Hai Jing. Salah satu kajian sejarah zoologi yang diringkas artikel menafsirkan Juru sebagai polecat stepa. Teks klasik menempatkan Juru pada Gunung Yidi.
long_description.en: The article connects its account with the eleventh central section of the Shan Hai Jing. One history of zoology study summarised in the article interprets Juru as a steppe polecat. The classical text places Juru on Mount Yidi.

long_description.id: Guo Pu mengakui bahwa bentuk tikus 鼣 yang menjadi pembanding Juru belum jelas, sedangkan Wang Fu menggambarkannya lebih besar dari tikus, mirip kelinci, dan berwarna ungu kebiruan. Tuzan karya Guo Pu menyebut Juru makhluk kecil yang tidak berbahaya, tetapi kemunculannya menandai perang. Wu Renchen mengutip sumber yang menempatkan Gunung Yidi di Nanyang.
long_description.en: Guo Pu admits that the form of the 鼣 rat to which Juru is compared is unknown, while Wang Fu describes it as larger than a rat, rabbit-like and purplish-blue. Guo Pu's Tuzan calls Juru a small, harmless creature whose appearance nonetheless signals war. Wu Renchen cites sources placing Mount Yidi in Nanyang.

statement.en: The classical text places Juru on Mount Yidi.

claims.quote: 其上多玉其下多金有獸焉其狀如鼣䑕〈郭曰爾雅說䑕有十三種中有此䑕形所未詳也音狗吠之吠　任臣案本草綱目作鼣廣博物志作鼣〉

statement.id: Guo Pu (郭) dalam Shanhaijing Guangzhu (山海經廣注) mencatat bahwa Erya (爾雅) menyebut tiga belas jenis tikus termasuk tikus 鼣, tetapi bentuknya belum jelas.
statement.en: Guo Pu (郭) in the Shanhaijing Guangzhu (山海經廣注) notes that the Erya (爾雅) lists thirteen kinds of rats including the 鼣 rat, but its form is not known.

claims.quote: 白耳白喙名曰狙如〈郭曰音即蛆　任臣案事物紺珠云狙如䑕耳白喙〉見則其國大兵〈任臣案圖贊曰狙如㣲蟲厥體無害見則師興兩陣交㑹物之所感焉有小大〉
claims.locator: 中次十一經, 倚帝之山 (注)

statement.id: Wu Renchen (任臣) mengutip Shiwu Ganzhu (事物紺珠) bahwa Juru bertelinga tikus dan bermoncong putih, dan Tuzan (圖贊) yang menyebut Juru makhluk kecil yang tubuhnya tidak berbahaya, tetapi kemunculannya menandai pasukan berangkat dan dua barisan bertempur.
statement.en: Wu Renchen (任臣) cites the Shiwu Ganzhu (事物紺珠): Juru has rat ears and a white snout, and the Tuzan (圖贊), which calls Juru a small creature whose body is harmless, yet whose appearance signals armies setting out and two battle lines clashing.

claims.quote: 又東三十里曰倚帝之山〈任臣案荒史循蜚紀倚帝氏都南陽倚帝山前編云南陽有倚帝之山唐吳筠下弟遂居南陽倚帝山即此竇子野云今内郷東三十里踦立山也〉其上多玉其下多金
claims.locator: 中次十一經, 倚帝之山 (注)

statement.id: Wu Renchen mengutip sumber yang menempatkan Gunung Yidi (倚帝之山) di Nanyang (南陽), dan Dou Ziye (竇子野) yang menyamakannya dengan Gunung Jili tiga puluh li di timur Neixiang (内郷).
statement.en: Wu Renchen cites sources placing Mount Yidi (倚帝之山) in Nanyang (南陽), and Dou Ziye (竇子野), who identifies it with Mount Jili thirty li east of Neixiang (内郷).

claims.quote: 郭璞《圖讚》：「狙如微蟲，厥體無害。見則師興，兩陣交會。物之所感，焉有小大。」

statement.id: Wikipedia mengutip Tuzan (圖讚) karya Guo Pu (郭璞): Juru makhluk kecil yang tidak berbahaya, tetapi kemunculannya menandai pasukan bergerak dan dua barisan bertempur.
statement.en: Wikipedia quotes Guo Pu's (郭璞) Tuzan (圖讚): Juru is a small, harmless creature, yet its appearance signals armies moving and two battle lines clashing.

claims.quote: 《事物紺珠》云：「狙如鼠耳白喙。」汪紱按：「鼣鼠如鼠而大，又似免，色紫紺，其皮可裘。」

statement.id: Wikipedia juga mengutip catatan Wang Fu (汪紱) bahwa tikus 鼣 seperti tikus tetapi lebih besar, juga mirip kelinci, berwarna ungu kebiruan, dan kulitnya dapat dibuat mantel bulu.
statement.en: Wikipedia also quotes Wang Fu's (汪紱) note that the 鼣 rat is like a rat but larger, also rabbit-like, purplish-blue in colour, and that its pelt can be made into fur clothing.

short_description.id: Changshe adalah ular legendaris yang tercatat dalam bagian utara Shan Hai Jing.
short_description.en: Changshe is a legendary serpent recorded in the northern section of the Shan Hai Jing.

long_description.id: Changshe adalah ular legendaris yang tercatat dalam bagian utara Shan Hai Jing. Rambut pada tubuhnya menyerupai bulu babi.
long_description.en: Changshe is a legendary serpent recorded in the northern section of the Shan Hai Jing. The hair on its body resembles pig bristles.

long_description.id: Suaranya dibandingkan dengan tabuhan drum dan kentongan. Teks menempatkan Changshe pada Gunung Daxian. Artikel membandingkan rupanya dengan Bashe dan Xiushe tanpa menyatakan bahwa ketiganya merupakan satu makhluk. Dalam teks klasik, Gunung Daxian tidak memiliki tumbuhan dan bagian bawahnya mengandung giok.
long_description.en: Its voice is compared to drums and wooden clappers. The text places Changshe on Mount Daxian. The article compares its form with Bashe and Xiushe without identifying all three as one creature. In the classical text, Mount Daxian has no vegetation and its lower area contains jade.

long_description.id: Guo Pu mencatat pendapat bahwa Changshe panjangnya seratus xun dan membandingkannya dengan ular beludak berbulu pada masanya. Wu Renchen mengutip Tuzan yang menyebut Changshe menelan segala binatang, dan mencatat bahwa satu anotasi menulis nama gunungnya Datong, yang ia anggap keliru.
long_description.en: Guo Pu notes the view that Changshe is a hundred xun long and compares it to the bristled vipers of his day. Wu Renchen cites the Tuzan, which says Changshe swallows every kind of beast, and notes that one annotation writes the mountain's name as Datong, which he considers an error.

claims.quote: 《山海經》中的長蛇記載為：「北二百八十里，曰大咸之山，無草木，其下多玉。是山也，四方，不可以上。有蛇名曰長蛇，其毛如彘豪，其音如鼓柝。」此蛇身上長著像豬毛般的毛髮，其叫聲則像大鼓、木梆一類敲擊樂器的聲音。

statement.id: Suaranya dibandingkan dengan tabuhan drum dan kentongan.
statement.en: Its voice is compared to drums and wooden clappers.

claims.quote: 《山海經》中的長蛇記載為：「北二百八十里，曰大咸之山，無草木，其下多玉。是山也，四方，不可以上。有蛇名曰長蛇，其毛如彘豪，其音如鼓柝。」此蛇身上長著像豬毛般的毛髮，其叫聲則像大鼓、木梆一類敲擊樂器的聲音。

statement.id: Teks menempatkan Changshe pada Gunung Daxian.
statement.en: The text places Changshe on Mount Daxian.

claims.quote: 與其形象相似的傳說中的蛇，尚有據說能吞象的巴蛇，與及被后羿殺死的修蛇。

statement.id: Artikel membandingkan rupanya dengan Bashe dan Xiushe tanpa menyatakan bahwa ketiganya merupakan satu makhluk.
statement.en: The article compares its form with Bashe and Xiushe without identifying all three as one creature.

claims.quote: 北二百八十里，曰大咸之山，無草木，其下多玉。是山也，四方，不可以上。有蛇名曰長蛇，其毛如彘豪，其音如鼓柝。

statement.id: Dalam teks klasik, Gunung Daxian tidak memiliki tumbuhan dan bagian bawahnya mengandung giok.
statement.en: In the classical text, Mount Daxian has no vegetation and its lower area contains jade.

claims.quote: 北二百八十里曰大咸之山〈任臣案事𩔖賦注引此作大同之山疑誤〉無草木其下多玉是山也四方不可以上有蛇名曰長蛇其毛如 豪

statement.id: Dalam Shanhaijing Guangzhu (山海經廣注), Wu Renchen (任臣) mencatat bahwa anotasi Shilei Fu (事𩔖賦注) menulis nama gunungnya Datong (大同之山), yang ia anggap keliru.
statement.en: In the Shanhaijing Guangzhu (山海經廣注), Wu Renchen (任臣) notes that the Shilei Fu annotation (事𩔖賦注) writes the mountain's name as Datong (大同之山), which he considers an error.

claims.quote: 郭曰説者云長百尋今蝮蛇色似艾綬文文間有毛如猪鬐此其𩔖也常山亦有長蛇與此形不同　任臣案豫章記永嘉末有大蛇長十餘丈亦此𩔖圖贊曰長蛇百尋厥鬛如 飛羣走𩔖靡不吞噬極物之惡盡毒之厲又吳淑蛇賦云毛若 豪本此也〉其音如皷柝

statement.id: Guo Pu (郭) mencatat pendapat bahwa Changshe panjangnya seratus xun, dan bahwa ular beludak masa itu yang berwarna seperti pita hijau dengan bulu seperti surai babi di sela coraknya tergolong jenis ini; Wu Renchen mengutip Yuzhang Ji (豫章記) tentang ular besar sepanjang lebih dari sepuluh zhang dan Tuzan (圖贊) yang menyebut Changshe menelan segala binatang.
statement.en: Guo Pu (郭) notes the view that Changshe is a hundred xun long, and that the vipers of his day, coloured like green ribbon with bristles like a pig's mane between their markings, are of this kind; Wu Renchen cites the Yuzhang Ji (豫章記) on a great snake over ten zhang long and the Tuzan (圖贊), which says Changshe swallows every kind of beast.

short_description.id: Yonghe adalah monster Tiongkok yang disamakan dengan kera dan terkait dengan kepanikan luas.
short_description.en: Yonghe is a Chinese monster likened to an ape and associated with widespread panic.

long_description.id: Yonghe adalah monster Tiongkok yang disamakan dengan kera dan terkait dengan kepanikan luas.
long_description.en: Yonghe is a Chinese monster likened to an ape and associated with widespread panic.

long_description.id: Ia berwarna kuning dengan mata dan paruh merah; kemunculannya ditakuti.
long_description.en: It has yellow coloration with red eyes and a red beak; its appearance is feared.

long_description.id: Teks Zhongshan Jing menempatkannya di Gunung Feng dan menyebut kemunculannya membawa ketakutan besar bagi negeri; sumber modern menyebutnya bencana kelaparan besar. Gunung yang sama dihuni dewa Gengfu yang bercahaya, dan memiliki sembilan lonceng yang berbunyi bila embun beku datang.
long_description.en: The Zhongshan Jing text places it on Mount Feng and says its appearance brings great fear to the country; a modern source speaks of a great famine. The same mountain is home to the shining god Gengfu and has nine bells that ring when frost comes.

description.id: Gunung tempat Yonghe hidup menurut Zhongshan Jing.
description.en: Mountain where Yonghe lives according to the Zhongshan Jing.

claims.quote: 雍和（ようわ Yunghe）は、中国に伝わる怪物の一種。 猿に似た姿をしているが体色は黄色く、赤い目と赤い嘴を持つという。 この怪物が現れた国は、大恐慌に見舞われるとされる。

statement.id: Yonghe adalah monster Tiongkok yang disamakan dengan kera dan terkait dengan kepanikan luas.
statement.en: Yonghe is a Chinese monster likened to an ape and associated with widespread panic.

claims.quote: 猿に似た姿をしているが体色は黄色く、赤い目と赤い嘴を持つという。 この怪物が現れた国は、大恐慌に見舞われるとされる。

statement.id: Ia berwarna kuning dengan mata dan paruh merah; kemunculannya ditakuti.
statement.en: It has yellow coloration with red eyes and a red beak; its appearance is feared.

claims.quote: 又東南三百里，曰豐山。有獸焉，其狀如猨，赤目，赤喙、黃身，名曰雍和，見則國有大恐。

statement.id: Teks Zhongshan Jing (中山經): di Gunung Feng (豐山) ada binatang seperti kera (猨) bermata merah, berparuh merah, dan bertubuh kuning bernama Yonghe (雍和); bila ia terlihat, negeri dilanda ketakutan besar (大恐).
statement.en: The Zhongshan Jing (中山經) text: on Mount Feng (豐山) there is a beast like an ape (猨) with red eyes, a red beak and a yellow body, named Yonghe (雍和); when it is seen, the country suffers great fear (大恐).

claims.quote: 見則國有大恐。神耕父處之，常遊清泠之淵，出入有光，見則其國為敗。

statement.id: Di gunung yang sama tinggal dewa Gengfu (耕父), yang sering bermain di kolam Qingling dan bercahaya saat keluar masuk; bila ia terlihat, negerinya runtuh (為敗).
statement.en: On the same mountain dwells the god Gengfu (耕父), who often roams the Qingling pool and shines as he comes and goes; when he is seen, his country falls (為敗).

claims.quote: 雍和是指一隻传说中的猿，红眼红嘴，黄毛，一出现就会有大灾荒。

statement.id: Wikipedia bahasa Tionghoa menyebut Yonghe kera legenda bermata dan bermulut merah dengan bulu kuning, yang kemunculannya diikuti bencana kelaparan besar (大灾荒).
statement.en: Chinese Wikipedia calls Yonghe a legendary ape with red eyes and mouth and yellow fur, whose appearance is followed by a great famine (大灾荒).

claims.quote: 見則其國為敗。有九鍾焉，是知霜鳴。其上多金，其下多榖柞杻橿。

statement.id: Gunung Feng juga memiliki sembilan lonceng yang berbunyi bila embun beku datang, dengan banyak emas di atasnya dan pohon gu, zuo, niu, serta jiang di bawahnya.
statement.en: Mount Feng also has nine bells that ring when frost comes, with much gold above and gu, zuo, niu and jiang trees below.

summary.id: Ketakutan besar (大恐) di negeri.
summary.en: Great fear (大恐) in the country.

summary.id: Bencana kelaparan besar (大灾荒).
summary.en: A great famine (大灾荒).

selection_criteria: computeFillStatus must be lengkap-informasi: complete, valid research without an approved image.
No active editorial artwork and no permanent artwork exclusion.
The accepted research entry is embedded unchanged; the image may only depict what its claims document.
Creatures an earlier batch left out keep that reason as catatan_sebelumnya; the generator may decline them with status tidak-digambar.

user_policy.name: sangar
user_policy.intent: Every illustration must feel 'sangar': dangerous, imposing or awe-inspiring, with the being as the undeniable subject. The owner rejected earlier images that read as an ordinary person, an ordinary animal, an empty landscape, or a calm, cute or decorative portrait. Those outcomes are failures regardless of technical quality.
user_policy.subject: The being dominates the frame and is clearly the subject. Head, eyes and distinguishing traits are readable even at thumbnail size. Never a landscape without the being, never a human who could be a passer-by, never a farm animal at pasture.
user_policy.moment: Depict a moment, not a pose: hunting, emerging, striking, commanding, towering, descending, tearing through weather or ground. Gaze and posture confront or loom over the viewer. Standing still and facing the camera with a neutral expression is not acceptable.
user_policy.effects: Visible power is wanted and may be strong, but every effect must come from a power, domain, attribute, habitat or deed documented in the research claims of that being, and it must act physically on the world: ground cracking, water rearing, trees bending, lightning striking, flame consuming, fog pouring, bodies of victims turned to stone. No generic glowing envelope, neon outline, energy ribbons, floating runes or luminous coloured mist. If the research documents no power, build menace from anatomy, scale, moment, light and setting instead, and record that in artistic_choices.
user_policy.fidelity: Anatomy, attributes, number of heads, eyes, limbs and iconography follow the research claims exactly. Effects and atmosphere add power; they never replace or invent anatomy. Fully opaque clothing where a humanlike form is clothed; no nudity, no explicit gore.
user_policy.composition: Low camera angle; monumental or predatory scale with small environmental references when size is documented, otherwise dominance through tight framing and foreshortening. Strong silhouette, high contrast, cinematic low-key lighting from one dominant source (moon, fire, lightning, dying sun), rim light, dust, smoke, rain or spray. Tactile surfaces: wet scales, matted fur, cracked skin, rust, weathered cloth, stone.
user_policy.setting: The place its stories name: graveyard, swamp, sea cliff, battlefield, celestial palace, desert storm. Weather and time of day heighten threat or majesty. Palette is dark and warm with one strong accent, consistent with the collection; no pastel, no flat even daylight.
user_policy.respect: Living religions (Hindu, Buddhist, Shinto, Abrahamic and folk deities still worshipped) are majestic and overwhelming rather than monstrous: cosmic scale, divine radiance from documented attributes, the elements they rule in motion. Malevolent beings are menacing. Literary beings follow their source text, never a film, game, anime or comic design.
user_policy.aniconic: If the research documents no bodily form at all, either depict the documented manifestation as an active, overwhelming force (the sky itself splitting, a storm swallowing the steppe) with the choice recorded in artistic_choices, or decline the entry with status tidak-digambar. A calm scene without agency fails.
user_policy.self_check: Before accepting an image the generator answers all of these with yes: the being dominates the frame; it still looks dangerous or majestic at 200 px; there is a moment, not a static pose; each visible effect points to a claim id; head, eye and limb counts match the claims; no text, watermark, border or borrowed design; it would not be rejected as ordinary person, ordinary animal, landscape only, or cute and calm. One no means regenerate, keep the rejected attempt as history, up to three attempts.
user_policy.style: Square premium painterly cinematic illustration in the house style of the existing artwork, more dramatic and higher contrast. No text, labels, logo, border or watermark.
user_policy.sources: Never copy designs from films, games, anime or comics (modern_depictions). Every design is original and sourced from the accepted research.
